BURHAN:v1p196/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p196/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p196/r1.claim: The Makkan Sūrat al-Najm verse is reported about Nabhan and a woman he tried to seduce; major sins are those ending in Hell, indecencies those carrying a fixed penalty, and lapses lie between them. The report is supported by the absence of legal penalties and campaigns in Mecca.
BURHAN:v1p196/r1.anchor: من ذلك قوله تعالى فى النجم ﴿ الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم ﴾ يعنى كل ذنب عاقبته النار ﴿ والفواحش ﴾

ITQAN:v1p53/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p53/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p53/r4.claim: The passage “those who avoid” through “most God-fearing” is listed as an exception to al-Najm's Meccan classification.
ITQAN:v1p53/r4.anchor: النجم استثني منها ﴿ الذين يجتنبون ﴾ إلى ﴿ اتقى ﴾

DAMGHANI:v1p110/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p110/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p110/r10.claim: Janīn means a child in its mother’s womb.
DAMGHANI:v1p110/r10.anchor: السادس الجنين الولد في بطن أمه قوله تعالى في سورة النجم وإذا أنتم أجنة في بطون أمهاتكم

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r5.claim: Only God controls the heavens and earth; those who avoid grave sins and indecencies, though they may commit minor sins without persisting, will receive His ample mercy.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r5.anchor: only those shall be rewarded in the Hereafter who used to abstain from heinous sins and open indecencies

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r3.claim: Those claiming Paradise through intercessors, lineage, or service to the sanctuary will be cast into Hell; those who avoid usurping rights and public indecency may be forgiven for sins if they repent, for God's mercy is vast.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r3.anchor: because of their intercessors or because of their lineage and race or because of some apparent service to the House of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r4.claim: People who boast of holiness should remember their earthly origin in mud, sludge, and impure fluid rather than claim to be sacred.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r4.anchor: a creature made from mud, sludge and an impure fluid should not claim to be so holy and sacred.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p60/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p60/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p60/r4.claim: An occasional sin by those who avoid grave sins and open indecency is a brief stumble: like people inclined to cleanliness, they do not dwell in it but repent and reform promptly.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p60/r4.anchor: these people too do not live in sin; they try to cleanse themselves as soon as a sin is committed by repenting and reforming themselves.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p60/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p60/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p60/r5.claim: Al-lamam and lamam mean to stay briefly at a place.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p60/r5.anchor: mean to stay at a place for a short period.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r1.speaker: Mujāhid and Ibn ‘Abbās (rta)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r1.claim: Islahi reports their view that a person may slip into sin but soon emerges from it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r1.anchor: ascribed to Mujāhid and Ibn ‘Abbās (rta)26 is that a person stumbles into a sin but then soon comes out of this state.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r2.claim: A sinless life is not required; faith should keep sin from taking over, so a person reforms as soon as he recognizes a lapse, and God forgives such people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r2.anchor: it is not required of a person to lead a sinless life. A person may at times while succumbing to emotions and desires commit a sin; however,

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r3.claim: He cites 4:17–18 to distinguish forgiveness for prompt repentance from the unaccepted repentance of lifelong sinners and those who die disbelieving.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r3.anchor: It is they who are forgiven by God. God is all-knowing and wise.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r4.claim: He defines ithm as sins involving usurpation of rights, oppression, and injustice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r4.anchor: sins which relate to usurpation of rights, oppression and injustice

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r5.claim: He defines fawāḥish as open indecencies and sexual transgressions.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r6.claim: Avoiding major sins does not exempt minor sins; strong faith prevents persistence in them, like a trusted person would not tolerate dishonesty over a small sum.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r6.anchor: so strong is the sense of faith of people who safeguard themselves from major sins that they never remain adamant on minor ones.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r7.claim: The warning addresses people mired in sin who expect Paradise through alleged deities, noble ancestors, or racial superiority; faith and righteous deeds alone avail them before God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r7.anchor: what is going to be of avail to them before God is faith and righteous deeds and not this false support.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r8.claim: Islahi says Quraysh and the People of the Book held false notions, while Quraysh also took pride in lineage and custodianship of the House of God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p61/r8.anchor: both the Quraysh and the People of the Book were inflicted with some sort of false notion or the other.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r1.claim: Quraysh pride in Abrahamic descent and Kaaba custodianship is answered with 9:19: pilgrim services cannot replace faith and righteous deeds or conceal crimes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r1.anchor: yet this cannot take the place of embracing faith and doing righteous deeds nor one which can conceal their crimes.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r2.claim: The People of the Book imagined their descent from Abraham and Isaac exempted them from Hell, or limited any punishment to a few days.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r2.anchor: since they were the chosen people and were the descendents of Abraham (sws) and Isaac (sws), the fire of Hell would not touch them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r3.claim: Jesus warned them against boasting of Abrahamic descent, saying God could raise Abraham’s progeny from stones (Matthew 3:9).
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r3.anchor: not show conceit on being the progeny of Abraham (sws) and that if his Lord wanted, he could create Abraham’s progeny from stones.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r4.claim: Muslims followed this Jewish conceit, treating themselves as automatically forgiven; some families and graveyards were regarded as guaranteeing Paradise regardless of belief or deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r4.anchor: Muslims too regarded themselves to be forgiven people and had thereby absolved themselves of all the responsibilities related to faith and deeds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r5.claim: The verse warns such people not to declare themselves holy: God knows their earthly and embryonic origins, and rank comes through faith and virtue, not bodily form.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p62/r5.anchor: all people who have this mentality are addressed and warned that they should not regard themselves to be holy and indulge in self-praise.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r1.claim: God alone knows and measures each person’s worth, so no one may proclaim high status before His judgment; Islahi points ahead to 70:38–39.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r1.anchor: It is He who will measure things by His scale and grant each person the status he deserves.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r2.claim: Islahi uses the verse’s degrading description of human origins to challenge waḥdat al-wujūd: if humans are part of God, why describe them so disparagingly?
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r2.anchor: If man is really a part of God, then did the Almighty refer to one His parts, God forbid, in such a degrading way in this verse?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r3.speaker: Sufis
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r3.claim: Islahi rejects the Sufi self-praise “I am pure and flawless; what majesty I have,” as arrogant and incompatible with the verse’s rebuke of self-exaltation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r3.anchor: these Sufis chant: ﺳﺒﺤﺎI am pure and flawless! What majesty I have! Exalted is my majesty).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r4.claim: Islahi says Sufis imported this creed from the Bāṭiniyya, extremist Shiites, and Brahmans rather than Qur’an and Hadith, and many repeat it without understanding.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r4.anchor: since the Sufis instead of receiving guidance from the Qur’ ān and Ḥadīth have received it from the bātaniyyah, extremist Shiites and the Brahmans

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p253#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p253#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p253#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says nothing resembles minor lapses more than Abū Hurayra’s report from the Prophet about each person’s allotted share of fornication.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p253#3/r2.anchor: سمعت ابن عباس قال ما رأيت شيئا أشبه باللمم مما قال أو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p253#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p253#3/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p253#3/r3.claim: The Prophet says each person has an inevitable share of fornication: the eyes’ share is looking, the tongue’s is speech, desire wishes, and the private part either confirms or denies it.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p253#3/r3.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله كتب على ابن آدم حظه من الزنا أدرك لا محالة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p253#3/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p253#3/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p253#3/r4.claim: A parallel transmission through Hammām from Abū Hurayra repeats the same Prophetic report about allotted fornication.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p253#3/r4.anchor: عن معمر عن همام عن أبي هريرة مثل حديث ابن طاوس عن أبيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r1.claim: Al-ilmām means approaching without fully mixing; Arabic also uses it for nearing or almost doing something.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r1.anchor: ألم بكذا، إذا قاربه ولم يخالطه. وقال الأزهري: العرب تستعمل الإلمام في المقاربة والدنو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r2.speaker: جرير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r2.claim: Jarīr's line uses limām for a visit that comes only occasionally or briefly, illustrating approach.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r2.anchor: بنفسي من تجنيه عزيز ... علي ومن زيارته لمام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r3.speaker: شاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r3.claim: An anonymous poet likewise describes the meeting of close friends as brief or occasional.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r4.claim: Al-ajnna is the plural of janīn, a child in the womb; the word reflects concealment, and al-ijtinan means concealment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r4.anchor: الأجنة: جمع جنين، وهو الولد في البطن، سمي بذلك لاستتاره، والاجتنان: الاستتار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r1.claim: The discussion of major sins was given earlier in al-Nisa; sins divide into major and minor, and الفواحش is coordinated with major sins to single out especially heinous major sins and stress their gravity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r1.anchor: وتقدم الكلام في الكبائر في قوله تعالى: إن تجتنبوا كبائر ما تنهون عنه في سورة النساء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r2.claim: He defines major sins as those whose punishment is not removed except through repentance; the author calls this an Mu'tazilite position.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: والكبائر: الذنوب التي لا يسقط عقابها إلا بالتوبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r3.claim: The exception إلا اللمم may be disconnected because minor sins were not included in what preceded, or an adjective meaning other than minor sins; he also allows a connected exception depending on the definition of lamam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r3.anchor: إلا اللمم: استثناء منقطع، لأنه لم يدخل تحت ما قبله، وهو صغار الذنوب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r4.speaker: الخدري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r4.claim: He defines lamam as a glance, wink, or kiss.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r5.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r5.claim: He defines lamam as a fleeting thought of sin.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة وابن عباس والشعبي والكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r6.claim: They define lamam as any sin for which God has specified neither a legal limit nor a punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r6.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة وابن عباس والشعبي والكلبي: كل ذنب لم يذكر الله تعالى عليه حدا ولا عذابا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r7.claim: They say lamam refers to the shirk and sins committed before Islam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وابن زيد: ما ألموا به من الشرك والمعاصي في الجاهلية قبل الإسلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن ثابت وزيد بن أسلم وابنه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r8.claim: They report that the verse was occasioned by unbelievers telling Muslims they had practiced the same things the day before; the author compares it with the exception for what occurred before Islam in the marriage prohibition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r8.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وزيد بن ثابت وزيد بن أسلم وابنه: أن سبب الآية قول الكفار للمسلمين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r9.claim: Another report says the verse was revealed about Nabhan al-Tammar, whose story is well known.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r9.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في نبهان التمار، وحديثه مشهور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r10.claim: He also defines lamam as a minor slip without persistence, followed by repentance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره: العلقة والسقطة دون دوام، ثم يتوب منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r11.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r11.claim: He defines lamam as adultery, theft, and wine drinking, provided one does not return to them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r11.anchor: وقال الحسن: والزنا والسرقة والخمر، ثم لا يعود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r12.speaker: ابن المسيب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r12.claim: He says lamam is what occurs to the heart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r12.anchor: وقال ابن المسيب: ما خطر على القلب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r13.speaker: نفطويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r13.claim: He defines lamam as something not habitual.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r14.speaker: الرماني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r14.claim: He takes it as intending sin or internal self-talk without carrying the act out.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r14.anchor: وقال الرماني: الهم بالذنب، وحديث النفس دون أن يواقع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r15.claim: Another view identifies lamam as an accidental glance.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r16.claim: God’s forgiveness is broad because avoiding major sins expiates minor ones.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r16.anchor: إن ربك واسع المغفرة، حيث يكفر الصغائر باجتناب الكبائر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r17.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r17.claim: He says major sins are forgiven through repentance; the author again calls this an Mu'tazilite tendency.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r18.claim: One occasion report says the verse addressed Jews who praised themselves and called a deceased child a righteous intimate of God; another says it addressed believers boasting of their works; the author takes it as general.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r18.anchor: قيل نزلت في قوم من اليهود عظموا أنفسهم، وإذا مات طفل لهم قالوا: هذا صديق عند الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r19.speaker: مكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r19.claim: He takes أعلم to mean simply knowing; the author sees no need to abandon its ordinary comparative sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r19.anchor: وقال مكي: بمعنى عالم بكم، ولا ضرورة إلى إخراجها عن أصل موضوعها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r20.claim: Being created from the earth refers primarily to Adam, though it may refer to human beings formed from food whose origins are earthly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r20.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بأنشأكم: أنشأ أصلكم، وهو آدم. ويجوز أن يراد من فضلة الأغذية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r21.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r21.claim: Do not praise yourselves for righteous deeds or freedom from sin; humble yourselves, since God knew the pious before their emergence from Adam and from their mothers’ wombs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p20/r21.anchor: فلا تزكوا أنفسكم: أي لا تنسبوها إلى زكاء الأعمال والطهارة عن المعاصي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r1.claim: The author criticizes people who advertise missed night worship, display a dark mark as proof of frequent prostration, theatrically gesture while forming the ihram intention, and swear by a house they visited, although they eagerly seize money; they want praise for displayed virtues.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r1.anchor: وكثيرا ما ترى من المتصلحين، إذا حدثوا، كان وردنا البارحة كذا، وفاتنا من وردنا البارحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r2.claim: Another interpretation forbids mutual self-praise for reputation or worldly praise, or categorical commendation; testimony to establish rights is allowed when necessary.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r2.anchor: وقيل: المعنى لا يزكي بعضكم بعضا تزكية السمعة أو المدح للدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r3.claim: A fetus is called janin while in the womb; after birth it is called a child or a miscarriage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r3.anchor: والجنين: ما كان في البطن، فإذا خرج سمي ولدا أو سقطا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r4.claim: Mentioning mothers’ wombs highlights God’s complete knowledge and power: the womb is profoundly dark, so the One who knows the hidden embryo also knows its visible state.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r4.anchor: تنبيه على كمال العلم والقدرة، فإن بطن الأم في غاية الظلمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r5.claim: One interpretation of those who are pious takes taqwa as avoiding shirk.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r6.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r6.claim: Ali defines piety as doing a good deed and turning away from a sin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p21/r6.anchor: وقال علي: عمل حسنة وارعوى عن معصية

MAJAZ:v2p236/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p236/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p236/r7.claim: Al-lamam is neither indecency nor a major sin; the exception is elliptical and means “unless someone slips into something outside those categories.”
MAJAZ:v2p236/r7.anchor: ليس هو من الفواحش ولا من كبائر الإثم وقد يستثنى الشيء من الشيء وليس منه

MAJAZ:v2p236/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p236/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p236/r8.claim: The poet's example of a land with no people except gazelles and camels shows that an exception may name something outside the class in the main statement.
MAJAZ:v2p236/r8.anchor: وبلدة ليس بها أنيس ... إلا اليعافير وإلا العيس

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r5.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r5.claim: Some consider verse 32 to be from the Madinan period.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r5.anchor: V. 32 is also considered by some to be from the Madinan period

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.claim: The third section calls people to reflect on their creation and transitions to enduring truths in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.anchor: the third section (vv. 31–54) calls upon people to reflect upon their creation

THALABI:v8p322/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p322/r1.speaker: يحيى بن رئاب وحمزة والكسائي وخلف
THALABI:v8p322/r1.claim: Yahya ibn Riʾab, Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf read the word in both surahs as singular “kabīr” (“major sin”); the other readers use plural “kabāʾir.”
THALABI:v8p322/r1.anchor: قرأ يحيى بن رئاب وحمزة والكسائي وخلف هاهنا وفي سورة النجم (كبير) على التوحيد

SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r1.claim: الذين يجتنبون may be an accusative بدل, explanatory apposition, or adjective of الذين أحسنوا, with an implied أعني.
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون منصوبا بدلا أو بيانا أو نعتا للذين أحسنوا، وبإضمار أعني،

SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r2.claim: Alternatively, it is the predicate of an omitted subject: هم الذين.
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r2.anchor: وأن يكون خبر مبتدأ مضمر أي: هم الذين،

SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r3.speaker: جماعة
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r3.claim: The well-known analysis treats the exception as disconnected because lammam means minor sins and is not included among major sins and immoralities.
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r3.anchor: أنه استثناء منقطع لأن اللمم الصغائر، فلم تندرج فيما قبلها، قاله جماعة وهو المشهور.

SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r4.claim: Alternatively, إلا means غير and qualifies the preceding phrase, as in 21:22.
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r4.anchor: أنه صفة و " إلا " بمنزلة " غير " كقوله: لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله [الأنبياء: 22]

SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r5.claim: A connected exception works for those who interpret lammam as something other than minor sins.
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r5.anchor: أنه متصل وهذا عند من يفسر اللمم بغير الصغائر، والخلاف مذكور في التفسير.

SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r6.claim: The root sense is something small or slight; related uses include a slight touch of madness, short stay, and little eating.
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r6.anchor: وأصل اللمم: ما قل وصغر، ومنه اللمم وهو المس من الجنون، وألم بالمكان قل لبثه به، ألم بالطعام أي: قل أكله منه.

SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r7.speaker: أبو العباس
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r7.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās explains the root as approaching something without fully doing or entering it.
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r7.anchor: وقال أبو العباس: " أصل اللمم: أن يلم بالشيء من غير أن يركبه

SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r8.speaker: الأزهري
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r8.claim: Al-Azharī says Arabs use الإلمام to mean nearness or approach.
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r8.anchor: وقال الأزهري: " العرب تستعمل الإلمام في معنى الدنو والقرب "

SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r9.speaker: جرير
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r9.claim: Jarīr’s line uses لمام for a brief or infrequent visit.
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r9.anchor: بنفسي من تجنبه عزيز علي ومن زيارته لمام

SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r10.claim: An anonymous verse uses تلمم for coming to visit, illustrating approach.
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r10.anchor: متى تأتنا تلمم بنا في ديارنا تجد حطبا جزلا ونارا تأججا

SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r11.claim: A second anonymous line calls the meeting of close friends لمام.

SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r12.claim: The word لمة for a lock of hair denotes less than a full الوفرة.
SAMIN-DURR:53:32/r12.anchor: ومنه لمة الشعر لما دون الوفرة.

SAMIN-DURR:53:32#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:32#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:32#2/r1.claim: أجنة is plural of جنين, a fetus in the womb; the name reflects concealment. Its pattern is like سرير/أسرة.
SAMIN-DURR:53:32#2/r1.anchor: أجنة } جمع جنين، وهو الحمل في البطن لاستتاره. وجنين وأجنة كسرير وأسرة.

ASAD-NOTES:53:31/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:31/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:31/r2.claim: Those avoiding grave sins and shameful deeds may stumble, and God's forgiveness is abundant.
ASAD-NOTES:53:31/r2.anchor: As for those who avoid the [tru ly] grave sins and shameful deeds

ASAD-NOTES:53:31/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:31/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:31/r3.claim: God knows people from their origin in dust through their time as embryos; they should not claim purity, since He knows the God-conscious.
ASAD-NOTES:53:31/r3.anchor: He is fully aware of you [25] when He brings you into being out of dust

ASAD-NOTES:53:31#n24/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:31#n24/r1.speaker: Baghawi, Razi, Ibn Kathir
ASAD-NOTES:53:31#n24/r1.claim: They take lamam as an occasional, unintended stumble into sin followed by sincere repentance.
ASAD-NOTES:53:31#n24/r1.anchor: followed by sincere repentance (Baghawi, Razi, Ibn Kathir)

ASAD-NOTES:53:31#n25/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:31#n25/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:31#n25/r1.claim: The reference implies humanity's inborn weakness, echoed in 4:28, which makes people liable to stumble into sin.
ASAD-NOTES:53:31#n25/r1.anchor: an implied echo of the statement that

ASAD-NOTES:53:31#n26/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:31#n26/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:31#n26/r1.claim: For the phrase 'out of the earth,' Asad points to his notes on 3:59 and 23:12.
ASAD-NOTES:53:31#n26/r1.anchor: see second half of note 47 on 3:59, as well as note 4 on 23:12

ASAD-NOTES:53:31#n27/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:31#n27/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:31#n27/r1.claim: People should remain humble rather than boast of purity, remembering that God purifies whom He wills, as in 4:49.
ASAD-NOTES:53:31#n27/r1.anchor: but remain humble and remember that

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r1.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read كبير الإثم in the singular; the other readers have كبائر الإثم.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r1.anchor: حمزة والكسائي: يجتنبون كبير الإثم [النجم/ 32]. الباقون: كبائر الإثم

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r2.claim: Al-Fārisī argues that فعيل can carry a collective or abundant sense like فعول, citing عدو for a group in 4:92 and 6:112.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r2.anchor: فعيلا قد جاء يعنى به الكثير، كما أن فعولا قد جاء كذلك في قوله: فإن كان من قوم عدو لكم

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r3.claim: Other Quranic examples support singular فعيل with plural reference: صديق among intercessors, رفيقا for the righteous, and قعيد for the two recording angels.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r3.anchor: قال: فما لنا من شافعين ولا صديق حميم [الشعراء/ 100، 101] وقال: وحسن أولئك رفيقا

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r4.claim: Al-Fārisī cites poetic usage of singular-form adjectives: an unattributed line has قليل and عزيز with collective reference, another uses فريق, and Ruʾba’s line contains صديق.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r4.anchor: وما ضرنا أنا قليل وجارنا عزيز وجار الأكثرين ذليل وقال رؤبة: دعها فما النحوي من صديقها

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r5.claim: He also cites the line فقال فريق القوم as a poetic example of a singular-form noun for a group; the source does not name its poet.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r5.anchor: فقال فريق القوم لما نشدتهم نعم وفريق ليمن الله ما ندري

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r6.claim: He notes that فعيل is not feminized in examples such as ريح خريق, ملحفة جديدة, ناقة سديس, and كتيبة خصيف, just as فعول stays uninflected in خذول تراعي ربربا.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r6.anchor: ومن ثم لم يؤنث في قولهم: ريح خريق، وملحفة جديدة، وناقة سديس، وكتيبة خصيف

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r7.claim: The singular source noun الإثم is collective here, not one particular sin; thus كبير can denote kinds of major sins, with singular conveying the plural sense.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r7.anchor: وهو أن المصدر المضاف، فعيل إليه واحد في معنى الكثرة. ألا ترى أنه ليس يراد به إثم بعينه؟

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r8.claim: Al-Fārisī says كبر and عظم both imply increase in a thing’s parts; this supports the singular إثم كبير reading at 2:219 and parallels إثم عظيم at 4:48.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r8.anchor: وقد وصف الإثم في الآية بالكبر، كما وصف بالعظم في قوله: افترى إثما عظيما [النساء/ 48] وهذا مما يقوي قراءة

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r9.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r9.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r9.claim: Asked why the adjective was not pluralized, al-Fārisī answers that the singular follows Quranic precedent such as عدو لكم for a group.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p234#2/r9.anchor: فإن قيل: فهلا جمعا ذلك ليكون أبين كما جمع ذلك سائرهم؟ قيل: إذا أتيا به على قياس ما جاء في التنزيل

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p336#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p336#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p336#2/r1.claim: The phrase is read with either singular كبير الإثم or plural كبائر الإثم; the source refers to the discussion in al-Shūrā (42:37) for the variants' rationale.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p336#2/r1.anchor: يقرأ بالتوحيد والجمع وقد ذكرت وجوهه

QIRAAT-ER:53:32:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:53:32:3#1/r1.speaker: Lvw
QIRAAT-ER:53:32:3#1/r1.claim: The Lvw singular kabīr replaces plural kabāʾir, shifting from major sins as a class to 'the great sin,' potentially one supreme sin.
QIRAAT-ER:53:32:3#1/r1.anchor: potentially identifying ONE supreme sin rather than a class of sins

QIRAAT-ER:53:32:26#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:53:32:26#1/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:53:32:26#1/r1.claim: This vw form of ummahāt replaces hamza with kasra on initial alif and has shadda on mīm with kasra, a dialectal form for mothers.
QIRAAT-ER:53:32:26#1/r1.anchor: Vowel shift on ummahāt: hamza replaced by kasra on initial alif

QIRAAT-ER:53:32:26#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:53:32:26#2/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:53:32:26#2/r1.claim: This vw variant has kasra on initial alif and fatḥa on doubled mīm, another dialectal pronunciation of ummahāt.
QIRAAT-ER:53:32:26#2/r1.anchor: Vowel variant: kasra on initial alif with fatḥa on doubled mīm — another dialectal pronunciation of ummahāt

QIRAAT-ER:53:32:27#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:53:32:27#1/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:53:32:27#1/r1.claim: This vw variant has kasra on alif and mīm; it is a dialectal pronunciation affecting the initial syllable, with no semantic shift.
QIRAAT-ER:53:32:27#1/r1.anchor: Vowel variant on ummahāt: kasra on alif + kasra on mīm — dialectal pronunciation affecting the initial syllable only, no semantic shift

QIRAAT-ER:53:32:27#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:53:32:27#2/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:53:32:27#2/r1.claim: This vw dialectal form has kasra on alif and fatḥa on mīm; the meaning 'mothers' is unchanged.
QIRAAT-ER:53:32:27#2/r1.anchor: Vowel variant: kasra on alif + fatḥa on mīm — another dialectal form; the semantic content (mothers) is unchanged

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p255#6/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p255#6/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p255#6/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd calls the minor lapses eye adultery by looking, lip adultery by kissing, hand adultery by touching, and foot adultery by walking; the genitals confirm or deny it.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p255#6/r1.anchor: عن سليمان الأعمش عن أبي الضحى أن ابن مسعود قال قوله ﴿ إلا اللمم ﴾ قال زنا العينين النظر وزنا الشفتين التقبيل

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p255#6/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p255#6/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p255#6/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says a person may commit a brief lapse in a grave indecency and then repent.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p255#6/r2.anchor: قال معمر وكان الحسن يقول تكون اللمة من الرجل بالفاحشة ثم يتوب

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r1.claim: الذين يجتنبون may substitute for the preceding relative, explain or qualify it, stand as a noun in praise, or be the predicate of an omitted subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r1.anchor: بدل من الموصول الثاني وصيغة الأستقبال في صلته للدلالة على تجدد الأجتناب

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r2.claim: The present tense indicates repeated, continuing avoidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r2.anchor: وصيغة الأستقبال في صلته للدلالة على تجدد الأجتناب واستمراره

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r3.claim: الإثم is an act that impedes reward; its major forms are sins whose punishment is great.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r3.anchor: وكبائره ما يكبر عقابه وقرأحمزة والكسائي وخلف

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r4.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، خلف
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r4.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf read كبير الإثم in the singular, meaning the genus or shirk.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r4.anchor: حمزة والكسائي وخلف كبير الأثم على إرادة الجنس أوالشرك

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r5.claim: Fawahish are especially ugly major sins, making the coordination a specific after a general; another view treats fawahish and kabair as synonyms.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r5.anchor: ما عظم قبحه من الكبائر فعطفه على ما تقدم من عطف الخاص على العام

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r6.claim: Lammam means minor sins; its root denotes a small amount, as in hair shorter than a full head of hair.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r6.anchor: ما صغر من الذنوب وأصله ما قل قدره ومنه لمه الشعر لأنها دون الوفرة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r7.claim: Abu Said al-Khudri illustrates lammam with a glance, gesture, or kiss.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r7.anchor: وفسره أبو سعيد الخدري بالنظرة والغمزة والقبلة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r8.speaker: الرماني
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r8.claim: Al-Rummani takes lammam as approaching a sin without committing it, including intending it or speaking to oneself about it.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r8.anchor: وعليه قول الرماني هو الهم بالذنب وحديث النفس دون أن يواقع

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r9.speaker: ابن المسيب
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r9.claim: Ibn al-Musayyab explains lammam as what crosses one's heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r9.anchor: وقول ابن المسيب : ما خطر على القلب

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r10.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd say it means sins and idolatry committed before Islam; the verse answered pagans who reproached Muslims for their former conduct, like 4:22.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r10.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وابن زيد هو ما ألموا به منالشرك والمعاصي في الجاهلية قبل الإسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r11.speaker: غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r11.claim: Another interpretation takes lammam as any sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r11.anchor: وقيل : هو مطلق الذنب + وفيرواية عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r12.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas defines it as sins a person occasionally falls into and then repents; most commentators explain it as minor sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه ما يلم به المرء في الحين من الذنوب ثم يتوب

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r13.claim: Most take the exception as disconnected; another view says there is no exception, treating إلا as “other than” and an adjective qualifying the generic major sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r13.anchor: والأستثناء منقطع وقيل : إنه لا استثناء فيه أصلا و ( إلا ) صفة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r14.claim: The adjective reading is defended because كبائر الإثم can count as indefinite, or because إلا and غير can become definite through annexation, as in غير المغضوب.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r14.anchor: يتعرفان بالإضافة كما في ( غير المغضوب )

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r15.speaker: ابن الحاجب
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r15.claim: Some object that إلا as an adjective must follow an unbounded indefinite plural, a condition absent here; this requirement is Ibn al-Hajib's view.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r15.anchor: شرط جواز وقوع ( إلا ) صفة كونها تابعة لجمع منكر غيرمحصور

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r16.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r16.claim: Sibawayh and most later grammarians allow إلا as an adjective wherever an exception is allowed, but al-Alusi says that parse is still unlikely here and unnecessary.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r16.anchor: وسيبويه يرى جواز وقوعها صفة جواز الاستثناء فهو لا يشترط ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r17.claim: Most commentators cite this verse to establish major and minor sins; several leading scholars deny the division and say every sin is major.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r17.anchor: والآية عند الأكثرين دليل على أن المعاصي منها كبائر ومنها صغائر وأنكر جماعة من الأئمة هذا الانقسام

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r18.speaker: الأستاذ أبو إسحاق الأسفرايني، القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني، إمام الحرمين، تقي الدين السبكي، ابن القريشي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r18.claim: Al-Isfarayini, al-Baqillani, al-Juwayni, al-Subki, and Ibn al-Qurashi are named among those who say all sins are major.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r18.anchor: منهم الأستاذ ألو إسحاق الأسفرايني والقاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r19.speaker: ابن فورك
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r19.claim: Ibn Furak transmits this view from the Asharites and chooses it in his tafsir; calling some sins small or large is relative.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r19.anchor: بل حكاه ابن فروك عنالأشاعرة واختاره في تفسيره فقالمعاصي الله تعالى كلها

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r20.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r20.claim: Ibn Furak attributes the division into major and minor sins to the Mu'tazilites but says their position is unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r20.anchor: عند المعتزلة وقال : إنه ليس بصحيح

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r21.speaker: القاضي عبد الوهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r21.claim: Qadi Abd al-Wahhab says a sin is called minor only relative to avoiding major sins; a disconnected report from Ibn Masud calls every divine prohibition major.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r21.anchor: وقال القاضي عبد الوهاب : لا يمكن أن يقال في معصية إنها صغيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r22.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r22.claim: In disconnected reports, Ibn Masud says every divine prohibition, or every disobedient act, is a major sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r22.anchor: كل ما نهى الله تعالى عنه فهو كبيرة وفي رواية كل شيء عصى الله تعالى فيه فهو كبيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r23.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r23.claim: The majority says the dispute is largely terminological: all agree some sins impair moral probity and others do not; opponents avoid “minor” out of reverence for God.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r23.anchor: والجمهور على الانقسام قيل : ولا خلاف في المعنى وإنما الخلاف

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r24.speaker: الغزالي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r24.claim: Al-Ghazali says denying a distinction between major and minor sins is inappropriate.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r24.anchor: قال الغزالي : لا يليق إنكارالفرق بين الكبائر والصغائر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r25.speaker: فقهاء
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r25.claim: Many jurists define a major sin as one for which a specific severe threat appears in Quran or Sunna.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r25.anchor: هي ما لحق صاحبها عليها بخصوصها وعيد شديد بنص كتاب أو سنة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r26.speaker: البغوي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r26.claim: Al-Baghawi and others define a major sin as an offense requiring a hadd; al-Alusi prefers the threat-based definition because it includes slander, tale-bearing, and filial disobedience, though al-Rafii leans toward the hadd definition.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p61/r26.anchor: وقيل : كل معصية أوجبت الحد وبه قال البغوي وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r1.speaker: غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r1.claim: One definition counts what the Quran explicitly prohibits, acts whose kind incurs a hadd, abandoning an immediate duty, false testimony or narration, and perjury.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r1.anchor: حدوترك فريضة تجب فورا والكذب في الشهادة والرواية واليمين

ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r2.speaker: الهروي، شريح
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r2.claim: Al-Harawi and Shurayh add any statement contrary to general consensus to the definition of major sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r2.anchor: زاد الهروي وشريح وكل قول خالف لأجماع العام

ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r3.speaker: شيخ الإسلام البارزي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r3.claim: Al-Barizi's definition also covers wrongful killing of someone believed inviolable, or sex with a woman believed to be another man's but actually one's wife or slave.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r3.anchor: كما لو قتل من يعتقده معصومافظهر أنه مستحقي لدمه أو طيء امرأة ظاناأنه زان بها فإذا هي زوجته أو أمته

ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r4.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r4.claim: Al-Wahidi compares the concealment of major sins to the hidden greatest name, middle prayer, Night of Decree, and hour of response.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r4.anchor: ونظير ذلك إخفاء الأسم الأعظم والصلاة الوسطى وليلة القدر وساعة الإجابة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r5.claim: Al-Alusi says al-Barizi's definition is the soundest account.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r5.anchor: وإليه ذهب شيخ الإسلام البارزي وقال : هو التحقيق

ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r6.speaker: إمام الحرمين
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r6.claim: Imam al-Haramayn defines a major sin as a crime showing little regard for religion; al-Adhra'i says the apparent scope includes vile minor sins, while the Imam meant sins invalidating probity.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r6.anchor: وقيل : كل جريمة تؤذنبقلة اكتراث مرتكبها بالدينورقة الديانة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r7.speaker: الماوردي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r7.claim: Al-Mawardi defines a major sin as anything requiring a hadd or exposed to a threat.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r7.anchor: وقيل : هي ما أوجب الحد أو توجه إليه الوعيد ذكره الماوردي في فتاويه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r8.speaker: القاضي حسين، الحليمي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r8.claim: A view from Qadi Husayn via al-Halimi says an intrinsically forbidden act becomes major when combined with another aggravating aspect, such as adultery with a neighbor's wife.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r8.anchor: وقيل : كل محرم لعينه منهي عنه لمعنى في نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r9.speaker: القاضي حسين، الحليمي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r9.claim: On that view, a kiss, touching, or fondling is minor by itself but major when directed at a neighbor's wife.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r9.anchor: فالقبلة واللمس والمفاخذة صغيرة ومع حليلة الجار كبيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r10.speaker: غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r10.claim: Another definition counts acts explicitly prohibited in the Quran, listing carrion, pork, orphan property, and fleeing battle; critics reject this restricted count.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r10.anchor: أكل الميتة ولحم الخنزير ومال اليتيم والفرار من الزحف

ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r11.speaker: شيخ الإسلام البارزي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r11.claim: Al-Barizi's preferred definition includes sins paired with a hadd, threat, curse, comparable harm, or evidence of religious contempt.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r11.anchor: وقيل : إنها كل ذنب قرن به حد أو وعيد أو لعن بنص كتاب أو سنة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r12.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r12.claim: Al-Wahidi says major sins have no humanly knowable boundary, lest people treat unlisted acts as permissible; God conceals them so people strive to avoid all forbidden acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r12.anchor: أخفى ذلك عنهم ليجتهدوا في اجتناب المنهي عنه رجاء أن تجتنب الكبائر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r13.speaker: ابن حجر الهيتمي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r13.claim: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami says proposed definitions only approximate major sins and cannot be exhaustive limits.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r13.anchor: كل ما ذكر من الحدود إنما قصد به التقريب وإلا فهي ليست بحدود جامعة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r14.claim: A group counts rather than defines major sins; Ibn Abbas counts those named from the opening of Surat al-Nisa through 4:31.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p62/r14.anchor: وذهب جمع إلى تعريفها بالعد فعن ابن عباس أنها ما ذكره الله تعالى في أول سورة النساء

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r1.speaker: علي، عطاء، عبيد بن عمير
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r1.claim: Ali, Ata, and Ubayd ibn Umayr say there are seven major sins, citing the Ṣaḥīḥayn report of seven destructive sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r1.anchor: وقيل : هي سبع وروي ذلك عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وعطاء

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r2.claim: The seven destructive sins listed are associating partners with God, magic, unlawful killing, consuming orphan property or usury, fleeing battle, and falsely accusing chaste believing women.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r2.anchor: الإشراك بالله تعالى والسحر وقتل النفس التي حرم الله تعالى إلا بالحق

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r3.speaker: غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r3.claim: Other counts proposed are fifteen, fourteen, four, three according to Ibn Masud, and ten in another report.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r3.anchor: وقيل : خمس عشرة وقيل : أربع عشرة وقيل : أربع وعن ابن مسعود ثلاث

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r4.speaker: شيخ الإسلام العلائي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r4.claim: Al-Alai says hadiths explicitly identify twenty-five major sins; Ibn Hajar criticizes him for omitting more.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r4.anchor: وقال شيخ الإسلام العلائي : المنصوص عليه في الأحاديث أنه كبيرة خمس وعشرون

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r5.speaker: أبو طالب المكي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r5.claim: Abu Talib al-Makki counts seventeen: four of the heart, four of the tongue, three of the belly, two sexual, two of the hands, fleeing battle, and filial disobedience; al-Alusi says this scheme has flaws.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r5.anchor: وقال أبو طالب المكي : هي سبع عشرة أربع في القلب الشرك والإصرار على المعصية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r6.speaker: أبو طالب المكي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r6.claim: Al-Makki's remaining categories are fornication and sodomy, murder and theft, fleeing battle, and parental disobedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r6.anchor: الفرارمن الزحف وواحدة في جمع الجسد عقوق الوالدين وفيه ما فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says major sins are nearer seven hundred than seven, adding that repentance removes the status of major sin and persistence removes the status of minor sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r7.anchor: وروي الطبراني عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس أن رجلا قال له

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r8.claim: Scholars have written dedicated works on major sins; al-Alusi directs readers to Ibn Hajar's al-Zawajir.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r8.anchor: وقد ألف فيها غير واحد من العلماء وفي كتاب الزواجر تأليف العلامة ابن حجر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r9.claim: God's abundant forgiveness covers minor sins when major sins are avoided; this explains the exception and shows the lapse remains a sin forgiven through mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r9.anchor: إن ربك واسع المغفرة ( حيث يغفر الصغائر باجتناب الكبائر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r10.claim: Alternatively, God may forgive any sins, small or great, as He wills, so major sinners do not despair or imagine punishment is incumbent upon God.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r10.anchor: يغفر لمن يشاء من المؤمنين ما شاء من الذنوب صغيرها وكبيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r11.claim: Al-Alusi rejects analyzing الذين as the subject and واسع المغفرة as its predicate with an omitted link meaning “for them.”
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r11.anchor: وزعم بعض جواز كون الموصول مبتدأوهذه الجملة خبره والرابط محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r12.claim: God knows people and their states better than anyone.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r13.claim: Their creation occurred within the creation of their father Adam.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63/r13.anchor: في ضمن إنشاء أبيكم آدم عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r1.claim: Creation from earth is general creation as previously explained; alternatively, humans derive from semen formed from foods whose origin is earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r1.anchor: إنشاءا إجماليا حسبما مر بحقيقه وقيل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, humans are from earth because semen derives from foods originating in the earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r2.anchor: المني الذي يتكونون منه من الأغذية التي منشؤها من الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r3.claim: The first إذ is a temporal adverb modifying أعلم and retains its ordinary comparative sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r3.anchor: فإذا ظرف لأعلم وهو على بابه من التفضيل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r4.speaker: مكي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r4.claim: Makki takes إذ to mean that God is the sole knower of their circumstances then; al-Alusi objects that God could inform angels of them.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r4.anchor: وقال مكي : هو بمعنى عالم غذ تعلق علمه تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r5.claim: Another proposal makes إذ governed by an omitted imperative, ‘remember when He created you’; al-Alusi dismisses it.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : ( إذ ) منصوب بمحذوف والتقدير اذكروا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r6.claim: Embryos develop through ordered stages, all their states and deeds—including lapses—known to God; without His vast forgiveness, consequences would strike them.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r6.anchor: على أطوار مختلفة مترتبة لا يخفى عليه سبحانه حال

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r7.claim: Mentioning the mothers’ wombs, though embryos are necessarily inside them, points to their successive stages.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r7.anchor: وذكر ( فيبطون أمهاتكم ) مع أن الجنين ما كان

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r8.claim: Another view says the womb phrase underscores God's knowledge because the womb is intensely dark.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r8.anchor: وقيل : لتأكيد شأن العلم لما أن بطن الأم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r9.claim: The فاء connects the ban to the preceding point: lapses go unpunished through divine forgiveness, not because they are not sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r9.anchor: والفاء في قوله تعالى : ( فلا تزكوا أنفسكم ( لترتيب

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r10.claim: Do not claim complete freedom from sin or purity and superiority in good works; acknowledge God's favor and forgiveness.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r10.anchor: فلا تثنوا على أنفسكم بالطهارة عن المعاصي

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r11.claim: This resumption reinforces the ban on self-praise and indicates that some people avoid every sin.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r12.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r12.claim: Other interpretations take piety as avoiding shirk, or avoiding some sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r12.anchor: وقيل : اتقى الشرك وقيل : اتقى شيئا من المعاصي

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r13.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r13.claim: The verse was reportedly revealed about believers listing their prayers, fasting, and pilgrimage; this is blameworthy when done from vanity or ostentation, but otherwise permissible.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r13.anchor: والآية نزلت على ما قيل : في قوم من المؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r14.claim: Taking pleasure in obedience is itself obedience, and mentioning it can be gratitude.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r14.anchor: ولذا قيل : المسرة بالطاعة طاعة وذكرها شكر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r15.claim: Self-purification can be conveyed by gestures as well as words, including names implying purity.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r15.anchor: ولا فرق في التزكية بين أن تكون عبارة وأن تكون إشارة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r16.speaker: زينب بنت أبي سلمة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r16.claim: When Zaynab bint Abi Salama was named Barra, the Prophet said God knows the truly pious and renamed her Zaynab; Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Saʿd transmit it.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r16.anchor: عن زينب بنت أبي سلمة أنها سميت برة فقال رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r17.claim: The Prophet also changed Barra bint Jahsh’s name; changing such names is recommended.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r17.anchor: غير عليه الصلاة والسلام إلى ذلك اسم برة بنت جحش

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r18.claim: Names such as Baraka and Yasar, which may invite ill omen, are discouraged for tanzih; al-Nawawi reads the reported ban on Nafiʿ, Aflah, and Baraka as prohibitive.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r18.anchor: كما روي جابر : إن عشت إن الله أنهى أمتي أن يسموا نافعا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r19.claim: Dislike applies where a name’s implication of praise is strong and conventionally explicit; names like Saʿid and Hasan are not objectionable.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r19.anchor: والظاهر أن كراهة ما يشعر بالتزكية مخصوص بما إذاكان الإشعار قويا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r20.claim: Umar reportedly renamed a daughter called ʿAsiya as Jamila, though al-Alusi notes that the discussion merits further review.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r20.anchor: ابنة يقال لها : عاصية فسماها رصص جميلة كذا قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r21.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r21.claim: Another reading forbids people to praise one another for reputation or worldly gain or to certify virtue absolutely; testimony establishing rights remains allowed.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r21.anchor: وقيل : معنى لا تزكوا أنفسكم لا يزكي بعضكم بعضا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r22.speaker: ثابت بن الحارث الأنصاري
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r22.claim: Thabit reports that Jews called a deceased infant a ṣiddiq; the Prophet rejected this, saying God knows every fetus’s felicity or misery, and this verse was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p63#2/r22.anchor: عن ثابت بن الحرث الأنصاري قال كانت اليهود إذاهلك لهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r1.claim: The ownership statement is parenthetical; the “so that He may reward” clause is syntactically attached to the earlier verse’s meaning.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r1.anchor: وهذا معترض بين الآية الأولى وبين قوله: {ليجزي الذين أساءوا بما عملوا} فاللام في قوله: "ليجزي" متعلق بمعنى الآية الأولى؛

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة، مجاهد، الحسن، ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r5.claim: They treat the exception as connected: a person may lapse into an indecency once, then repent and stop; Ibn Abbas’s view is transmitted by ʿAṭāʾ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r5.anchor: إلا أن يلم بالفاحشة مرة ثم يتوب، ويقع الوقعة ثم ينتهي وهو قول أبي هريرة [ومجاهد، والحسن] (1) ، ورواية عطاء عن ابن عباس (2) .

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r6.claim: He defines “lamam” as anything short of associating partners with God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r6.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص: اللمم ما دون الشرك (3) .

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r7.speaker: أبو صالح، ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r7.claim: Abu Ṣāliḥ said it is a sin a person commits briefly and does not repeat; Ibn Abbas approved, saying a noble angel had helped him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r7.anchor: قال السدي قال أبو صالح: سئلت عن قول الله تعالى: "إلا اللمم"، فقلت: هو الرجل يلم بالذنب ثم لا يعاوده، فذكرت ذلك لابن عباس فقال: لقد أعانك عليها ملك كريم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r8.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas quotes the Prophet praying, “If You forgive, You forgive much; and what servant of Yours does not lapse?”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r8.anchor: وروينا عن عطاء عن ابن عباس في قوله: "إلا اللمم"، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن تغفر اللهم تغفر جما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r9.claim: The root sense of “lamam” or “ilmām” is a passing, occasional act, without repetition or persistence.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r9.anchor: وأصل "اللمم والإلمام": ما يعمله الإنسان الحين بعد الحين، ولا يكون إعادة، ولا إقامة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r10.claim: Another group takes the exception as disconnected, meaning “but minor lapses,” which are not major sins or indecencies.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r10.anchor: وقال آخرون: هذا استثناء منقطع، مجازه: لكن اللمم، ولم يجعلوا اللمم من الكبائر والفواحش،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r11.speaker: زيد بن ثابت، زيد بن أسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r11.claim: They say the lapses were deeds from the pre-Islamic past that God would not hold against the believers; this answered polytheists who taunted converts for formerly acting with them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411#2/r11.anchor: فقال بعضهم: هو ما سلف في الجاهلية فلا يؤاخذهم الله به، وذلك أن المشركين قالوا للمسلمين: إنهم كانوا بالأمس يعملون معنا؟ فأنزل الله هذه الآية. وهذا قول زيد بن ثابت، وزيد بن أسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r1.claim: God’s forgiveness is broad for someone who committed such a lapse and then repented; the phrase concludes there.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لمن فعل ذلك وتاب، تم الكلام هاهنا، ثم قال:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r2.claim: God created their forefather Adam from earth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r2.anchor: أي خلق أباكم آدم من التراب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r3.claim: “Ajinnah” is the plural of “janīn,” named for being concealed inside the womb.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r3.anchor: أجنة} جمع جنين، سمي جنينا لاجتنانه في البطن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the prohibition as “do not praise yourselves.”

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r5.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r5.claim: God knows what every soul will do and become, so people must neither absolve themselves of sins nor boast of their good deeds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r5.anchor: قال الحسن: علم الله من كل نفس ما هي صانعة وإلى ما هي صائرة، فلا تزكوا أنفسكم، لا تبرؤوها عن الآثام،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r6.speaker: الكلبي، مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r6.claim: They say the verse was revealed when people boasted of their worship, saying they prayed, fasted, and performed pilgrimage.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r6.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل: كان الناس يعملون أعمالا حسنة ثم يقولون: صلاتنا وصيامنا وحجنا، فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r7.claim: The person of piety is one who does good, obeys, and dedicates his work sincerely to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p413/r7.anchor: هو أعلم بمن اتقى} أي: بر وأطاع وأخلص العمل لله تعالى.

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r1.claim: Major sins are those with grave punishment, specifically sins with a stated threat.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r1.anchor: ما يكبر عقابه من الذنوب وهو ما رتب عليه الوعيد

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r2.claim: Another definition of major sins is those that incur a fixed penalty.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r2.anchor: الوعيد بخصوصه. وقيل ما أوجب الحد

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r3.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read كبير الإثم, intending the genus or idolatry.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف كبير الإثم على إرادة الجنس

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r4.claim: الفواحش means especially what is obscene among major sins.

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r5.claim: The exception means small sins, forgiven for those who avoid major sins; it is a disconnected exception.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r5.anchor: إلا ما قل وصغر فإنه مغفور من مجتنبي الكبائر

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r6.claim: الذين may be accusative as an adjective or praise, or nominative as predicate of an omitted subject.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r6.anchor: ومحل { الذين } النصب على الصفة أو المدح

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r7.claim: God may forgive minor sins when major ones are avoided, or any sins He wills; this prevents despair and the claim that punishment is incumbent on God.

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r8.claim: God knows people's states better than they do, from their creation from earth and formation in the womb.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r8.anchor: هو أعلم بكم } أعلم بأحوالكم منكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r9.claim: Do not praise yourselves for righteous deeds or claim purity from sins and base traits.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r9.anchor: فلا تثنوا عليها بزكاء العمل وزيادة الخير

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r10.claim: God knew the pious and others before bringing them forth from Adam's loins.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:32/r10.anchor: قبل أن يخرجكم من صلب آدم عليه السلام

BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r10.claim: Those who do good exert themselves to avoid major sins and indecencies.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r10.anchor: أي يكلفون أنفسهم ويجهدونها على أن يتركوا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r11.claim: Major sins are offenses the revealed law marks as grave through a threat of punishment or a legal penalty.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r11.anchor: أي ما عظم الشارع إثمه بعد الحريمه بالوعيد والحد

BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r12.claim: Indecencies are major offenses rejected by natural disposition and reason and regarded as vile.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r12.anchor: والفاحشة من الكبائر ما يكرهه الطبع وينكره العقل ويستخسه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r13.claim: The author reads the exception as disconnected: minor slips are forgiven, and those who fall into them remain among the people of good.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r14.claim: He calls the exception disconnected, yet notes that a minor sin can become major when treated lightly, as in the cited warning about slander.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p327/r14.anchor: ولعله وضع فيه { إلا } موضع { لكن }

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r1.claim: Lamam means minor sins, especially occasional slips that happen without deliberate choice, not a repeated practice or habit.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r1.anchor: ما يحصل منها في الأحيان كأنه وقع في صحابه فلتة بغير اختيار منه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r2.claim: Repeated or habitual minor wrongdoing is excluded from the pardon being described.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r3.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī says the root sense is approaching a sin, then refraining before committing it.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r3.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : وأصله مقاربة الذنب ثم الامتناع منه قبل الفعل

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r4.speaker: ذو النون
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r4.claim: Dhū al-Nūn says that an accomplished gnostic's mention of an indecency is like another person's committing it.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r4.anchor: قال ذو النون : ذكر الفاحشة من العارف كفلعها من غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r5.claim: The expression ألم بالمكان means to stay only briefly in a place.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r5.anchor: يقال : وألم بالمكان - إذا قل لبثه فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r6.speaker: أبو صالح
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r6.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ defines lamam as a person falling into a sin and then not repeating it; al-Suddī transmits the answer through al-Baghawī.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r6.anchor: وقال البغوي : قال السدي : قال أبو صالح أنه سئل عن اللمم فقال : هو الرجل يلم بالذنب ثم لا يعاوده

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r7.claim: When Abū Ṣāliḥ shared that definition, Ibn ʿAbbās praised it, saying a noble angel had helped him.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r7.anchor: فذكرت ذلك لابن عباس رضي الله عنهما فقال : لقد أعانك عليها ملك كريم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r8.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r8.claim: Al-Baghawī says the root idea is an act done from time to time without repeating it or persisting in it, which allows a connected exception.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r8.anchor: وعلى هذا يصح أن يكون الاستثناء متصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r9.claim: The author calls the exception disconnected, while noting that al-Baghawī's account also permits treating it as connected.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r9.anchor: وعلى هذا يصح أن يكون الاستثناء متصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r10.claim: God truly forgives minor sins and may forgive major ones; unlike human kings, His forgiveness is not limited by fear of losing control of His realm.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r10.anchor: فهو يغفر الصغائر حقا أوجبه على نفسه ويغفر الكبائر إن شاء بخلاف غيره من الملوك

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r11.claim: God knows people themselves and their condition, countering the assumption that He knows them only through their deeds or that readers can certify themselves as righteous.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r12.claim: God created humanity through Adam from earth, whose cold and dry character is associated with death; human capacities had not yet emerged to disclose what each person would become.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r12.anchor: التي طبعها طبع الموت : البرد واليبس

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r13.claim: The womb language specifies the hidden embryos in their mothers' bellies, where the four temperaments arise after the elements mix.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r13.anchor: فكانت هذه الأربعة الأخلاط الزكية والدنية , ولكن لا علم لكم أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r14.claim: God already knows each person's future good or evil, even if their conduct later seems different; people do not know what is within themselves.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r14.anchor: فهو يعلم إذ ذاك ما أنتم صائرون إليه من خير وشر وإن عملتم مدة من العمر بخلاف ذلك فإنه يعلم ما جبلكم عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r15.claim: People should not boast about virtue because humans love status out of deficiency and a person's course can change before death.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r15.anchor: ولما كان من عادة من سلم من الذنوب أن يفتخر على من قارفها لما بني الإنسان عليه من محبة الفخر

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r16.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r16.claim: Al-Qushayrī explains self-purification as praising oneself for purity and says doing so signals being veiled from God.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r16.anchor: فإن تزكيته لنفسه من علامات كونه محجوبا عن الله - قال القشيري -

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r17.claim: The warning can also cover praising a fellow believer, since praise may prove false and cause harm.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r17.anchor: أو مجازا بأن يثني على غيره من إخوانه فإنه كثيرا ما يثني بشيء فيظهر خلافه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r18.claim: He invokes a hadith warning that a person may do the deeds of the people of Paradise until near its end, yet their outcome can change.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r18.anchor: العبد ليعمل بعمل أهل الجنة حتى ما يكون بينه وبينها إلا باع أو ذراع

BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r19.claim: God knows who struggles against the self until attaining piety and gives that person more reward in both worlds than expected, especially when piety becomes settled.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p328/r19.anchor: فهو يوصله فوق ما يؤمل من الثواب في الدارين

DURR-FULL:v7p655/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas defines major sins as sins for which the Fire is named.
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش} قال: الكبائر ما سمى فيه النار

DURR-FULL:v7p655/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas defines indecencies as acts carrying a worldly legal penalty.
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش} قال: الكبائر ما سمى فيه النار {والفواحش} ما كان فيه حد في الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v7p655/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet's account of the bodily steps toward zina best resembles the meaning of lmam.
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: ما رأيت شيئا أشبه باللمم مما قال أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

DURR-FULL:v7p655/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r5.claim: The Prophet says each person's share of zina is written: the eye looks, the tongue speaks, the self desires, and the genitals either confirm or deny it.
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: ما رأيت شيئا أشبه باللمم مما قال أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن الله كتب على ابن آدم حظه من الزنا

DURR-FULL:v7p655/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r6.claim: Ibn Masud counts looking, kissing, touching, and walking toward zina as bodily zina; intercourse confirms actual zina, otherwise it is lmam.
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله {إلا اللمم} قال: زنا العينين النظر وزنا الشفتين التقبيل وزنا اليدين البطش وزنا الرجلين المشي

DURR-FULL:v7p655/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra identifies lmam as a glance, gesture, kiss, or touching; when the circumcised parts meet, ritual washing is required and it is zina.
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أنه سئل عن قوله {إلا اللمم} قال: هي النظرة والغمزة والقبلة والمباشرة فإذا مس الختان الختان

DURR-FULL:v7p655/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r8.claim: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr says lmam is what lies between the two prescribed penalties.
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r8.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الزبير قال: اللمم ما بين الحدين

DURR-FULL:v7p655/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says lmam is a person falling into an indecency and then repenting.
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {إلا اللمم} قال: هو الرجل يلم بالفاحشة ثم يتوب منها

DURR-FULL:v7p655/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r10.claim: The Prophet's quoted supplication says that God forgives abundant lapses and asks what servant is without lmam.
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r10.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن تغفر اللهم تغفر جما وأي عبد لك لا ألما

DURR-FULL:v7p655/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses lmam as whatever has already passed.
DURR-FULL:v7p655/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {إلا اللمم} يقول: إلا ما قد سلف

DURR-FULL:v7p656/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd says lmam refers to sins committed in pre-Islamic days, which God forgave when the people embraced Islam.
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r1.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال: قال المشركون: إنما كانوا بالأمس يعملون معنا فأنزل الله {إلا اللمم} ما كان منهم في الجاهلية

DURR-FULL:v7p656/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies major sin as shirk and indecency as zina; converts left these and were forgiven for their earlier lapses.
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r2.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم في قوله {الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم} قال: الشرك {والفواحش} قال: الزنا

DURR-FULL:v7p656/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
