DURR-FULL:v7p656/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra, in a report the narrator thinks is elevated to the Prophet, describes a lapse into zina or wine-drinking followed by repentance and no return.
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أراه رفعه في قوله {إلا اللمم} قال: اللمة من الزنا ثم يتوب ولا يعود

DURR-FULL:v7p656/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet's Companions called lmam an occasional lapse into zina or drinking, which one avoids or repents from.
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r4.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {إلا اللمم} قال: كان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقولون: هو الرجل يصيب اللمة

DURR-FULL:v7p656/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r5.claim: In a report from al-Hasan, the Prophet defines lmam as a passing act of zina, drinking, or theft that is not repeated.
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r5.anchor: عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أتدرون ما اللمم قالوا: الله ورسوله أعلم

DURR-FULL:v7p656/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the person lapses into the sin temporarily and then repents.
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {إلا اللمم} قال: يلم بها في الحين ثم يتوب

DURR-FULL:v7p656/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r7.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r7.claim: Abu Salih defines lmam as a person committing a sin and then repenting.
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r7.anchor: عن أبي صالح قال: سئلت عن اللمم فقلت: هو الرجل يصيب الذنب ثم يتوب

DURR-FULL:v7p656/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas praised Abu Salih's answer, saying a noble angel had helped him formulate it.
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r8.anchor: وأخبرت بذلك ابن عباس فقال: لقد أعانك عليها ملك كريم

DURR-FULL:v7p656/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r9.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r9.claim: Al-Hasan glosses lmam as zina committed for a brief time.
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r9.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {إلا اللمم} قال: الزنية في الحين

DURR-FULL:v7p656/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r10.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r10.claim: Abu Salih says lmam is a single sexual encounter that is not repeated.
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r10.anchor: عن أبي صالح في قوله {إلا اللمم} قال: الوقعة من الزنا لا يعود لها

DURR-FULL:v7p656/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r11.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r11.claim: Ata defines lmam as less than intercourse.
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r11.anchor: عن عطاء في قوله {إلا اللمم} قال: هو ما دون الجماع

DURR-FULL:v7p656/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r12.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r12.claim: Ikrima rejects al-Hasan's definition as a passing thought of zina; he says lmam means an embrace, kiss, or smelling.
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r12.anchor: عن عكرمة أنه ذكر له قول الحسن في اللمم هي الخطرة من الزنا فقال: لا ولكنها الضمة والقبلة والشمة

DURR-FULL:v7p656/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r13.speaker: ابن عمرو
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r13.claim: Ibn Amr says lmam is anything less than associating partners with God.
DURR-FULL:v7p656/r13.anchor: عن ابن عمرو قال: اللمم ما دون الشرك

DURR-FULL:v7p657/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas defines lmam as everything between the worldly and afterlife penalties, expiated by prayer; the former is a stipulated worldly penalty and the latter an offense ending in Hell.
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: اللمم كل شيء بين الحدين حد الدنيا وحد الآخرة يكفره الصلاة وهو دون كل موجب

DURR-FULL:v7p657/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r2.claim: Qatada likewise defines lmam as between the two penalties, below a worldly hadd and below an offense for which God has prescribed Hell.
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {إلا اللمم} قال: اللمم ما بين الحدين ما لم يبلغ حد الدنيا ولا حد الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v7p657/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r3.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit answers that God has prohibited indecencies, both outward and inward.
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r3.anchor: زيد بن ثابت عن هذه الآية {الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم} فقال: حرم الله عليك الفواحش

DURR-FULL:v7p657/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r4.claim: When Jews called a dead child a righteous intimate, the Prophet rejected that claim and said each soul is destined in the womb for misery or happiness; the whole verse was revealed then.
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r4.anchor: عن ثابت بن الحارث الأنصاري قال: كانت اليهود إذا هلك لهم صبي صغير قالوا: هذا صديق فبلغ ذلك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v7p657/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r5.claim: Mujahid links God's knowledge here to His being most knowing of the guided.
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {هو أعلم بكم إذ أنشأكم من الأرض} قال: هو كنحو قوله (وهو أعلم بالمهتدين)

DURR-FULL:v7p657/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the reference is to God creating Adam from earth and then creating you from Adam.
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r6.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله {إذ أنشأكم من الأرض وإذ أنتم أجنة} قال: حين خلق الله آدم من الأرض ثم خلقكم من آدم

DURR-FULL:v7p657/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r7.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says God knows what each soul will do and make, and where it will end.
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r7.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {هو أعلم بكم إذ أنشأكم من الأرض وإذ أنتم أجنة في بطون أمهاتكم} قال: علم الله من كل نفس ما هي عاملة

DURR-FULL:v7p657/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r8.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r8.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam explains the prohibition as not declaring yourselves innocent.
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r8.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم في قوله {فلا تزكوا أنفسكم} قال: لا تبرئوا أنفسكم

DURR-FULL:v7p657/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r9.claim: Mujahid says not to commit sins while claiming to act obediently.
DURR-FULL:v7p657/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {فلا تزكوا أنفسكم} قال: لا تعملوا بالمعاصي وتقولون: نعمل بالطاعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r4.claim: The clause describing those who avoid major sins modifies those who did good, defining them as people who perform good deeds and avoid prohibitions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r4.anchor: وقوله : { الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم } الخ صفة ل { الذين أحسنوا } ، أي الذين أحسنوا واجتنبوا كبائر الإثم والفواحش

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r5.claim: Doing good while avoiding forbidden acts completes piety; avoiding sins is itself part of excellence, since sins negate it and omitting good deeds is also bad.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r5.anchor: وهذا تنبيه على أن اجتناب ما ذكر يعد من الإحسان لأن فعل السيئات ينافي وصفهم بالذين أحسنوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r6.claim: Most readers have the plural kabāʾir; Hamza and al-Kisa'i read the singular masculine kabīr, since a collective noun can be singular or plural.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { كبائر الإثم } بصيغة جمع ( كبيرة ) . وقرأ حمزة والكسائي { كبير الإثم } بصيغة الإفراد والتذكير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r7.claim: Major sins are offenses that Islamic law strongly warns against, threatens with punishment, or assigns a prescribed penalty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r7.anchor: والمراد بكبائر الإثم : الآثام الكبيرة فيما شرع الله وهي ما شدد الدين التحذير منه أو ذكر له وعيدا بالعذاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r8.speaker: إمام الحرمين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r8.claim: Imam al-Haramayn defines major sins as crimes showing that the perpetrator has little regard for religion and weak religiosity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r8.anchor: قال إمام الحرمين : ( الكبائر كل جريمة تؤذن بقلة اكتراثث مرتكبها بالدين وبرقة ديانته )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r9.claim: The conjunction marks indecencies as distinct from major sins, though the categories overlap; indecencies are narrower and more serious.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r9.anchor: وعطف الفواحش يقتضي أن المعطوف بها مغاير للكبائر ولكنها مغايرة بالعموم والخصوص الوجهي ، فالفواحش أخص من الكبائر وهي أقوى إثما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r10.claim: Indecencies are acts that make their perpetrator an extreme transgressor, such as adultery, theft, and murder by ambush; the term is discussed at 7:33 and 4:31.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p120/r10.anchor: والفواحش : الفعلات التي يعد الذي فعلها متجاوزا الكبائر مثل الزنى والسرقة وقتل الغيلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r1.claim: God's vast forgiveness explains why lapses are excepted while the righteous can still be described as people who avoid major sins and indecencies.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r1.anchor: تعليل لاستثناء اللمم من اجتنابهم كبائر الإثم والفواحش شرطا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r2.claim: Calling God their Lord rather than using His proper name conveys the tender care a lord gives righteous servants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r2.anchor: وفي بناء الخبر على جعل المسند إليه { ربك } دون الاسم العلم إشعار بأن سعة المغفرة رفق بعباده الصالحين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r3.claim: Addressing the Prophet with your Lord, rather than addressing the community collectively, hints that his followers receive this care through his blessing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r3.anchor: وفي إضافة ( رب ) إلى ضمير النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم دون ضمير الجماعة إيماء إلى أن هذه العناية بالمحسنين من أمته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r4.claim: Vast means abundant forgiveness; spatial breadth is metaphorically used for abundant inclusion, as in 40:7.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r4.anchor: والواسع : الكثير المغفرة ، استعيرت السعة لكثرة الشمول لأن المكان الواسع يمكن أن يحتوي على العدد الكثير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r5.claim: The address is to believers in the context of recompense and forgiveness, not to Jews as some occasion reports claim; the sura is Meccan, while debate with Jews occurred in Medina.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r5.anchor: الخطاب للمؤمنين ، ووقوعه عقب قوله : { ليجزي الذين أساءوا بما عملوا ويجزي الذين أحسنوا بالحسنى } ينبىء عن اتصال معناه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r6.speaker: ثابت بن حارث الأنصاري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r6.claim: A report says Jews called a dead child a ṣiddīq; the Prophet denied this, saying every soul is destined as wretched or blessed, and the verse was then revealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r6.anchor: وأصله لعبد الله بن لهيعة عن ثابت بن حارث الأنصاري . قال : ( كانت اليهود إذا هلك لهم صبي صغير يقولون : هو صديق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r7.speaker: ابن معين ووكيع ويحيى القطان وابن مهدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r7.claim: Ibn Lahi'a, who transmitted the reported occasion, was judged weak by Ibn Ma'in and abandoned by Waki', Yahya al-Qattan, and Ibn al-Mahdi.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r7.anchor: وعبد الله بن لهيعة ضعفه ابن معين وتركه وكيع ويحيى القطان وابن مهدي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r8.speaker: الذهبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r8.claim: Al-Dhahabi says the critical practice is to treat Ibn Lahi'a as weak.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r9.claim: Ibn Ashur suspects a transmitter misstated that the verse was revealed then; the Prophet likely cited it generally against the Jews, since the sura is Meccan and their debate was in Medina.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r9.anchor: وإنما قرأها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أخذا بعموم قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya reports al-Tha'labi's account from al-Kalbi and Muqatil that the verse was revealed about believers who boasted of their deeds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : حكى الثعلبي عن الكلبي ومقاتل أنها نزلت في قوم من المؤمنين فخروا بأعمالهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r11.claim: Seeking an occasion of revelation aimed to connect the prohibition with the preceding forgiveness: God shows mercy and ease, then warns people not to commend themselves, as in 8:66.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p122/r11.anchor: وكأن الباعث على تطلب سبب لنزولها قصد إبداء وجه اتصال قوله : { فلا تزكوا أنفسكم } بما قبله وما بعده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r1.claim: The statement that God knows people is an explanatory answer to the implied question raised by His generous forgiveness: He knows their condition better and arranges what they cannot foresee.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r1.anchor: فينبغي أن تحل جملة { هو أعلم بكم } إلى آخرها استئنافا بيانيا لجملة { إن ربك واسع المغفرة }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r2.speaker: الله تعالى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r2.claim: A hadith qudsi similarly says God has prepared for the righteous what no eye has seen, ear heard, or human heart imagined.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r2.anchor: ونظيره ما في الحديث القدسي قال الله تعالى : ( أعددت لعبادي الصالحين ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r3.claim: The phrase when He created you is a temporal adjunct to He knows, and refers to creating humanity's origin, Adam, from earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r3.anchor: وقوله : { إذ أنشأكم } ظرف متعلق ب ( أعلم ) ، أي هو أعلم بالناس من وقت إنشائه إياهم من الأرض وهو وقت خلق أصلهم آدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r4.claim: Humanity's earthly origin entails limited capacity for hardship; God knew the stages of human development and that Muhammad's community would be especially weak.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r4.anchor: والمعنى : أن إنشاءهم من الأرض يستلزم ضعف قدرهم عن تحمل المشاق مع تفاوت أطوار نشأة بني آدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r5.speaker: موسى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r5.claim: During the night journey, after fifty prayers were prescribed, Moses told Muhammad that his community could not bear them, drawing on his experience with Israel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r5.anchor: من قول موسى لمحمد عليهما الصلاة والسلام حين فرض الله على أمته خمسين صلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r6.claim: Human weakness is inherent from Adam's earthly origin, although it varies; 4:28 states that the human being was created weak.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r7.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r7.claim: The Prophet is also quoted as saying that woman was created from a crooked rib.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124/r7.anchor: ومنه قوله النبي : ( إن المرأة خلقت من ضلع أعوج )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r1.speaker: أم عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r1.claim: After Uthman ibn Maz'un died, Umm Atiyya praised him; the Prophet asked how she knew God honored him, then said he hoped for his good but did not know his fate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r1.anchor: ودخل عليه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت أم عطية : ( رحمة الله عليك أبا السائب ( كنية عثمان بن مظعون ) فشهادتي عليك لقد أكرمك الله فقال لها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وما يدريك أن الله أكرمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r2.claim: After hearing the Prophet, Umm Atiyya said she would no longer praise anyone; companions commonly limited praise to what they knew and declined to certify anyone before God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r2.anchor: قالت أم عطية : فلا أزكي أحدا بعد ما سمعت هذا من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد شاع من آداب عصر النبوة بين الصحابة التحرز من التزكية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r3.claim: Muslim reports that the Prophet prohibited the name Barra, saying people should not praise themselves; he renamed her Zaynab because God knows the truly pious.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r3.anchor: وروى مسلم عن محمد بن عمرو بن عطاء قال : ( سميت ابنتي برة فقالت لي زينب بنت بن سلمة إن رسول الله نهى عن هذا الإسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r4.claim: The prohibition concerns declaring one's own soul pure or righteous; judgment belongs to God because inward states may not match outward appearances.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r4.anchor: وقد ظهر أن النهي متوجه إلى أن يقول أحد ما يفيد زكاء النفس ، أي طهارتها وصلاحها ، تفويضا بذلك إلى الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r5.claim: The rule trains people to be cautious in judgment and in assessing reports, clues, and outward signs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r5.anchor: وهذا من التأديب على التحرز في الحكم والحيطة في الخبرة واتهام القرائن والبوارق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r6.claim: The prohibition does not bar reporting tested trustworthiness or justice for testimony and transmission; later technical ta'dil uses تزكية with a different, clear meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r6.anchor: فلا يدخل في هذا النهي الإخبار عن أحوال الناس بما يعلم منهم وجربوا فيه من ثقة وعدالة في الشهادة والرواية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r7.claim: God's superior knowledge explains why people should leave this judgment to Him: He knows the degree, deficiency, or falsity of anyone's piety.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r7.anchor: ووقعت جملة { هو أعلم بمن اتقى } موقع البيان لسبب النهي أو لأهم أسبابه ، أي فوضوا ذلك إلى الله إذ هو أعلم بمن اتقى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r8.claim: The hadith formula I do not certify anyone before God means a speaker must not exceed their standing by claiming God's prerogative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p125/r8.anchor: وهذا معنى ما ورد في الحديث أن يقول من يخبر عن أحد بخير : ( لا أزكي على الله أحدا ) أي لا أزكى أحدا معتليا حق الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r1.claim: In Arabic, al-lamam denotes drawing near to something; Ibn al-Jawzi introduces six interpretations for its Qur’anic use.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r1.anchor: يجتنبون كبير الإثم واللمم في كلام العرب المقاربة للشيء وفي المراد به ها هنا ستة أقوال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r2.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r2.claim: Lamam means sins and indecencies committed before Islam, which are forgiven upon entering Islam.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r2.anchor: ما ألموا به من الإثم والفواحش في الجاهلية فإنه يغفر في الإسلام قاله زيد بن ثابت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والسدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r3.claim: Lamam is committing a sin once, then repenting and not returning to it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r3.anchor: أن يلم بالذنب مرة ثم يتوب ولا يعود قاله ابن عباس والحسن والسدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو هريرة والشعبي ومسروق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r4.claim: Lamam means minor sins such as a glance or kiss and anything short of illicit intercourse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r4.anchor: أنه صغار الذنوب كالنظرة والقبلة وما كان دون الزنا قاله ابن مسعود وأبو هريرة والشعبي ومسروع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r5.claim: A report from the Prophet describes the eyes’ zina as looking, the tongue’s as speaking, and desire within the soul; actual intercourse makes it zina, otherwise it is lamam.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r5.anchor: حديث أبي هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن الله كتب على ابن آدم حظه من الزنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r6.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r6.claim: Lamam is something a person merely intends or is on the verge of doing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r6.anchor: أنه ما يهم به الإنسان قاله محمد بن الحنفية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r7.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r7.claim: Lamam is a thought that occurs in the heart.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r7.anchor: أنه ألم بالقلب أي خطر قاله سعيد بن المسيب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r8.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r8.claim: Lamam is looking without deliberately intending to look.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r8.anchor: أنه النظر من غير تعمد قاله الحسين بن الفضل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r9.claim: On the first two interpretations the exception is of the same kind as what precedes; on the remaining interpretations it is not.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r9.anchor: فعلى القولين الأولين يكون الاستثناء من الجنس وعلى باقي الأقوال ليس من الجنس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r10.claim: God’s forgiveness is ample for someone who commits such a lapse and then repents.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس لمن فعل ذلك ثم تاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r11.claim: God knew people before creating them from earth, beginning with Adam, and as embryos; He knows their deeds and what they will become.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r11.anchor: هو أعلم بكم يعني قبل خلقكم إذ أنشأكم من الأرض يعني آدم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r12.claim: Do not testify that you are pure and innocent of sins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r12.anchor: فلا تزكوا أنفسكم أي لا تشهدوا لها أنها زكية بريئة من المعاصي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r13.claim: An alternative explanation is that people should not boast about the goodness of their deeds.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r14.speaker: عائشة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r14.claim: Aisha says the verse was revealed because Jews called a child who died among them a ṣiddīq.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r14.anchor: أن اليهود كانوا إذا هلك لهم صبي قالوا صديق فنزلت هذه الآية هذا قول عائشة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r15.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r15.claim: Muqatil says some Muslims praised themselves for praying and fasting, prompting the verse’s revelation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r15.anchor: أن ناسا من المسلمين قالوا قد صلينا وصمنا وفعلنا يزكون أنفسهم فنزلت هذه الآية قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r16.speaker: علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r16.claim: Ali explains the God-fearing person as one who performs a good deed and turns away from sin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r16.anchor: أحدها عمل حسنة و أرعوى عن معصية قاله علي رضي الله عنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r17.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r17.claim: Hasan says the God-fearing person acts sincerely for God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r17.anchor: والثاني أخلص العمل لله قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r18.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r18.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r18.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi interprets piety here as avoiding idolatry and believing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#4/r18.anchor: والثالث اتقى الشرك فآمن قاله الثعلبي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r2.claim: The people rewarded with goodness are those who avoid major sins and indecencies; if they commit lesser sins, God forgives and conceals them, as 4:31 says.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r2.anchor: ثم فسر المحسنين بأنهم الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش، أي: لا يتعاطون المحرمات والكبائر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r3.claim: The exception of minor lapses is disconnected because lumam means small sins and insignificant deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r3.anchor: وهذا استثناء منقطع؛ لأن اللمم من صغائر الذنوب ومحقرات الأعمال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet's description reported by Abu Hurayra is the closest example of lumam: a person's inevitable share of zina includes the eye's gaze, tongue's speech and the soul's desire, while the genitals either enact or refuse it; the report is in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: ما رأيت شيئا أشبه باللمم مما قال أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r5.claim: Ibn Masud counts gaze, kissing, touching and walking toward sin as forms of zina; if the genitals complete the act it is zina, otherwise it is lumam. Masruq and al-Shaʿbi say likewise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r5.anchor: عن أبي الضحى؛ أن ابن مسعود قال: "زنا العينين النظر، وزنا الشفتين التقبيل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra explains lumam as a kiss, squeeze, glance or touching; intercourse requiring ghusl is zina.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r6.anchor: عبد الرحمن بن نافع -الذي يقال له: ابن لبابة الطائفي-قال: سألت أبا هريرة عن قول الله: {إلا اللمم} قال: القبلة، والغمزة، والنظرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، وزيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ali ibn Abi Talha, and Zayd ibn Aslam interpret lumam as what has already passed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460/r7.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {إلا اللمم} إلا ما سلف. وكذا قال زيد بن أسلم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says lumam is a person who briefly commits a sin and then leaves it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه قال: في هذه الآية: {إلا اللمم} قال: الذي يلم بالذنب ثم يدعه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r2.speaker: شاعر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r2.claim: An unnamed poet's line cited with Mujahid's explanation uses ألما for a lapse that may be forgiven, asking what servant has not slipped.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r2.anchor: قال الشاعر: إن تغفر اللهم تغفر جما … وأي عبد لك ما ألما?!

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says pre-Islamic people circumambulated the Kaaba reciting the line asking God to forgive generously and asking what servant has not slipped; Ibn Jarir and others also transmit it as a Prophetic report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {إلا اللمم} قال: الرجل يلم بالذنب ثم ينزع عنه، قال: وكان أهل الجاهلية يطوفون بالبيت وهم يقولون:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says lumam is a person who falls into an indecency and repents, and attributes the forgiveness verse to the Prophet's recitation of the couplet; al-Tirmidhi calls this report hasan sahih gharib, known only through Zakariyya ibn Ishaq, while al-Bazzar says it is the only connected route and Ibn Kathir questions its Prophetic attribution.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم} قال: هو الرجل يلم بالفاحشة ثم يتوب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan, tentatively raising the report to the Prophet, says a brief instance of zina, theft or drinking counts as lumam if the person repents and does not return; al-Hasan also reports the same definition without naming a Prophetic attribution.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p460#2/r5.anchor: عن الحسن، عن أبي هريرة -أراه رفعه-: {الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم} قال: "اللمة من الزنا ثم يتوب ولا يعود،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r1.speaker: أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet's Companions understood lumam as a brief instance of zina or drinking that one avoids thereafter and repents from.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r1.anchor: عن أبي رجاء، عن الحسن في قول الله: {الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم} قال: كان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقولون: هو الرجل يصيب اللمة من الزنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains lumam as a sin committed from time to time; when asked whether he meant zina, he answers yes, followed by repentance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r2.anchor: عن عطاء، عن ابن عباس: {إلا اللمم} يلم بها في الحين. قلت: الزنا؟ قال: الزنا ثم يتوب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r3.claim: In another report Ibn Abbas defines lumam as committing a sin once.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: {اللمم} الذي يلم المرة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r4.speaker: السدي، وابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says, through Abu Salih, that lumam is a sin followed by repentance; Ibn Abbas praises the answer as helped by a noble angel.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: قال أبو صالح: سئلت عن {اللمم} فقلت: هو الرجل يصيب الذنب ثم يتوب. وأخبرت بذلك ابن عباس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r5.claim: Ibn Amr defines lumam as anything short of associating partners with God; Ibn Kathir notes that the route through al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah is weak.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r5.anchor: عن عمرو بن شعيب؛ أن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: {اللمم} : ما دون الشرك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r6.speaker: ابن الزبير، وابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r6.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr and Ibn Abbas define lumam as what lies between the worldly legal penalty and the punishment of the afterlife.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r6.anchor: عن ابن الزبير: {إلا اللمم} قال: ما بين الحدين: حد الدنيا (1) وعذاب الآخرة. وكذا رواه شعبة، عن الحكم، عن ابن عباس، مثله سواء.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، وعكرمة، وقتادة، والضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says lesser acts between the worldly and afterlife penalties are lumam and are expiated by prayers; worldly penalties are prescribed punishments, while afterlife penalties are sins whose punishment is deferred to Hell. Ikrima, Qatada and al-Dahhak agree.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p461/r7.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {إلا اللمم} كل شيء بين (2) الحدين: حد الدنيا (3) وحد الآخرة، تكفره الصلوات، وهو (4) اللمم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462/r1.claim: God's mercy encompasses everything, and He forgives every sin for whoever repents, as stated in 39:53.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462/r1.anchor: {إن ربك واسع المغفرة} أي: رحمته وسعت كل شيء، ومغفرته تسع الذنوب كلها لمن تاب منها،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462/r2.claim: God knows people's conditions, actions and words from the time He created their forefather Adam from earth, drew his descendants from his loins like tiny particles, and divided them into the people of Paradise and of the Fire.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462/r2.anchor: حين أنشأ أباكم آدم من الأرض، واستخرج ذريته من صلبه أمثال الذر، ثم قسمهم فريقين: فريقا للجنة وفريقا للسعير (6) .

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462/r3.claim: While people are embryos, the angel assigned to them records provision, lifespan, deeds and whether each will be wretched or blessed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462/r3.anchor: وكذا قوله: {وإذ أنتم أجنة في بطون أمهاتكم} قد كتب الملك الذي يوكل به رزقه وأجله وعمله، وشقي أم سعيد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462/r4.speaker: مكحول
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462/r4.claim: Makḥul reflects that at every stage—embryo, nursing child, youth and old age—some die while others survive, ending with the question of what remains to await; Ibn Abi Hatim transmits this from him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462/r4.anchor: قال مكحول: كنا أجنة في بطون أمهاتنا، فسقط منا من سقط، وكنا فيمن بقي، ثم كنا مراضع فهلك منا من هلك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462#2/r1.claim: Do not praise yourselves, congratulate yourselves, or boast about your deeds; God knows best who is pious, as 4:49 says.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462#2/r1.anchor: أي: تمدحوها وتشكروها وتمنوا بأعمالكم، {هو أعلم بمن اتقى} ، كما قال: {ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم بل الله يزكي من يشاء ولا يظلمون فتيلا} [النساء: 49] .

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462#2/r2.speaker: زينب بنت أبي سلمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462#2/r2.claim: Zaynab bint Abi Salama reports that the Prophet forbade naming a girl Barrah because it self-praises; he said God knows the virtuous better than people and renamed her Zaynab. Muslim records the report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462#2/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تزكوا أنفسكم، إن الله أعلم بأهل البر منكم".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462#2/r3.speaker: أبو بكرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462#2/r3.claim: The Prophet warns that praising someone to his face is like cutting his neck; if praise is unavoidable, say you think well of him while leaving his true standing to God and avoiding a claim of purity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462#2/r3.anchor: عن أبيه قال: مدح رجل رجلا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ويلك! قطعت عنق صاحبك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462#2/r4.speaker: المقداد بن الأسود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462#2/r4.claim: When a man praised Uthman to his face, Miqdad threw dirt at him and said the Prophet ordered them to throw dirt in the faces of flatterers; Ahmad, Muslim and Abu Dawud transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p462#2/r4.anchor: عن منصور، عن إبراهيم، عن همام بن الحارث قال: جاء رجل إلى عثمان فأثنى عليه في وجهه، قال: فجعل المقداد بن الأسود يحثو في وجهه التراب

BURSEVI:v9p197#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p197#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p197#2/r7.claim: The clause about avoiding major sins may qualify 'those who do good' or replace it; Saʿdī al-Muftī objects that treating it as the focus leaves the earlier phrase idle.
BURSEVI:v9p197#2/r7.anchor: صفة للذين أحسنوا أو بدل منه لكن قال سعدي المفتي

BURSEVI:v9p197#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p197#2/r8.speaker: سعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v9p197#2/r8.claim: Saʿdī al-Muftī considers the parsing awkward if 'those who avoid' is the main focus and 'those who do good' is effectively omitted; reversing the order would work.
BURSEVI:v9p197#2/r8.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي : لا حسن في جعل الذين الخ مقصودا بالنسبة

BURSEVI:v9p197#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p197#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p197#2/r9.claim: Avoidance is purification, which comes before adornment; its present tense indicates continuous practice. Believers must habitually avoid sins to merit Paradise, whereas one voluntary good deed earns reward even once.
BURSEVI:v9p197#2/r9.anchor: يقول الفقير : الاجتناب من باب التخلية بالمعجمة وهي أقدم

BURSEVI:v9p198/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p198/r1.claim: Major sins are offenses with grave punishment and a specific threat, including idolatry, adultery, and murder, especially killing one's own buried-alive daughters.
BURSEVI:v9p198/r1.anchor: الإثم ما يكبر عقابه من الذنوب وهو ما رتب عليه الوعيد بخصوصه

BURSEVI:v9p198/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198/r2.speaker: ابن جبير
BURSEVI:v9p198/r2.claim: Ibn Jubayr defines major sins as those for which the sinner does not seek forgiveness, citing the saying that no major sin remains with repentance and no minor sin with persistence.
BURSEVI:v9p198/r2.anchor: وقال ابن جبير : هي ما لا يستغفر منه

BURSEVI:v9p198/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p198/r3.claim: A hadith warns against treating sins as trivial; Ibn ʿAbbās estimates major sins at nearly seventy, and the commentary refers to an earlier discussion in Sūrat al-Shūrā.
BURSEVI:v9p198/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : هي إلى سبعين أقرب

BURSEVI:v9p198/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p198/r4.claim: Fawāḥish are especially shameful major offenses, particularly adultery and unlawful killing; naming them after major sins specifies grave examples within the general category.
BURSEVI:v9p198/r4.anchor: وما فحش من الكبائر خصوصا الزنى والقتل بغير حق

BURSEVI:v9p198/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198/r5.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v9p198/r5.claim: Al-Rāghib defines fāḥish, faḥshāʾ, and fāḥisha as acts or words of great ugliness.
BURSEVI:v9p198/r5.anchor: قال الراغب : الفحش والفحشاء والفاحشة ما عظم قبحه

BURSEVI:v9p198/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p198/r6.claim: Lamam denotes approaching a sin without committing it, and by extension a minor sin; the exception is disconnected because minor sins are outside the major sins and are forgiven when major sins are avoided.
BURSEVI:v9p198/r6.anchor: اللمم مقاربة المعصية ويعبر به عن الصغيرة من قولك الممت بكذا

BURSEVI:v9p198/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p198/r7.claim: Five daily prayers, one Friday to the next, and one Ramadan to the next expiate intervening sins when major sins are avoided; good deeds erase evil deeds.
BURSEVI:v9p198/r7.anchor: يعني أن الصلوات الخمس والجمعة إلى الجمعة ورمضان

BURSEVI:v9p198/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p198/r8.claim: One view calls an unintentional glance lamam, but a repeated deliberate glance is sinful; it also includes a wink or kiss.
BURSEVI:v9p198/r8.anchor: وقيل : هي النظر بلا تعمد فإن أعاد النظر فليس بلمم

BURSEVI:v9p198/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198/r9.speaker: نبهان التمار
BURSEVI:v9p198/r9.claim: Nabhān the date seller embraced and kissed a customer who came to buy dates; she rebuked him, he regretted it, and went to the Messenger.
BURSEVI:v9p198/r9.anchor: كما روى أن نبهان التمار أتته امرأة لتشتري التمر

BURSEVI:v9p198/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p198/r10.claim: Another explanation limits lamam to a sinful thought that crosses the heart without a firm resolve.
BURSEVI:v9p198/r10.anchor: وقيل : هي الخطرة من الذنب أي ما خطره من الذنب

BURSEVI:v9p198/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p198/r11.claim: Another view defines lamam as any sin for which God has specified neither a legal penalty nor punishment.
BURSEVI:v9p198/r11.anchor: وقيل : كل ذنب لم يذكر الله عليه حدا ولا عذابا

BURSEVI:v9p198/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198/r12.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v9p198/r12.claim: Some say lamam is a sin committed from time to time, without becoming a settled habit or persistent practice.
BURSEVI:v9p198/r12.anchor: وقال بعضهم : اللمم والإلمام ما يعمله الإنسان الحين بعد الحين

BURSEVI:v9p198/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198/r13.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
BURSEVI:v9p198/r13.claim: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya says every good or evil intention is lamam, citing the Prophet's report that Satan and the angel each prompt a person; Satan whispers and the angel inspires.
BURSEVI:v9p198/r13.anchor: قال محمد بن الحنفية : كل ما هممت به من خير وشر فهو لمم

BURSEVI:v9p198/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v9p198/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says lamam is a single lapse into indecency followed by repentance without persistence; the exception is then connected, and God accepts repentance.
BURSEVI:v9p198/r14.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما معناه إلا أن يلمم بالفاحشة مرة ثم يتوب

BURSEVI:v9p198/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v9p198/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās cites Abū Hurayra's Prophetic report: the eye, lips, hand, and feet each have a share of adultery; the genitals either consummate or deny it, and without consummation it is lamam.
BURSEVI:v9p198/r15.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : ما رأيت شيئا أشبه باللمم مما نقله أبو هريرة

BURSEVI:v9p198/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198/r16.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
BURSEVI:v9p198/r16.claim: Al-Asʾila al-Muqḥima says all sins are major in the absolute sense because they disobey God, though some are greater relatively; shirk is greatest, and lamam is major if it means a sin whose perpetrator repents, as Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan, and Companions including Abū Hurayra say.
BURSEVI:v9p198/r16.anchor: وفي الأسئلة المقحمة الذنوب كلها كبائر على الحقيقة لأن الكل تتضمن مخالفة أمر الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r1.claim: God's forgiveness is vast enough to cover minor sins when major sins are avoided; this explains the exception and shows they are exempt through forgiveness, not because they are no sins.
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r1.anchor: حيث يغفر الصغائر باجتناب الكبائر فالجملة تعليل لاستثناء اللمم

BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r2.claim: The Najmī gloss identifies three major attachments: the commanding self, desire that fans the self's fire, and worldly life, the root of wrongdoing; their obscenities are violating law for nature, loving worldly pleasures, and turning from God toward other things.
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r2.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : كبائر الإثم ثلاث مراتب : محبة النفس

BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r3.claim: In that reading, lamam is a slight humanly necessary inclination toward self, desire, or the world, such as bodily rest and a modest worldly share taken as a right rather than selfish gain; fulfilling rights is forgiven, while pursuing gratification is delusion.
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r3.anchor: قوله إلا اللمم أي الميل اليسير إلى النفس والهوى والدنيا بحسب الضرورة البشرية

BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r4.claim: The Sufi gloss sees vast forgiveness as covering the darkness of metaphorical existence with the light of real existence through annihilation of human nature and subsistence through divine identity.
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r4.anchor: ومن سعة غفرانه ستر ظلمة الوجود المجازي بنور الوجود الحقيقي

BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r5.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r5.claim: A spiritual elder says legitimate worldly obligations, such as serving people or thanking them for benefits, do not impair servanthood; egoistic worldly aims without divine command do and require returning to God.
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r5.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : من استرقه الكون بحكم مشروع كالسعي في مصالح العباد

BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r6.speaker: بعض العارفين
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r6.claim: Some gnostics reason that a believer who sins under threat of punishment must feel regret; since the Prophet says regret is repentance, that remorse cancels the threat, while the believer combines good and bad deeds.
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r6.anchor: وقال بعض العارفين : من المحال أن يأتي مؤمن معصية توعد الله عليها بالعقوبة

BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r7.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r7.claim: The cited Prophetic saying declares that remorse is repentance, supporting the view that a believer's regret cancels the threatened punishment.
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r7.anchor: وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم الندم توبة

BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r8.speaker: بعض العارفين
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r8.claim: The gnostics connect the believer who combines good and bad deeds to the verse saying God may turn in mercy to such people.
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r8.anchor: فهو من الذين خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا وقد قال تعالى فيهم عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم

BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r9.claim: One should regret one's sins and not presume upon God's mercy, since alongside His vast forgiveness God is severe in force and punishment.
BURSEVI:v9p198#2/r9.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يندم على المعاصي الواقعة منه ولا يغتر بالرب الكريم

BURSEVI:v9p199/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p199/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p199/r1.claim: God knows people's circumstances and acts, including lamam, from their creation within Adam from earth and their successive stages as embryos in their mothers' wombs.
BURSEVI:v9p199/r1.anchor: أي خلقكم في ضمن إنشاء أبيكم آدم عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v9p199/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p199/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p199/r2.claim: Ajinnah is the plural of janīn, a fetus, literally something buried or concealed in the womb; the word derives from covering, and after birth the child is called a newborn or miscarriage instead.
BURSEVI:v9p199/r2.anchor: والجنين الدفين في الشيء المستتر فيه من جنه إذا ستره

BURSEVI:v9p199/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p199/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p199/r3.claim: The author lists age terms in ordinary Arabic and legal usage: fetus, child, boy, young man, middle-aged man, and elder, with differing age boundaries in language and law.
BURSEVI:v9p199/r3.anchor: هذا في اللغة وفي الشرع يسمى غلاما إلى البلوغ

BURSEVI:v9p199/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p199/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p199/r4.claim: Mentioning the mothers' wombs after 'embryos' intensifies the proof of God's knowledge and power: wombs are utterly dark, so knowledge of a fetus there means no state is hidden from Him.
BURSEVI:v9p199/r4.anchor: فإن بطون الأمهات في غاية الظلمة ومن علم حال الجنين فيها

BURSEVI:v9p199/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p199/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p199/r5.claim: The prohibition follows because freedom from punishment for lamam comes from God's forgiveness despite His knowledge of the sin, not from its being no sin; do not claim total purity or imply immaculate deeds, but thank God for His grace.
BURSEVI:v9p199/r5.anchor: الفاء لترتيب الهي عن تزكية النفس على ما سبق

BURSEVI:v9p199/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p199/r6.speaker: الحسن
BURSEVI:v9p199/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says God knows what each soul will do and what it will become; people should neither declare themselves free of sins nor praise their good deeds, which count only when sincerely for God.
BURSEVI:v9p199/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن رحمه الله : علم الله من كل نفس ما هي صانعة

BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r1.claim: The Persian couplet reinforces the warning against self-praise: do not claim a pure musk unless you possess it, since quality becomes apparent on its own.
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r1.anchor: اكر مسك خالص ندارى مكوى وكرهست خود فاش كردد ببوى

BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r2.claim: A Prophetic report commands throwing dust in flatterers' faces, meaning people who praise qualities absent from the person praised; dust may be literal or a metaphor for rebuffing them before they become arrogant.
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r2.anchor: وأما من زكاه الغير ومدحه فقد ورد فيه (احثوا في وجه المداحين)

BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r3.claim: Other explanations take the command to mean either giving flatterers nothing or paying them to silence them and prevent slander; the author also sees a hint that money is lowly like dust.
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : المراد به أن لا يعطوهم شيئا لمدحهم

BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r4.speaker: أبو الليث
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r4.claim: Abū al-Layth distinguishes three kinds of praise: praise to someone's face is forbidden; praise in absence when one knows it will reach them is also forbidden; private praise without concern whether it reaches them is allowed if truthful.
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r4.anchor: قال ابو الليث في تفسيره : المدح على ثلاثة أوجه : الأول

BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r5.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r5.claim: The Mathnawī verses say humans naturally seek praise because the Creator loves thanks and praise; even a person of virtue can be inflated by it, while false praise exposes an empty person.
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r5.anchor:
وفي المثنوي :
خلق ما در صورت خود كرد حق

BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r6.claim: Praising someone after death is permissible if it does not exceed bounds, unlike the excessive praise of the Rāfiḍa for the Prophet's family.
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r6.anchor: وأما المدح بعد الموت فلا بأس به إذا لم يجاوز الحد

BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r7.claim: God knows who avoids all sins; the statement reinforces the ban on self-purification and signals that some people in the group fear all sins.
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r7.anchor: وهو استئناف مقرر للنهي ومشعر تأن فيهم

BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r8.claim: It is said that people who boasted of prayer, fasting, and pilgrimage prompted the verse; this applies to self-admiration or ostentation, not gratitude for God's success or joy in obedience.
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r8.anchor: وقيل : كان ناس يعملون أعمالا حسنة ثم يقولون

BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r9.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r9.claim: The Najmī gloss contrasts people's finite, faculty-bound general knowledge of themselves with God's unrestricted, detailed knowledge, which is more complete and comprehensive.
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r9.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية يشير به إلى أن علم الإنسان بنفسه علم إجمالي

BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r10.claim: The author cites the Prophetic report that God created Adam in His image, then notes another version whose wording is left unfinished in this excerpt.
BURSEVI:v9p199#2/r10.anchor: إن الله خلق آدم على صورته وفي رواية أخرى على صورة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r1.speaker: الطبري
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says major sins are associating partners with God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r2.speaker: بعض الفقهاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r2.claim: Some jurists define them as sins punished by a fixed penalty.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r2.anchor: ما زجر عنه بالحد , حكاه بعض الفقهاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r3.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĪsā says they are sins only repentance can expiate.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r3.anchor: ما لا يكفر إلا بالتوبة , حكاه ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r4.claim: The Prophet names associating a partner with God, killing a child from fear of sharing food, and adultery with a neighbor’s wife; Sharāḥbīl reports this from Ibn Masʿūd.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r4.anchor: عن الكبائر فقال : ( أن تدعو لله ندا وهو خلقك

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r5.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr reports Ibn ʿAbbās: major sins are nearer seven hundred than seven; no major sin with forgiveness sought, nor minor sin persisted in. Al-Māwardī infers sins not repented are major.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r5.anchor: أن رجلا سأل ابن عباس عن الكبائر أسبع هي ؟ قال : إلى سبعمائة أقرب

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r6.claim: One view takes al-fawāḥish as all disobedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r6.anchor: أنها جميع المعاصي . الثاني : أنها الزنى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r7.claim: Another view restricts them to fornication.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r7.anchor: الثاني : أنها الزنى . وأما اللمم المستثنى ففيه ثمانية

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r8.speaker: ابن زيد بن ثابت
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd b. Thābit says the exception covers pre-Islamic sins forgiven upon entering Islam.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r8.anchor: إلا اللمم الذي ألموا به في الجاهلية من الإثم والفواحش

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r9.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid say it is a sin one commits and then repents of.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r9.anchor: قاله الحسن ومجاهد . الثالث : هو أن يعزم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r10.claim: Lamam may be intending intercourse, then turning back and desisting; Ibn ʿAbbās transmits a supporting Prophetic saying.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p399#2/r10.anchor: هو أن يعزم على المواقعة ثم يرجع عنها مقلعا وقد روى عمرو بن دينار

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r1.claim: The quoted supplication asks God to forgive abundantly, since no servant is without a lapse; the preceding fragment introduces it as the Prophet’s saying.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r1.anchor: إن تغفر اللهم تغفر جما وأي عبد لك لا ألما

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says lamam includes acts short of intercourse: kissing, touching, looking, and lying together.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r2.anchor: القبلة والغمزة والنظرة والمضاجعة , قاله ابن مسعود

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r3.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says each soul has an allotted share of illicit sex: eye is looking, tongue is speech, self desires, and genitals confirm or deny; Ibn ʿAbbās calls it like lamam.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r3.anchor: من قول أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( كتب الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r4.claim: Another view says lamam means minor sins.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda say it is a sin without a worldly penalty or afterlife punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r5.anchor: حد في الدنيا ولم يستحق عليه في الآخرة عذاب , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r6.speaker: بعض التابعين
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r6.claim: Some Successors say it is the first glance; a repeated glance is no longer lamam, so the term covers nonrecurring sins, as poetry supports.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r6.anchor: قاله بعض التابعين , فجعله ما لم يتكرر من الذنوب

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r7.claim: Abū Hurayra gives marriage as another meaning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r7.anchor: النكاح , وهذا قول أبي هريرة . وذكر مقاتل

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r8.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r8.claim: Muqātil says the verse was revealed about Nabhān the date seller, who tried to seduce a customer; she refused, and he confessed to the Prophet, who asked if her husband was on campaign.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r8.anchor: وذكر مقاتل بن سليمان أن هذه الآية نزلت في رجل كان يسمى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r9.claim: Creating people from the earth means creating Adam.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r9.anchor: يعني أنشأ آدم . { وإذ أنتم أجنة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r10.speaker: مكحول
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r10.claim: Makḥūl reminds hearers that people die as fetuses, youths, adults, and elders, asking what more they await.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r10.anchor: قال مكحول : في بطون أمهاتنا فسقط منا من سقط ، وكنا فيمن بقي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r11.speaker: ابن شوذب
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r11.claim: Ibn Shūdhhab says not to praise yourselves.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r11.anchor: يعني لا تمادحوا ، قاله ابن شوذب

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r12.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r12.claim: Ibn Jurayj says not to commit sins while claiming obedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r12.anchor: لا تعملوا بالمعاصي وتقولوا نعمل بالطاعة ، قاله ابن جريج

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r13.claim: Another view forbids saying ‘I did such-and-such’ after doing good.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r13.anchor: إذا عملت خيرا فلا تقل عملت كذا وكذا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r14.claim: Al-Māwardī also allows ‘do not exchange ugliness for good or vice for virtue.’
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r14.anchor: لا تبادلوا قبحكم حسنا ومنكركم معروفا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r15.claim: He further allows a prohibition on showing off to appear pure.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r15.anchor: لا تراؤوا بعملكم المخلوقين لتكونوا عندهم أزكياء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r16.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r16.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God knows every soul’s deeds and destination.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p401/r16.anchor: قد علم الله كل نفس ما هي عاملة وما هي صانعة وإلى ما هي صائرة

MUJAHID:v2p631#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p631#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
MUJAHID:v2p631#2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan glosses lapses as a passing thought of fornication or drinking wine followed by repentance.
MUJAHID:v2p631#2/r1.anchor: قال حدثنا عقبة الأصم قال سمعت الحسن يقول ﴿ اللمم ﴾ الخطرة من الزنا والخطرة من شرب الخمر ثم يتوب

MUJAHID:v2p631#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p631#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p631#2/r2.claim: Mujahid links God's knowing people from their creation to the statement that He knows best who is guided.
MUJAHID:v2p631#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ هو أعلم بكم إذ أنشأكم من الأرض ﴾ قال هو كقوله ﴿ وهو أعلم بالمهتدين ﴾

MUQATIL:53:32/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:32/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:32/r1.claim: Major sins are any sins whose punishment ends in the Fire.

MUQATIL:53:32/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:32/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:32/r2.claim: The enormities are sins that incur a prescribed legal punishment.

MUQATIL:53:32/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:32/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:32/r3.claim: Lamam means sins between those punishable by the Fire and those incurring a fixed penalty.
MUQATIL:53:32/r3.anchor: يعني كل ذنب يختم بالنار { والفواحش } يعني كل ذنب فيه حد { لا اللمم } يعني ما بين الحدين

MUQATIL:53:32/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:32/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:32/r4.claim: The verse was revealed about date seller Nabhan al-Tammar: he lured a woman into his shop, tried to molest her, struck her backside when she resisted, then regretted it and reported himself to the Prophet.
MUQATIL:53:32/r4.anchor: نزلت في نبهان التمار، وذلك أنه كان له حانوت يبيع فيه التمر، فأتته امرأة تريد تمرا، فقال لها: ادخلى الحانوت

MUQATIL:53:32/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:32/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:53:32/r5.claim: The Prophet warned Nabhan that the woman's husband might be campaigning for God's cause, adding that God has greater protective jealousy for the campaigner than for one at home.
MUQATIL:53:32/r5.anchor: فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ويحك يا نبهان،

MUQATIL:53:32/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:32/r6.speaker: أبو بكر وعمر بن الخطاب
MUQATIL:53:32/r6.claim: After Nabhan told them, Abu Bakr and Umar each repeated that the woman's husband might be campaigning for God's cause.
MUQATIL:53:32/r6.anchor: فلقي أبا بكر، رضي الله عنه، فأعلمه، فقال: ويحك فلعل زوجها غاز في سبيل الله

MUQATIL:53:32/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:32/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:53:32/r7.claim: Umar brought Nabhan to the Prophet and demanded his execution; the Prophet laughed and told Umar to release him.
MUQATIL:53:32/r7.anchor: فضحك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال: " أرسله يا عمر " ،

MUQATIL:53:32/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:32/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:32/r8.claim: The particular lamam was Nabhan's striking the woman's backside with his hand; God is vast in forgiveness for whoever repents.
MUQATIL:53:32/r8.anchor: يعني ضربه عجزيتها بيده { إن ربك واسع المغفرة } لمن تاب

MUQATIL:53:32/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:32/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:32/r9.claim: God knows people better than anyone else because he created them from earth and knew them as embryos in their mothers' wombs.
MUQATIL:53:32/r9.anchor: من غيره { إذ أنشأكم من الأرض } يعني خلقكم من تراب { و } هو أعلم بكم { وإذ أنتم أجنة في بطون أمهاتكم }

MUQATIL:53:32/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:32/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:32/r10.claim: Some Muslims claimed merit by saying they had prayed and performed good deeds; God forbids self-praise because he knows best who is pious.
MUQATIL:53:32/r10.anchor: قال: وقال ناس من المسلمين: صلينا وفعلنا فزكوا أنفسهم، فقال الله تعالى: { فلا تزكوا أنفسكم هو أعلم بمن اتقى } [آية: 32]

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r1.claim: “Those who” is an appositive, or nominative as a phrase of praise: “they are those who.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r1.anchor: بدل أوفى موضع رفع على المدح اى هم الذين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r2.claim: Major sins are the grave members of the genus of sin, which includes both major and minor sins; they are sins whose punishment is great.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r2.anchor: اى الكبائر من الاثم لان الاثم جنس يشتمل على كبائرر وصغائر والكبائر لاذنوب التى يكبر عقابها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r3.speaker: حمزة وعلى
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r3.claim: Hamza and ʿAlī read the phrase in the singular, “the major kind of sin.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r3.anchor: كبير حمزة وعلى اى النوع الكبير منه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r4.claim: Fawāḥish are more heinous than major sins and are a particular subset of them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r4.anchor: ﴿ والفواحش ﴾ افحس من الكبائر انه قال والفواحش منها خاصة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r5.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r5.claim: One reported distinction calls major sins those threatened with Hellfire and fawāḥish those for which a legal ḥadd is prescribed.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r5.anchor: قيل الكبائر ما اوعد الله عليه النار والفواحس ما شرع فيها الحد

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r6.claim: Al-lamam means minor sins; the exception is disconnected because minor sins are not part of major sins or fawāḥish.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r6.anchor: اى الصغائر والاستثناء منقطع لانه ليس من اكبائر والفواحش

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r7.claim: Examples of al-lamam include a glance, a remark, a touch, and a gesture.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r8.claim: God's forgiveness is vast: He forgives whatever sins He wills even without repentance.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r8.anchor: فيغفر ما شاء من الذنوب من غي توبة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r9.claim: God knew people when He created their father Adam from earth and when they were embryos in their mothers, before they emerged from Adam's loins or their mothers' wombs.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r9.anchor: قبل ان يخرجكم من صلب آدم عليه السلام وقبل ان تخرجوا منبطون امهاتكم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r10.claim: Do not claim purity of deeds, abundant good works, or freedom from sins, and do not praise yourselves; humble yourselves, since God knew the pure and pious before you existed.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r10.anchor: فلا تنسبوها إلى زكاء العمل وزيادة الخير والطاعات أو إلى الزكاة والطهارة من المعاصى ولا تثنوا عليها واهضموها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r11.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r11.claim: The verse was revealed about people who performed good deeds and then boasted, “our prayers, fasting, and pilgrimage.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r11.anchor: وقيل كان نهاس يعملون اعمالا حسنة ثم يقولون صلاتنا وصيامنا وحجنا فنزلت

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r12.claim: Self-praise is forbidden when it expresses vanity or ostentation; mentioning obedience is allowed as gratitude, since rejoicing in obedience is itself obedience.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r12.anchor: وهذا اذا كان على سبيل الاعجاب أو الرياء لاعلى سبيل الاعتراف بالنعمة فانه جائز

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r13.claim: Let God's knowledge suffice instead of people's knowledge, and His reward instead of their praise.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191/r13.anchor: فاكتفوا بعلمه عن علم الناس وبجزائه عن ثناء الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r4.claim: Those who avoid major sins and indecencies describe the people who do good.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r4.anchor: هذا نعت للمحسنين أي هم لا يرتكبون كبائر الإثم

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r5.claim: Al-Qurtubi identifies the greatest sin, shirk, as the intended major sin.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r6.speaker: الأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب وحمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r6.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read the singular kabīr; Ibn Abbas explains that form as shirk.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r6.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب وحمزة والكسائي «كبير» على التوحيد وفسره ابن عباس بالشرك.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r7.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r7.claim: Muqatil says major sins are any sins whose punishment ends in the Fire, while indecencies are any sins carrying a prescribed legal penalty.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل: { كبائر الإثم } كل ذنب ختم بالنار. { والفواحش } كل ذنب فيه الحد.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi also identifies indecencies with zina.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r8.anchor: { والفواحش } الزنى: وقال مقاتل: { كبائر الإثم }

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r9.claim: The exception of lamam is disconnected and refers to minor sins, which no one avoids completely except those God protects.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r9.anchor: ثم استثنى استثناء منقطعا وهي: المسألة الثانية: فقال: { إلا اللمم } وهي الصغائر

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة وابن عباس والشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r10.claim: Abu Hurayra, Ibn Abbas, and al-Shaʿbi interpret lamam as everything short of zina.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r10.anchor: فقال أبو هريرة وابن عباس والشعبي: «اللمم» كل ما دون الزنى.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r11.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r11.claim: Muqatil ibn Sulayman reports the occasion: date-seller Nibhan lured a customer into his shop and solicited her; she refused, and he confessed to the Prophet, who asked whether her husband might be away campaigning; the verse then came down.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32/r11.anchor: وذكر مقاتل بن سليمان: " أن هذه الآية نزلت في رجل كان يسمى نبهان التمار

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو سعيد الخدري وحذيفة ومسروق
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r1.claim: Ibn Masud, Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, Hudhayfa, and Masruq say lamam is what falls short of intercourse: kissing, touching, looking, or lying together.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r1.anchor: وكذا قال ابن مسعود وأبو سعيد الخدري وحذيفة ومسروق: إن اللمم ما دون الوطء

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r2.speaker: مسروق عن عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r2.claim: Masruq transmits Ibn Masud's account that the eyes' zina is looking, the hands' is touching, and the feet's is walking; the genitals confirm or disprove it, making it full zina if consummated and lamam otherwise.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r2.anchor: وروى مسروق عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: زنى العينين النظر، وزنى اليدين البطش

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r3.claim: In Bukhari and Muslim, Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet's teaching that each person inevitably has a share of zina: the eyes look, the tongue speaks, the soul desires, and the genitals confirm or deny it.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r3.anchor: وفي صحيح البخاري ومسلم عن ابن عباس قال: ما رأيت شيئا أشبه باللمم مما قال أبو هريرة

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r4.claim: The complete, punishable zina is the act of the genitals; other bodily parts have their own share of sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r4.anchor: والمعنى: أن الفاحشة العظيمة والزنى التام الموجب للحد في الدنيا والعقوبة في الآخرة هو في الفرج

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r5.speaker: أبو صالح عن أبي هريرة عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r5.claim: A Muslim report adds that the ears' zina is listening, the heart desires, and the other limbs' zina is speech, touch, or walking, with the genitals confirming or denying it.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r5.anchor: وفي رواية أبي صالح عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r6.speaker: طاووس عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r6.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi cites a report from Tawus from Ibn Abbas that adds the lips' zina as kissing.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r6.anchor: وقد ذكر الثعلبي حديث طاوس عن ابن عباس فذكر فيه الأذن واليد والرجل، وزاد فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r7.claim: Another interpretation from Ibn Abbas is a person who slips into a sin and then repents; he cites the verse about God forgiving abundantly.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس أيضا: هو الرجل يلم بذنب ثم يتوب.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r8.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r8.claim: Al-Nahhas calls the Ibn Abbas interpretation of a sin followed by repentance the soundest and best-attested view.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r8.anchor: قال النحاس: هذا أصح ما قيل فيه وأجلها إسنادا.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد والحسن والزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r9.claim: Mujahid, al-Hasan, and al-Zuhri say lamam is a sin committed once and not repeated; al-Zuhri gives zina, theft, and drinking wine followed by repentance as examples.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#2/r9.anchor: عن الزهري، قال: اللمم أن يزني ثم يتوب فلا يعود، وأن يسرق أو يشرب الخمر

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r3.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As says lamam means anything short of shirk.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r3.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص: اللمم ما دون الشرك.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r4.speaker: ابن زيد وعكرمة والضحاك وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd, Ikrima, al-Dahhak, and Qatada define lamam as a sin with no worldly hadd and no threatened afterlife punishment, expiated by the five daily prayers; al-Awfi and al-Hakam transmit this from Ibn Abbas.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r4.anchor: قاله ابن زيد وعكرمة والضحاك وقتادة. ورواه العوفي والحكم بن عتيبة عن ابن عباس.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r5.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi gives two senses: a minor sin with no hadd or afterlife threat, expiated by the five prayers while short of major sins, or a grave sin repeatedly committed and then repented from.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r5.anchor: وقال الكلبي: اللمم على وجهين: كل ذنب لم يذكر الله عليه حدا في الدنيا ولا عذابا في الآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو هريرة وزيد بن ثابت
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayra, and Zayd ibn Thabit say lamam means deeds from before Islam, which are not charged against converts; polytheists taunted Muslims that they had done such things before, prompting the verse. Zayd ibn Aslam and his son agree.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا وأبي هريرة وزيد بن ثابت: هو ما سلف في الجاهلية فلا يؤاخذهم به.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r7.claim: The pre-Islam interpretation is compared with the rule allowing what preceded the prohibition on marrying two sisters to stand.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r7.anchor:
وهو كقوله تعالى:
وأن تجمعوا بين الأختين إلا ما قد سلف
[النساء: 23].

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r8.speaker: نفطويه
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r8.claim: Niftawayh says lamam is an occasional rather than habitual sin, since Arabs say someone visits only now and then; he rejects mere intention without action because the phrase for visiting requires that one actually came.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r8.anchor: وقيل: اللمم هو أن يأتي بذنب لم يكن له بعادة قاله نفطويه.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r9.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r9.claim: Al-Farraʾ rejects interpreting lamam as merely intending without acting, since the Arabic phrase “he visited us” describes an act rather than an unfulfilled intention.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r9.anchor: قال: ولا يكون أن يلم ولا يفعل، لأن العرب لا تقول ألم بنا إلا إذا فعل الإنسان

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r10.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r10.claim: Al-Jawhari defines lamam as minor sins and also records the sense of approaching a sin without committing it.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r10.anchor: وفي الصحاح: وألم الرجل من اللمم وهو صغائر الذنوب، ويقال: هو مقاربة المعصية

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r11.claim: An unattributed verse using alimmam before the caravan departs is cited to illustrate the sense of drawing near.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r11.anchor:
وأنشد غير الجوهري:
بزينب ألمم قبل أن يرحل الركب

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r12.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r12.claim: Ata ibn Abi Rabah says lamam is a habit of the self that occurs from time to time.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r12.anchor: وقال عطاء بن أبي رباح: اللمم عادة النفس الحين بعد الحين.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r13.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r13.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says lamam is what merely crosses the heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r13.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب: هو ما ألم على القلب أي خطر.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r14.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r14.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya says anything one intends, good or bad, is lamam, supported by the report that Satan and the angel each have a prompting.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#3/r14.anchor: وقال محمد بن الحنفية: كل ما هممت به من خير أو شر فهو لمم.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r1.claim: A prophetic report says that Satan has a prompting and the angel has a prompting.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi notes that he discussed the prompting report under the verse about Satan promising poverty in al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r2.anchor:
وقد مضى في «البقرة» عند قوله تعالى:
الشيطان يعدكم الفقر
[البقرة: 286].

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r3.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the root implies something done repeatedly but briefly, without deep involvement or persistence; it can mean visiting now and then, and hence a passing apparition of a dream.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r3.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق الزجاج: أصل اللمم والإلمام ما يعمله الإنسان المرة بعد المرة ولا يتعمق فيه ولا يقيم عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r4.speaker: الأعشى
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r4.claim: Al-Aʿsha's line about a vision of Qutayla briefly visiting illustrates the sense of ilmam.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r4.anchor:
قال الأعشى:
ألم خيال من قتيلة بعدما
وهى حبلها من حبلنا فتصرما

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r5.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r5.claim: Some take illa to mean “and,” but al-Farraʾ rejects this and construes lamam as sins approaching the category of minor offenses.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r5.anchor: وقيل: إلا بمعنى الواو. وأنكر هذا الفراء وقال: المعنى إلا المتقارب من صغار الذنوب.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r6.claim: Al-Qurtubi rejects lamam as a merely accidental glance: such a glance is excused from the outset because it occurs without intent or choice.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r6.anchor: وقيل: اللمم النظرة التي تكون فجأة. قلت: هذا فيه بعد إذ هو معفو عنه ابتداء غير مؤاخذ به
