QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r7.claim: Lamam can also mean a touch of madness, a person afflicted with it, or a slight touch from jinn; a verse compares it to a dreamer's imagined word.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r7.anchor: واللمم أيضا طرف من الجنون، ورجل ملموم أي به لمم.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says God's forgiveness is vast for anyone who repents of sin and seeks forgiveness.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r8.anchor: لمن تاب من ذنبه واستغفر قاله ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r9.speaker: أبو ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r9.claim: Abu Maysara dreamed of domes in Paradise for Dhu al-Kala and Hawshab, who had killed one another; he was told they met God and found Him vast in forgiveness.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r9.anchor: وقال أبو ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل وكان من أفاضل أصحاب ابن مسعود: رأيت في المنام كأني دخلت الجنة فإذا قباب مضروبة

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r10.speaker: أبو خالد
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r10.claim: Abu Khalid says he heard that Dhu al-Kala freed twelve thousand girls.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r10.anchor: فقال أبو خالد: بلغني أن ذا الكلاع أعتق اثني عشر ألف بنت.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r11.claim: God knows people better than they know themselves; “He created you from the earth” refers to their father Adam, created from clay, though the wording addresses descendants in the plural.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r11.anchor: يعني أباكم آدم من الطين وخرج اللفظ على الجمع

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r12.speaker: الترمذي أبو عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r12.claim: Al-Tirmidhi Abu Abdullah rejects an Adam-only reading: creation happened in the shared soil raised from earth, from which waters and essences entered loins and were later extracted in differing forms, colors, and degrees of brightness.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#4/r12.anchor: الترمذي أبو عبد الله: وليس هو كذلك عندنا

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r1.claim: A report says the first and later generations were shown before the Prophet's room, including those still in men's loins and mothers' wombs, represented in clay; he recognized them as Adam had learned the names.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r1.anchor: عرض علي الأولون والآخرون بين يدي حجرتي هذه الليلة

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi recalls the statement at the opening of al-Anʿam that each person is created from the soil of the place where he will be buried.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r2.anchor: قلت: وقد تقدم في أول «الأنعام» أن كل إنسان يخلق من طين البقعة التي يدفن فيها.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r3.claim: Ajnna is the plural of janin, a child while in the womb; the name derives from being concealed and covered.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r3.anchor: جمع جنين وهو الولد ما دام في البطن، سمي جنينا لاجتنانه واستتاره.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r4.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r4.claim: Amr ibn Kulthum's verse describing a child not yet known as a fetus is cited as linguistic evidence for janin.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r4.anchor:
قال عمرو بن كلثوم:
هجان اللون لم تقرأ جنينا

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r5.speaker: مكحول
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r5.claim: Mak-hul reflects that people survive successive stages—fetus, infant, youth, and elder—while many die at each stage, asking what remains to await in old age.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r5.anchor: وقال مكحول: كنا أجنة في بطون أمهاتنا فسقط منا من سقط وكنا فيمن بقي

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r6.speaker: ثابت بن الحارث الأنصاري عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r6.claim: Thabit ibn al-Harith reports that Jews called a dead infant a ṣiddiq; the Prophet said they lied, since every soul created in the womb is destined either blessed or wretched, and this verse was revealed. A similar report comes from Aisha.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r6.anchor:
وروى ابن لهيعة عن الحرث بن يزيد عن ثابت بن الحرث الأنصاري قال:
" كانت اليهود تقول إذا هلك لهم صبي صغير: هو صديق

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r7.claim: Do not praise or commend yourselves: this keeps one farther from ostentation and nearer to humility.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r7.anchor:
فلا تزكوا أنفسكم
[النجم: 32] أي لا تمدحوها ولا تثنوا عليها

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r8.speaker: الحسن وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r8.claim: Al-Hasan and others explain the one who is mindful as one who makes deeds sincere and fears God's punishment; God knows each soul's deeds and final destination.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r8.anchor: أي أخلص العمل واتقى عقوبة الله عن الحسن وغيره.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r9.claim: Al-Qurtubi refers readers to the discussion of self-purification at the verse about people who praise themselves in al-Nisaʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r9.anchor: وقد مضى في «النساء» الكلام في معنى هذه الآية عند قوله تعالى: { ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم }

QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says he would declare no one in this community purified except the Messenger of God.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:31-32#5/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ما من أحد من هذه الأمة أزكيه غير رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم.

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r1.claim: الذين is most likely بدل of الذين أحسنوا: God recompenses evil-doers and good-doers, and the good-doers are those who avoid major sins and receive the best reward.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r1.anchor: الذين يحتمل أن يكون بدلا عن الذين أحسنوا وهو الظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r2.claim: On this reading, the good-doer does not benefit God; avoiding evil defines the praised good-doer, while one who commits major sins is an evil-doer.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r2.anchor: ويتبين به أن المحسن ليس ينفع الله بإحسانه شيئا وهو الذي لا يسيء

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r3.claim: Someone performing voluntary devotions exceeds the defined rank of muḥsin; since God promises muḥsins an increase, those above them receive multiplied rewards.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r3.anchor: فالذي يأتي بالنوافل يكون فوق المحسن

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, this begins a new sentence: God forgives those who avoid major sins, as the following statement about His ample forgiveness indicates.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ابتداء كلام تقديره الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم يغفر الله لهم

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r5.claim: On the new-sentence reading, the passage distinguishes wrongdoers, good-doers, and people who neither sinned nor performed good deeds, such as children not yet accountable; their reward is below the best reward.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r5.anchor: وحال من لم يحسن ولم يسيء وهم الذين لم يرتكبوا سيئة وإن لم تصدر منهم الحسنات

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r6.claim: The present tense denotes a settled habit of avoiding sins, rather than someone who avoided them once but later returned to them, as in saying that habitual visitors asked and were given.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r6.anchor: أي الذين عادتهم ودأبهم الاجتناب لا الذين اجتنبوا مرة وقدموا عليها أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r7.claim: The present tense for avoiding sins stresses repeated, continuing restraint because sins have many kinds; 42:37 likewise uses it for avoiding major sins.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r7.anchor: فإن قيل : في كثير من المواضع قال في الكبائر { والذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r8.claim: By contrast, 39:17 uses the past for avoiding idols: repudiating idolatrous belief is lasting and unitary, whereas particular sins fluctuate and require renewed avoidance.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#2/r8.anchor: وقال في عباد الطاغوت : { والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أن يعبدوها وأنابوا إلى الله }

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r1.claim: كبائر is a feminine adjective whose implied noun is sinful acts: “the great acts of sin.”
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r1.anchor: نقول : هي صفة الفعلة كأنه يقول : الفعلات الكبائر من الإثم

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r2.claim: Good deeds cannot be great beside the gratitude owed for God's countless favors; a servant's sin is weighty, though God forgives and lightens some sins.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r2.anchor: الحسنة لا تكون كبيرة لأنها إذا قوبلت بما يجب أن يوجد من العبد في مقابلة نعم الله

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r3.claim: كبائر marks the magnitude of a sin, while فواحش marks the conspicuous degree of its ugliness: quantity versus quality.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r3.anchor: الكبائر إشارة إلى ما فيها من مقدار السيئة ، والفواحش إشارة

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r4.claim: In Arabic, فاحش is manifestly repugnant; Rāzī adduces the root's permutations and the usage فحشت الناقة for a camel's conspicuous posture while urinating.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r4.anchor: والفاحش في اللغة مختص بالقبيح الخارج قبحه عن حد الخفاء

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r5.claim: كبائر needs the qualifier الإثم to identify what is great; فواحش already conveys ugliness, so the verse does not add “of sin” to it.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r5.anchor: ولهذا لم يقل : الفواحش من الإثم وقال في الكبائر : { كبائر الإثم }

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r6.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r6.claim: One definition makes major sins those for which God explicitly and plainly threatens hell, and obscenities those carrying a worldly prescribed penalty.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r6.anchor: فقيل : الكبائر ما أوعد الله عليه بالنار

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r7.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r7.claim: Another definition says major sins are those whose permissibility would make the person who deems them lawful an unbeliever.

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r8.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r8.claim: The Muʿtazilite definition is that a major sin is not forgiven for its perpetrator until repentance.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r8.anchor: وقيل : الكبائر مالا يغفر الله لفاعله إلا بعد التوبة وهو على مذهب المعتزلة

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r9.claim: Rāzī rejects these definitions as explaining an unclear term with an equally or more obscure one; he instead defines major by magnitude and obscene by quality.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r9.anchor: كل هذه التعريفات تعريف الشيء بما هو مثله في الخفاء أو فوقه

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r10.claim: In principle every disobedience is major relative to God's immense favors; God exempts error and forgetfulness because they do not indicate disregard for reverence, given their prevalence or frequent occurrence.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r10.anchor: إن الأصل في كل معصية أن تكون كبيرة ، لأن نعم الله كثيرة

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r11.claim: An occasional lie or slander, a glance, or an ambiguous offense may be treated as minor because few people in any era avoid such acts altogether.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r11.anchor: كالكذبة والغيبة مرة أو مرتين والنظرة والقبائح التي فيها شبهة

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r12.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r12.claim: Rāzī's companions say listening to music with string instruments makes one openly sinful, while listening in a town whose people do not take the matter seriously does not.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r12.anchor: قال أصحابنا : إن استماع الغناء الذي مع الأوتار يفسق به

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r13.claim: A sin is minor when sensible people in its context do not judge its agent to have abandoned proper reverence; that standard varies with time and person.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r13.anchor: إن العقلاء إن لم يعدوه تاركا للتعظيم لا يكون مرتكبا للكبيرة

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r14.claim: The same pastime can be major for a pious scholar who chases women or plays excessively, but not for a peddler, seller, or otherwise idle person; playing during prayer time differs from other times.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r14.anchor: تختلف الأمور باختلاف الأوقات والأشخاص فالعالم المتقي إذا كان يتبع النساء

RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r15.claim: Rāzī concludes that every sin is major except what the accountable person knows or reasonably supposes God has excluded through grace and pardon.
RAZI-FULL:v29p7#3/r15.anchor: كل ذنب كبيرة إلا ما علم المكلف أو ظن خروجه بفضل الله وعفوه عن الكبائر

RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r1.claim: One view reads اللمم as an intention the believer forms but does not carry out, linking the word to gathering or collecting resolve.
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r1.anchor: ما يقصده المؤمن ولا يحققه وهو على هذا القول من لم يلم إذا جمع

RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r2.claim: A second view makes اللمم a sin the believer commits and immediately regrets, like a passing touch of madness; 3:135 supports this through its account of remembering God and seeking forgiveness.
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r2.anchor: ما يأتي به المؤمن ويندم في الحال وهو من اللمم الذي هو مس من الجنون

RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r3.claim: A third view takes اللمم as a minor sin, from ألم meaning to alight briefly; ألم بالطعام can mean eating only a little.
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r3.anchor: اللمم الصغير من الذنب من ألم إذا نزل نزولا من غير لبث طويل

RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r4.claim: If إلا is an exception from الفواحش, it may be disconnected because اللمم is not itself an obscenity.
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r4.anchor: استثناء منقطع لأن اللمم ليس من الفواحش

RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r5.claim: The exception may instead be connected: relative to what is due to God, every sin is major and obscene, but God exempts some offenses and promises to pardon them.
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r5.anchor: غير منقطع لما بينا أن كل معصية إذا نظرت إلى جانب الله تعالى وما يجب أن يكون عليه فهي كبيرة وفاحشة

RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r6.claim: إلا may mean غير, making the phrase “obscenities other than اللمم”; the force differs according to whether غير distinguishes a class or merely emphasizes and clarifies.
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r6.anchor: ثانيها : { إلا } بمعنى غير وتقديره والفواحش غير اللمم

RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r7.claim: A further parse makes the exception attach to the implied action in يجتنبون: they avoid sins except for approaching them without actually committing them, which is اللمم.
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r7.anchor: وثالثها : هو استثناء من الفعل الذي يدل عليه قوله تعالى : { الذين يجتنبون }

RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r8.claim: Ample forgiveness fits both readings: good-doers are rewarded, avoiders of major sins are forgiven minor ones, and major sinners who repent are forgiven; persistent wrongdoers remain outside forgiveness.
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r8.anchor: المحسن مجزى وذنبه مغفور ، ومجتنب الكبائر كذلك ذنبه الصغير مغفور

RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r9.claim: God's withholding forgiveness from persistent wrongdoers reflects His will, not any limit in its capacity: He could forgive everyone who does good and evil.
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r9.anchor: بين أن ذلك ليس لضيق فيها ، بل ذلك بمشيئة الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r10.claim: مغفرة means covering; measured against God's blessings, every creature falls short, so each needs its deeds covered, even one who repays an unstinting benefactor only a dirham or less.
RAZI-FULL:v29p8/r10.anchor: والمغفرة من الستر ، وهو لا يكون إلا على قبيح ، وكل من خلقه الله

RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r1.claim: The statement that God knows people from their creation may reinforce 53:30: secret nighttime acts are no more hidden than the conditions of embryos in their mothers' wombs.
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r1.anchor: أحدها : هو تقرير لما مر من قوله : { هو أعلم بمن ضل }

RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r2.claim: Another explanation links guidance and misguidance to divine decree: God knew their states in the wombs and wrote some as misguided and others as guided.
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r2.anchor: ثانيها : هو إشارة إلى الضال والمهتدي حصلا على ما هما عليه بتقدير الله

RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r3.claim: A third explanation connects the verse to recompense in 53:31: God can reassemble each person's scattered bodily parts correctly because He knows them as He created them.
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r3.anchor: ثالثها : تأكيد وبيان للجزاء ، وذلك لأنه لما قال : { ليجزى الذين أساءوا بما عملوا }

RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r4.claim: إذ may be governed by the implied meaning of أعلم: God knew you at the time of your creation.
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r4.anchor: العامل في : { إذ } يحتمل أن يكون ما يدل عليه : { أعلم }

RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r5.claim: Alternatively, إذ is governed by an implied اذكروا: the completed statement says God knows you, then tells doubters to recall their creation from earth.
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r5.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون اذكروا فيكون تقريرا لكونه عالما

RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r6.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r6.claim: Some take “He created you from the earth” as referring to Adam, who was made from soil.
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r6.anchor: من الناس من قال آدم فإنه من تراب

RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r7.claim: Rāzī says every person originates from earth: earth becomes nourishment and then semen.
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r7.anchor: وقررنا أن كل أحد أصله من التراب ، فإنه يصير غذاء ، ثم يصير نطفة

RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r8.claim: A hypothetical objection says the first creation clause must concern Adam, since the embryo clause concerns other people; making both clauses about everyone would imply that all were embryos in wombs, attributed here to philosophers.
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r8.anchor: لو قال قائل : لا بد من صرف { إذ أنشأكم من الأرض } إلى آدم ، لأن { وإذ أنتم أجنة

RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r9.claim: Rāzī answers that the address concerns those present when spoken; whether it extends to all after the revelation or only its contemporaries, all are from earth and were embryos.
RAZI-FULL:v29p9/r9.anchor: ولا شك أن كل هؤلاء من الأرض وهم كانوا أجنة

RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r1.claim: Although a fetus is already understood to be in the womb, the phrase highlights God's perfect knowledge and power: knowledge of a fetus in deep darkness means no public human condition escapes Him.
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r1.anchor: فإن بطن الأم في غاية الظلمة

RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r2.claim: If God's knowing people means knowing who has gone astray, the command not to claim purity follows directly from that knowledge.

RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r3.claim: If God's knowledge instead confirms resurrection, believers must not plead that scattered bodily particles prevent punishment; the One who knew them at creation knows them at return, restores the pious person's parts, and rewards him.

RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r4.claim: One possible addressee is the unbelievers who had questioned how God could know them; this statement answers their objection.
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r4.anchor: وهذا على قولنا إنهم قالوا كيف يعلمه الله

RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r5.claim: A second possible addressee is everyone, believers and unbelievers, both at the time of address and afterward.
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r5.anchor: كل من كان زمان الخطاب وبعده من المؤمنين والكفار

RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r6.claim: Addressing believers after the order to turn away from those who reject the reminder, God tells them not to proclaim themselves right and the polytheists wrong; He knows who is pious and who transgresses. Razi says the claim that the earlier order was abrogated is more apparent on this reading.
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r6.anchor: قد علم كونك ومن معك على الحق

RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r7.claim: Another reading treats the verse as guidance to believers: avoid ostentatious self-praise and claims of being better, purer, or more pious, since judgment belongs to God, who has known their whole lives.

RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p10/r8.claim: The verse also warns believers against certainty about their final salvation: God knows who will prove pious at the end, supporting the formula I am a believer, God willing.

STUDYQURAN:53:32/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r1.claim: Islamic tradition has no agreed definition of grave sins and preserves many different lists.
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r1.anchor: there is no agreement on a single definition and there are many different lists of “grave sins”

STUDYQURAN:53:32/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r2.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r2.claim: Some define grave sins as offenses whose retribution is removed only through repentance.
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r2.anchor: Some define grave sins as “sins for which the retribution is not removed except

STUDYQURAN:53:32/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r3.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r3.claim: Fawāḥish can mean fornication or, more generally, especially atrocious grave sins.
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r3.anchor: Indecencies translates fawāḥish, which is often equated with fornication or, more generally, with grave sins that are considered particularly atrocious (Z)

STUDYQURAN:53:32/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r4.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r4.claim: Most understand slight sins as minor sins from which one repents.
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r4.anchor: Save what is slight is understood by most to mean minor sins from which one repents (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:53:32/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r5.claim: A hadith cited by many commentators says people have a share of fornication through looking, speech, desire, and whether sexual activity occurs.
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r5.anchor: The fornication of the eye is by looking, the fornication of the tongue is by talking; the heart wishes and lusts

STUDYQURAN:53:32/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r6.speaker: Ibn Masʿūd
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says eyes, lips, hands, and feet commit lesser forms of zina; intercourse makes one a fornicator, otherwise it is slight sin.
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r6.anchor: Ibn Masʿūd is reported to have said, “The eyes fornicate by looking, the lips by kissing, the hands by transgressing

STUDYQURAN:53:32/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r7.claim: Even minor sins, though more readily forgiven, should be avoided because of what they may lead to.
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r7.anchor: one must still avoid them and be wary of what they may lead to

STUDYQURAN:53:32/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r8.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r8.claim: God forgives small sins by keeping one from grave sins and forgives grave sins through repentance.
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r8.anchor: Your Lord is of vast forgiveness in that He forgives small sins by keeping one

STUDYQURAN:53:32/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r9.speaker: al-Baghawī
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r9.claim: Al-Baghawī says this phrase may follow praise of the virtuous to keep less virtuous or grave sinners from despairing of God’s Mercy.

STUDYQURAN:53:32/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r10.speaker: JJ, Q
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r10.claim: Being brought forth from the earth refers to God’s creation of Adam from dust.
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r10.anchor: Brought you forth from the earth is understood as a reference to God’s creation of Adam from dust (JJ, Q)

STUDYQURAN:53:32/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r11.speaker: Bḍ, IK, Q
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r11.claim: God knows every person before birth, from when humanity was in Adam’s loins.
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r11.anchor: the loins of Adam(Bḍ, IK, Q; see 7:172)

STUDYQURAN:53:32/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r12.claim: Since only God knows who is truly pure, people should not congratulate themselves for pious deeds.
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r12.anchor: Thus people should not think well of themselves for performing pious deeds

STUDYQURAN:53:32/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r13.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r13.claim: Pious deeds themselves come only through God’s support.
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r13.anchor: the deeds themselves only come through God’s support (Z), as in 4:49

STUDYQURAN:53:32/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r14.speaker: The Prophet
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r14.claim: The Prophet warns against crediting companions’ good deeds to them, saying such praise cuts off a companion’s neck.
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r14.anchor: The Prophet even enjoined his followers not to ascribe good deeds to their companions, but only to God, saying several times, “Woe to you!

STUDYQURAN:53:32/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r15.claim: The recommended praise says one thinks a friend has certain qualities, leaves knowledge of him to God, and declares no one pure before God.
STUDYQURAN:53:32/r15.anchor: let him say, ‘I think that so-and-so is this and that; God knows best about him, and I would never declare anyone pure before God,’

QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r7.claim: All sins are grave because they oppose God's command, though some are greater than others; nothing is greater than associating partners with God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r7.anchor: الذنوب كلها كبائر لأنها مخالفة لأمر الله ، ولكن بعضها أكبر من بعض . ولا شيء أعظم من الشرك

QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r8.claim: He glosses al-fawāḥish as sins or acts of disobedience.

QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r9.speaker: تكلموا فيه وقالوا
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r9.claim: One reported view makes the exception disconnected: lammam is neither sin nor part of the indecencies.
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r9.anchor: تكلموا فيه ، وقالوا : إنه استثناء منقطع ، واللمم ليس بإثم ولا من جملة الفواحش

QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r10.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r10.claim: Another view includes lammam among the indecencies but treats it as ambiguous, with God promising to forgive it.
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r10.anchor: ويقال : اللمم من جملة الفواحش ولكن فيها اشتباها - فأخبر أنه يغفرها

QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r11.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r11.claim: A reported definition of lammam is committing the lapse and then abandoning it through repentance.
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r11.anchor: ويقال : اللمم هو أن يأتي المرء ذلك ثم يقلع عنه بالتوبة

QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r12.speaker: بعض السلف
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r12.claim: Some early authorities define lammam as a single occurrence of adultery, wine drinking, theft, or similar sin that the person does not repeat.
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r12.anchor: وقال لعض السلف : هو الوقعة من الزنا تحصل مرة ثم لا يعود إليها ، وكذلك شرب الخمر ، والسرقة

QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r13.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r13.claim: Another view calls lammam the intention to commit a lapse without actually doing it.
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r13.anchor: ويقال : هو أن يهم بالزلة ثم لا يفعلها

QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r14.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r14.claim: Another reported explanation of lammam is looking.

QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r15.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r15.claim: Another view defines lammam as sins that carry no prescribed legal penalty and are expiated by the prayers.
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r15.anchor: ويقال : ما لا حد عليه من المعاصي ، وتكفر عنه الصلوات

QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r16.claim: Qushayrī prefers a disconnected exception: lammam is not among the sins.
QUSHAYRI:v3p250/r16.anchor: والأصح أنه استثناء منقطع وأن اللمم ليس من جملة المعاصي

QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r1.claim: Being created from the earth refers to the creation of Adam.
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r1.anchor: إذ أنشأكم من الأرض } : يغني خلق آدم

QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r2.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r2.claim: Self-praise signals that a person is veiled from God; one absorbed in witnessing the Lord does not praise himself.
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r2.anchor: ويقال : تزكية النفس من علامات كون المرء محجوبا عن الله ؛ لأن المجذوب إلى الغاية والمستغرق في شهود ربه لا يزكي نفسه

QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r3.claim: God knows who is Godfearing better than people know themselves.
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r3.anchor: { هو أعلم بمن اتقى } : لأنه أعلم بكم منكم

QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r4.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r4.claim: A person who believes anyone on earth is worse than himself is arrogant; a Muslim should view every other Muslim as better, imagining elders more obedient and youth less sinful.
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r4.anchor: ويقال : من اعتقد أن على البسيطة أحدا شر منه فهو متكبر . ويقال : المسلم يجب أن يكون بحيث يرى كل مسلم خيرا منه

TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r1.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r1.claim: Some interpreters take illa as a disconnected exception for pre-Islamic sins that God pardoned when people entered Islam.
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r1.anchor: إلا اليعافير وإلا العيس واليعافير: الظباء، والعيس: الإبل وليسا من الناس

TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the exception as whatever had already passed before Islam.
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم} [النجم: 32] يقول: «إلا ما قد سلف»

TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says former polytheists had committed these major sins and indecencies before Islam, and God forgave them when they converted.
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r3.anchor: حدثني يونس قال: أخبرنا ابن وهب قال: قال ابن زيد، في قوله

TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r4.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r4.claim: Asked about the verse, Zayd ibn Thabit answers that God forbids indecencies, both outward and inward.
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r4.anchor: سأل رجل زيد بن ثابت، عن هذه الآية، {الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم} [النجم: 32] فقال: «حرم الله عليك الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن»

TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies the major sin as shirk and indecency as adultery, whose pre-Islamic instances were forgiven upon conversion.
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r5.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم في قول الله: {الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم} [النجم: 32] قال: " كبائر الشرك والفواحش: الزنى

TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r6.speaker: بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r6.claim: Some Arabic-language scholars take illa as a disconnected exception to an implied category: minor slips are excepted although they are not major sins or indecencies, like gazelles and camels excepted from a place with no people.
TAB-FULL:v22p60#2/r6.anchor: إلا اليعافير وإلا العيس واليعافير: الظباء، والعيس: الإبل وليسا من الناس

TAB-FULL:v22p63/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿud calls looks, kisses, grasping, and walking forms of sexual sin; if intercourse confirms them it is zina, otherwise they are lamam.
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r1.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن أبي الضحى، أن ابن مسعود قال: " زنى العينين: النظر، وزنى الشفتين: التقبيل

TAB-FULL:v22p63/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra's Prophetic report says each person has a decreed share of sexual sin: the eyes look, the tongue speaks, the self desires, and the genitals confirm or deny it.
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r2.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن الله كتب على ابن آدم حظه من الزنى أدركه ذلك لا محالة

TAB-FULL:v22p63/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r3.speaker: مسروق
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r3.claim: Masruq says an act is zina if intercourse comes first, but lamam if it does not.
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r3.anchor: عن مسروق، في قوله: {إلا اللمم} [النجم: 32] قال: «إن تقدم كان زنى، وإن تأخر كان لمما»

TAB-FULL:v22p63/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r4.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r4.claim: Al-Shaʿbi defines lamam as conduct short of zina and cites Ibn Masʿud's examples of bodily acts short of intercourse.
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r4.anchor: سألت الشعبي، عن قول الله: {يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم} [النجم: 32] قال: هو ما دون الزنى

TAB-FULL:v22p63/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra lists kissing, winking, looking, and touching as lamam, distinguishing intercourse as zina and saying it requires ritual washing.
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r5.anchor: سألت أبا هريرة عن قول الله: {الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم} [النجم: 32] قال: «القبلة، والغمزة، والنظرة، والمباشرة

TAB-FULL:v22p63/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r6.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r6.claim: Another group reads illa as a connected exception: people avoid major sins and indecencies unless they lapse into them and then repent.
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل ذلك استثناء صحيح، ومعنى الكلام: الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم إلا أن يلم بها ثم يتوب

TAB-FULL:v22p63/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains lamam as a person falling into an indecency and then repenting.
TAB-FULL:v22p63/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم} [النجم: 32] قال: «هو الرجل يلم بالفاحشة ثم يتوب»

TAB-FULL:v22p65/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r1.claim: The Prophet is quoted with a poem acknowledging that every servant may slip, offered in connection with lamma.
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r1.anchor:
وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
إن تغفر اللهم تغفر جما …

TAB-FULL:v22p65/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r2.claim: Mujahid says lamma is committing a sin and then abandoning it; he cites the poem that no servant is entirely free of lapses.
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، أنه قال في هذه الآية {إلا اللمم} [النجم: 32] قال: «الذي يلم بالذنب ثم يدعه

TAB-FULL:v22p65/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra, tentatively tracing the report to the Prophet, describes lamma as adultery, theft, or wine drinking followed by repentance and no return.
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أراه رفعه: {الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم}

TAB-FULL:v22p65/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r4.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r4.claim: Al-Hasan defines lamma as adultery, theft, or wine drinking after which the person does not return to the sin.
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r4.anchor: عن عوف، عن الحسن، في قول الله: {الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم}

TAB-FULL:v22p65/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r5.speaker: أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r5.claim: The Companions reportedly described a person committing a small act of adultery or wine drinking secretly, then repenting.
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r5.anchor: أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقولون: هذا الرجل يصيب اللمة من الزنا، واللمة من شرب الخمر

TAB-FULL:v22p65/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says lamma is a sin committed occasionally; when asked about adultery, he says it is adultery followed by repentance.
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {إلا اللمم} [النجم: 32] «يلم بها في الحين»

TAB-FULL:v22p65/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r7.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r7.claim: Al-Hasan also describes lamma broadly as an indecent act from which a person repents.
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r7.anchor: كان الحسن يقول في اللمم: " تكون اللمة من الرجل: الفاحشة ثم يتوب

TAB-FULL:v22p65/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r8.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r8.claim: Abu Salih explains lamma as adultery followed by repentance.
TAB-FULL:v22p65/r8.anchor: عن سفيان، عن إسماعيل، عن أبي صالح قال: «الزنى ثم يتوب»

TAB-FULL:v22p66/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p66/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v22p66/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says lamma is a sin committed once, after which the person stops.
TAB-FULL:v22p66/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، عن الحسن، {إلا اللمم} [النجم: 32] قال: «أن يقع الوقعة ثم ينتهي»

TAB-FULL:v22p66/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p66/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p66/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses lamma as something one does once or occasionally.
TAB-FULL:v22p66/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: اللمم: الذي تلم المرة

TAB-FULL:v22p66/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p66/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
TAB-FULL:v22p66/r3.claim: Ibn Amr says lamma means anything short of associating partners with God.
TAB-FULL:v22p66/r3.anchor: أن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص قال: " اللمم: ما دون الشرك

TAB-FULL:v22p66/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p66/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن القاسم
TAB-FULL:v22p66/r4.claim: Ibn al-Qasim explains lamma as a sin that befalls a person.
TAB-FULL:v22p66/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن القاسم، في قوله: {إلا اللمم} [النجم: 32] قال: «اللمة يلم بها من الذنوب»

TAB-FULL:v22p66/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p66/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p66/r5.claim: Mujahid says lamma is touching a sin and then withdrawing; he reports that pre-Islamic pilgrims recited the poem asking God to forgive lapses.
TAB-FULL:v22p66/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {إلا اللمم} [النجم: 32] قال: «الرجل يلم بالذنب ثم ينزع عنه»

TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r1.speaker: ابن الزبير
TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr defines lamma as what lies between the worldly legal penalty and the punishment of the afterlife.
TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن الزبير، {إلا اللمم} [النجم: 32] قال: «ما بين الحدين، حد الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas defines lamma as sins below both the worldly legal penalty and the afterlife punishment; prayers expiate these sins, while the two limits are a prescribed worldly penalty and a sin assigned to the Fire.
TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم} [النجم: 32] قال: «كل شيء بين الحدين، حد الدنيا وحد الآخرة، تكفره الصلوات

TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r3.claim: Ikrima says lamma is any sin carrying neither a worldly legal penalty nor an afterlife punishment.
TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: {إلا اللمم} [النجم: 32] يقول: «ما بين الحدين، كل ذنب ليس فيه حد في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r4.claim: Qatada says lamma falls short of both the worldly penalty and the punishment in the Fire, unlike an offense requiring a worldly penalty.
TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم} [النجم: 32] واللمم: «ما كان بين الحدين لم يبلغ حد الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r5.claim: An unnamed view reported through Qatada likewise defines lamma as what lies between the two limits, worldly penalty and afterlife punishment.
TAB-FULL:v22p66#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة قال: " قال بعضهم: اللمم: ما بين الحدين

TAB-FULL:v22p68/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas again describes lamma as what lies between the worldly penalty and the punishment of the afterlife.
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، عن ابن عباس قال: " اللمم: ما بين الحدين: حد الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v22p68/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says every sin between the limits of worldly and afterlife punishment is lamma, which God forgives.
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r2.anchor: قال الضحاك {إلا اللمم} [النجم: 32] قال: «كل شيء بين حد الدنيا والآخرة

TAB-FULL:v22p68/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r3.claim: Al-Tabari prefers a disconnected exception: lamma means sins below major sins and below offenses requiring a worldly penalty or afterlife punishment, which God forgives for those avoiding major sins.
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r3.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك عندي بالصواب قول من قال «إلا» بمعنى الاستثناء المنقطع،

TAB-FULL:v22p68/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r4.claim: Al-Tabari compares this promise to the promise that avoiding major sins brings forgiveness for lesser sins and admission to an honored place.
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r4.anchor: وذلك عندي نظير قوله جل ثناؤه: {إن تجتنبوا كبائر ما تنهون عنه نكفر عنكم سيئاتكم وندخلكم مدخلا كريما} [النساء: 31]

TAB-FULL:v22p68/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r5.claim: The Prophet says the eyes, hands, and legs commit forms of adultery, while the genitals confirm or deny them; al-Tabari uses this to mark lesser acts as lamma.
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r5.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «العينان تزنيان، واليدان تزنيان، والرجلان تزنيان، ويصدق ذلك الفرج أو يكذبه»

TAB-FULL:v22p68/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r6.claim: Al-Tabari argues that acts short of penetration incur no legal penalty, supporting his view that lesser sexual misconduct is forgiven lamma.
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r6.anchor: وذلك أنه لا حد فيما دون ولوج الفرج في الفرج، وذلك هو العفو من الله في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v22p68/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r7.claim: Al-Tabari reasons that God is too generous to reinstate punishment for what He has forgiven.
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r7.anchor: والله جل ثناؤه أكرم من أن يعود فيما قد عفا عنه، كما روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم،

TAB-FULL:v22p68/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r8.speaker: الفراء
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r8.claim: Al-Farra explains lamma as approaching something, citing an Arab expression for a blow that nearly kills and usage of alama meaning nearly did.
TAB-FULL:v22p68/r8.anchor: ذكر الفراء أنه سمع العرب تقول: ضربه ما لمم القتل، يريدون ضربا مقاربا للقتل

TAB-FULL:v22p69/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p69/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p69/r1.claim: God's forgiveness is vast for sinners guilty of grave sins and indecencies; He forgives lamma for those who avoid major sins and indecencies.
TAB-FULL:v22p69/r1.anchor: ذنوبهم الفواحش وكبائر الإثم وإنما أعلم جل ثناؤه بقوله هذا عباده أنه يغفر اللمم

TAB-FULL:v22p69/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p69/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p69/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says that God has forgiven them.
TAB-FULL:v22p69/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {إن ربك واسع المغفرة} [النجم: 32] «قد غفر ذلك لهم»

TAB-FULL:v22p70/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p70/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p70/r1.claim: God knows believers from disbelievers, the good from the sinful, and the obedient from the disobedient, both when He created Adam from earth and when people were embryos.
TAB-FULL:v22p70/r1.anchor: تولدوا منكم، وأنفسكم بعدما صرتم رجالا ونساء

TAB-FULL:v22p70/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p70/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p70/r2.claim: Mujahid links God's knowing people at their creation with the statement that He knows those who are rightly guided.
TAB-FULL:v22p70/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {هو أعلم بكم إذ أنشأكم من الأرض} [النجم: 32]

TAB-FULL:v22p70/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p70/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p70/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says God first created Adam from earth and then created people from Adam.
TAB-FULL:v22p70/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {إذ أنشأكم من الأرض} [النجم: 32] قال: «حين خلق آدم من الأرض ثم خلقكم من آدم»

TAB-FULL:v22p71/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p71/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p71/r1.claim: People must not testify that their own souls are pure and free of sins and disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v22p71/r1.anchor: فلا تشهدوا لأنفسكم بأنها زكية بريئة من الذنوب والمعاصي

TAB-FULL:v22p71/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p71/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v22p71/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam glosses the command as not declaring oneself innocent.
TAB-FULL:v22p71/r2.anchor: سمعت زيد بن أسلم، يقول {فلا تزكوا أنفسكم} [النجم: 32] يقول: «فلا تبرئوها»

SULAMI:v2p287#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p287#3/r1.speaker: ذو النون
SULAMI:v2p287#3/r1.claim: Dhu al-Nun says that a knower's mention of indecency is like another person's commission of it.
SULAMI:v2p287#3/r1.anchor: قال ذو النون . ذكر الفاحشة من العارف كفعلها من غيره .

SULAMI:v2p287#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p287#3/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p287#3/r2.claim: God's forgiveness is vast for whoever seeks it and recognizes their own failure to fulfill His commands.
SULAMI:v2p287#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ واسع المغفرة ﴾ لمن استغفره ورأى تقصيره بالقيام بواجب أمره .

SULAMI:v2p287#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p287#3/r3.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p287#3/r3.claim: Ja'far says God knew and decreed each person's felicity or misery before creating them; deeds do not alter the prior decree concerning lifespan, provision, and destiny.
SULAMI:v2p287#3/r3.anchor: قال جعفر : أعلم بكم لأنه خلقكم وقدر عليكم السعادة والشقاء قبل إيجادكم فإنكم ستقبلون في ما جرى عليكم في السبق

SULAMI:v2p287#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p287#3/r4.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p287#3/r4.claim: Abu Uthman says anyone who knows their origin and destination knows they are unfit to praise themselves: the commanding ego sees only the lowliness and deficiency of servitude.
SULAMI:v2p287#3/r4.anchor: قال أبو عثمان رحمة الله عليه : من علم أين هو وإلى أين هو في الوقت علم انه ليس بمحل التزكية

TABATABAI:53:31-32/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r1.claim: The author cites 4:31, which promises expiation of lesser sins for those who avoid major sins.
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r1.anchor: إن تجتنبوا كبائر ما تنهون عنه نكفر عنكم سيئاتكم

TABATABAI:53:31-32/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r2.claim: “Fawāḥish” are repulsive, grave sins; the Qur’an calls adultery and sodomy by this term, and the verse may suggest that these are the major sins.

TABATABAI:53:31-32/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r3.claim: One reported interpretation takes “lamam” as minor sins, making the exception disconnected.

TABATABAI:53:31-32/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r4.claim: Another reported interpretation is intending or approaching a sin without committing it; this too makes the exception disconnected.
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r4.anchor: وقيل هو أن يلم بالمعصية ويقصدها ولا يفعل والاستثناء أيضا منقطع

TABATABAI:53:31-32/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r5.claim: The author favors occasional, nonhabitual sin, which may be minor or major and accords with the description in 3:135 of people who repent and do not persist.
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r5.anchor: وقيل هو المعصية حينا بعد حين من غير عادة أي المعصية على سبيل الاتفاق فيكون أعم من الصغيرة والكبيرة

TABATABAI:53:31-32/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r6.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r6.claim: Reports from the Imams of the Prophet’s household interpret “lamam” according to the third view: sin committed from time to time without habit.
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r6.anchor: وقد فسر في روايات أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام بثالث المعاني

TABATABAI:53:31-32/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r7.claim: This verse explains the preceding description of those who excel: they avoid major sins and indecencies, though an occasional lapse may occur.
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r7.anchor: فهم الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش ومن الجائز أن يقع منهم لمم

TABATABAI:53:31-32/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r8.claim: God’s abundant forgiveness encourages them to repent in hope of pardon.

TABATABAI:53:31-32/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r9.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r9.claim: Al-Rāghib defines “nashʾ” and “nashʾa” as bringing something into being and nurturing it.
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r9.anchor: قال الراغب النشء والنشأة إحداث الشيء وتربيته

TABATABAI:53:31-32/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r10.claim: God’s creating people from earth encompasses their stages from elemental matter to semen and then their entry into the wombs.
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r10.anchor: فإنشاؤهم من الأرض ما جرى عليهم في بدء خلقهم طورا بعد طور من أخذهم من المواد العنصرية إلى أن يتكونوا في صورة المني

TABATABAI:53:31-32/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r11.claim: “Ajnna” is the plural of “janīn”; this clause coordinates with the earlier “when,” stating that God knew them as embryos and knows their reality, inward state, and eventual outcome.

TABATABAI:53:31-32/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r12.claim: Since God has known them from the beginning, they should not claim purity for themselves; He knows best who is truly pious.
TABATABAI:53:31-32/r12.anchor: إذا كان الله أعلم من أول أمر

TABRISI:53:31-32/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-32/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:31-32/r7.claim: Kabāʾir are grave sins; fawāḥish is the plural of fāḥisha and denotes the ugliest and most heinous sins.
TABRISI:53:31-32/r7.anchor: جمع فاحشة وهي أقبح الذنوب وأفحشها

TABRISI:53:31-32/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-32/r8.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:53:31-32/r8.claim: One definition makes a major sin any sin whose warning ends with Hell, and a fahisha any sin carrying a prescribed legal penalty.
TABRISI:53:31-32/r8.anchor: وقد قيل إن الكبيرة كل ذنب ختم بالنار والفاحشة كل ذنب فيه الحد

TABRISI:53:31-32/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-32/r9.speaker: قارئ
TABRISI:53:31-32/r9.claim: The singular reading kabīr al-ithm is used because the following noun is grammatically singular even though plurality is intended.
TABRISI:53:31-32/r9.anchor: ومن قرأ كبير الإثم فلأنه يضاف إلى واحد في اللفظ وإن كان يراد به الكثرة

TABRISI:53:31-32/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-32/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو هريرة والشعبي
TABRISI:53:31-32/r10.claim: Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Hurayra, and al-Sha'bi take lamam as minor sins such as looking or kissing and acts short of adultery.
TABRISI:53:31-32/r10.anchor: فقيل هو صغار الذنوب كالنظر والقبلة وما كان دون الزنا عن ابن مسعود وأبي هريرة والشعبي

TABRISI:53:31-32/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-32/r11.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
TABRISI:53:31-32/r11.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit says lamam refers to sins committed in the pre-Islamic period and forgiven upon entering Islam, making the exception disconnected.
TABRISI:53:31-32/r11.anchor: ما ألموا به في الجاهلية من الإثم فهو معفو عنه في الإسلام عن زيد بن ثابت

TABRISI:53:31-32/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-32/r12.speaker: الحسن والسدي
TABRISI:53:31-32/r12.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Suddi define lamam as committing a sin once, then repenting and not returning to it.
TABRISI:53:31-32/r12.anchor: أن يلم بالذنب مرة ثم يتوب ولا يعود عن الحسن والسدي

TABRISI:53:31-32/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-32/r13.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:53:31-32/r13.claim: Al-Zajjaj's preferred view is that a person has lapsed into a sin but does not persist in it; God's vast forgiveness supports this reading, and Ibn Abbas applies it to the repentant.
TABRISI:53:31-32/r13.anchor: وهو اختيار الزجاج لأنه قال اللمم هو أن يكون الإنسان قد ألم بالمعصية

TABRISI:53:31-32/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-32/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:53:31-32/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas says God's mercy encompasses all sins for the person who commits such a lapse and repents.
TABRISI:53:31-32/r14.anchor: قال ابن عباس لمن فعل ذلك وتاب ومعناه إن رحمته تسع جميع الذنوب

FARRA:v3p99/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p99/r10.speaker: يحيى وأصحاب عبد الله
FARRA:v3p99/r10.claim: Yahya and Abdullah’s companions read كبير الإثم and explained it as shirk.
FARRA:v3p99/r10.anchor: وقوله: يجتنبون كبير الإثم (32) . قرأها يحيى، وأصحاب عبد الله ، وذكروا: أنه الشرك.

FARRA:v3p99/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p99/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p99/r11.claim: اللمم means sins close to the category of minor offenses; Arab speech ضربه ما لمم القتل means beating nearly to death, with ما as an extra particle, and ألم يفعل can mean he almost did it.
FARRA:v3p99/r11.anchor: وقوله: إلا اللمم (32) . يقول: إلا المتقارب من صغير الذنوب، وسمعت العرب تقول: ضربه ما لمم القتل، (ما) صلة

FARRA:v3p99/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p99/r12.speaker: الكلبي
FARRA:v3p99/r12.claim: Al-Kalbi says it is an unintentional glance, forgiven as لمم; looking again is a sin and no longer counts as لمم.
FARRA:v3p99/r12.anchor: وذكر الكلبي بإسناده: أنها النظرة عن غير تعمد، فهي لمم وهي مغفورة، فإن أعاد النظر فليس بلمم هو ذنب

FARRA:v3p100/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p100/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p100/r1.claim: The one created from earth is your father Adam.
FARRA:v3p100/r1.anchor: يريد: أنشأ أباكم آدم من الأرض .

FARRA:v3p100/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p100/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p100/r2.claim: God knows people from beginning to end, so they should not boast of their deeds; He knows who is pious.
FARRA:v3p100/r2.anchor: وقوله: وإذ أنتم أجنة في بطون أمهاتكم (32) . يقول: هو أعلم بكم أولا وآخرا فلا تزكوا أنفسكم

THALABI:v9p150/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p150/r2.claim: God's creating people from the earth refers to creating their father from dust.
THALABI:v9p150/r2.anchor: هو أعلم بكم إذ أنشأكم من الأرض أي خلق أباكم من التراب

THALABI:v9p150/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p150/r3.claim: Ajnna is the plural of janīn, a child while in the womb; it is called that because it is hidden there.
THALABI:v9p150/r3.anchor: وإذ أنتم أجنة جمع جنين، وهو الولد ما دام في البطن، سمي جنينا لاجتنانه

THALABI:v9p150/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150/r4.speaker: مسروق
THALABI:v9p150/r4.claim: Masrūq reports from ʿĀʾisha that Jews called a deceased friend a ṣiddīq; the Prophet called this false and said every fetus God creates is either wretched or happy, after which this verse was revealed.
THALABI:v9p150/r4.anchor: روى مسروق عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: كانت اليهود إذا هلك لهم صديق

THALABI:v9p150/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v9p150/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the prohibition as not praising yourselves.

THALABI:v9p150/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150/r6.speaker: مجاهد وزيد بن أسلم
THALABI:v9p150/r6.claim: Mujāhid and Zayd ibn Aslam explain it as not declaring yourselves free of sin.
THALABI:v9p150/r6.anchor: مجاهد وزيد بن أسلم: فلا تبرئوها،

THALABI:v9p150/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150/r7.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
THALABI:v9p150/r7.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say the verse addressed people who did vile deeds and then boasted of their prayer, fasting, and pilgrimage.
THALABI:v9p150/r7.anchor: وقال الكلبي ومقاتل: كان أناس يعملون أعمالا خبيثة

THALABI:v9p150/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p150/r8.claim: The Prophet said that when people see those who lavish praise, they should throw dust in their faces.
THALABI:v9p150/r8.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إذا رأيتم المداحين فاحثوا في وجوههم التراب

THALABI:v9p150/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p150/r9.claim: God knows best who has feared associating partners with Him and believed.
THALABI:v9p150/r9.anchor: هو أعلم بمن اتقى الشرك فآمن،

THALABI:v9p150/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150/r10.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
THALABI:v9p150/r10.claim: ʿAlī explains the God-fearing person as one who does a good deed and turns back from an evil one.
THALABI:v9p150/r10.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب كرم الله وجهه: يعني عمل حسنة وارعوى

THALABI:v9p150/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150/r11.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v9p150/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains it as making one's deeds sincere for God.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r1.claim: Muqatil defines major sins as sins ending in Hell, and indecencies as sins carrying a prescribed worldly penalty.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: كبائر الإثم، يعني: كل ذنب ختم بالنار، والفواحش يعني: كل ذنب فيه الحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r2.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi recite the phrase in the singular, kabīr al-ithm.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r3.claim: The singular faʿīl, like faʿūl, can convey abundance; the author supports this with Qur'anic examples and poetry.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r3.anchor: وفعيل قد جاء يعني به الكثرة كما أن فعولا كذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r4.claim: The singular form is suitable because the genitive verbal noun means sins generally, not one particular sin, so the singular conveys a plural sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r4.anchor: ليس يراد به إثم بعينه، إنما يراد به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r5.claim: Singular and plural forms can both express the intended abundance, as the Qur'an alternates between singular and plural for enemy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r5.anchor: فأفرد، وجمع في قوله: {ويوم يحشر أعداء الله إلى النار}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r6.claim: Those who read the plural kabāʾir do so because the meaning is plural, while ithm itself can be singular in form and abundant in sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p53/r6.anchor: وأما من جمع فقال: {كبائر الإثم} فلأنه في المعنى جمع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r1.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r1.claim: One interpretation takes al-lamam as minor sins, namely acts falling short of fornication.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r1.anchor: قال عطاء، عن ابن عباس: إلا ما كان دون الزنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r2.speaker: الكلبي عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r2.claim: An unintended glance is lamam; repeating the glance makes it a sin rather than lamam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي عنه: اللمم النظرة عن غير تعمد، فإن أعاد النظر فليس بلمم وهو ذنب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r3.speaker: نافع بن جبير بن مطعم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r3.claim: Al-lamam means what falls short of sexual intercourse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r3.anchor: وعن نافع بن جبير بن مطعم: هو ما دون الوقاع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود، وأبو هريرة، ومسروق، والشعبي، وطاووس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r4.claim: These authorities likewise define lamam as what is short of fornication.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r4.anchor: وهذا قول ابن مسعود، وأبي هريرة، ومسروق، والشعبي، وطاووس، قالوا: ما دون الزنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r5.claim: The Prophet describes a person's destined share of fornication through looking, speech, kissing, touching, walking, and desire, while the genitals either confirm or deny it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r5.anchor: واحتجوا بما روى أبو هريرة أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال: "إن الله -عز وجل- كتب على ابن آدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r6.claim: If intercourse occurs, the person has committed fornication; without it, the lesser acts remain lamam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r6.anchor: فإن تقدم فرجه كان زان وإلا فهو اللمم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r7.speaker: ابن الزبير، وعكرمة، وقتادة، والضحاك، ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r7.claim: They define lamam as sin between the limits of a worldly penalty and a punishment threatened in the afterlife; prayers expiate it for those who avoid major sins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r7.anchor: قال ابن الزبير، وعكرمة، وقتادة، والضحاك، ومقاتل: هو ما بين الحدين، حد الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r8.speaker: العوفي والحكم عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r8.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas gives the same view: lamam is a sin with neither a worldly penalty nor a promised afterlife punishment, forgiven for those who avoid major sins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r8.anchor: وهي رواية العوفي، والحكم عن ابن عباس، وهؤلاء قالوا: اللمم تكفره الصلوات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r9.claim: A second main interpretation is a person falling into a sin once, then repenting and not returning to it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {إلا اللمم} قال: يلم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r10.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r10.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that if God forgives, He forgives abundantly, since no servant is free of error.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r10.anchor: وكان النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- يقول: "إن تغفر اللهم تغفر جما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r11.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r11.claim: Al-Hasan defines lamam as a person committing an act once and then desisting.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r11.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو الرجل يلم المرة ثم ينزع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r12.speaker: السدي عن أبي صالح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r12.claim: Al-Suddi reports Abu Salih's definition: a person falls into a sin but does not repeat it; Ibn Abbas praised this answer, and the view is also attributed to Mujahid.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r12.anchor: وروى السدي عن أبي صالح، قال: سألني رجل عن اللمم، فقلت: هو الرجل يلم بالذنب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r13.claim: When told Abu Salih's definition, Ibn Abbas said that a noble angel had helped him reach it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p55/r13.anchor: فحدثت بذلك ابن عباس قال: لقد أعانك عليها ملك كريم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r1.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad explains alamma bi-kadhā as approaching something without entering into it, or taking only a little without persisting, since one has not gained control of it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r1.anchor: وقال المبرد: يقال: ألم فلان بكذا إذا قاربه ولم يخالطه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r2.claim: On the minor-sins reading, lamam is approaching a major sin through a glance, kiss, or touch; on the repentance reading, it is a single lapse into fornication or drinking followed by repentance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r2.anchor: فعلى ما ذكر اللمم ما قارب به من الكبيرة كالنظر والقبلة واللمس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r3.speaker: جرير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r3.claim: Jarir's line uses limām for an occasional visit, illustrating the sense of infrequency.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r3.anchor: قال جرير: بنفسي من تجنبه عزيز ... علي ومن زيارته لمام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses limām as visits occurring now and then, without regularity or a fixed time.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: معناه الأحيان على غير مواظبة ولا وقت معلوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r5.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r5.claim: Al-Azhari says Arabic uses ilām for nearness and approach, including the sense of almost doing something.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r5.anchor: قال الأزهري: والعرب تستعمل الإلمام في المقاربة والدنو، يقال: ألم بفعل كذا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r6.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r6.claim: Abu Zayd says the phrase lamām of a month or two means approximately that period.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r6.anchor: قال أبو زيد: كان ذلك منذ شهرين أو لمامهما، ومنذ شهر أو لممه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r7.claim: In the Prophetic saying about spring vegetation, Abu Ubayda explains aw yalimm as something that comes close to causing harm.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r7.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: معناه أو يقرب إليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r8.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r8.claim: A Prophetic saying uses yalimm for what nearly causes an animal to die from overgrazing spring growth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r8.anchor: ومنه قوله -صلى الله عليه وسلم-: "وإن مما ينبت الربيع ما يقتل حبطا أو يلم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r9.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r9.claim: Abu Zayd calls a tree that is nearly bearing fruit al-mulim.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r9.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: في أرض بني فلان من الشجر الملم كذا وكذا، وهو الذي قارب أن يحمل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r10.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r10.claim: Al-Mubarrad says a man described as dead or mulimm is near death, a palm is near bearing, and a lamma of hair nearly reaches the ear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r10.anchor: وقال المبرد: فلان ميت أو ملم، أي قد قارب الموت، ونخل ملم قد قارب الإطعام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r11.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r11.claim: The cited verse about Zayd illustrates a person close to death, while lamma describes hair that has nearly reached the ear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r11.anchor: وزيد ميت كمد الحبارى ... إذا بانت لطيفة أو ملم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r12.claim: The imperative alimmū means grant us the smallest share of your visit, as the following verse illustrates.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r12.anchor: وقوله: ألمم، معناه اجعل لنا من زيارتك أدنى حظ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r13.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r13.claim: Under both main interpretations, the exception is external rather than an exception of an item belonging to the preceding category.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r13.anchor: وأما الاستثناء في قوله: {إلا اللمم} على القولين جميعا استثناء خارج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r14.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r14.claim: Abu Ubayda says lamam was not permitted and is not itself a major sin or indecency; the phrase means unless someone happens to lapse into such an act, under the first interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r14.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: لم يؤذن لهم في اللمم وليس اللمم من الفواحش ولا من كبائر الإثم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r15.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r15.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r15.claim: Al-Mubarrad likewise denies that lamam is permitted; he reads the exception as meaning that if they lapse, they repent, comparing it with seeking God's face in 92:19–20.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p58/r15.anchor: وقال المبرد: لم يبحهم اللمم، ومعناه استثناء ليس من الأول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r1.speaker: ابن أحمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r1.claim: Ibn Ahmar's licentious verse pretends that God permitted lamam to deceive a woman; the source says he knew it was not permitted, as her righteous response shows.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r1.anchor: وقال ابن أحمر-وأراد أن يخدع من يخاطبه- فقال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r2.speaker: قوم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r2.claim: Some say lamam belongs to the same category as indecencies: a person commits the indecency once, then repents and stops, which the word itself implies.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r2.anchor: وقال قوم: اللمم على القول الثاني من جنس الفواحش والاستثناء وقع من الجنس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r3.claim: The author prefers the external-exception reading, because treating lamam as an exception from the same category would make it seem permitted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r3.anchor: والصحيح هو الأول؛ لأن هذا يؤدي إلى إباحة اللمم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r4.speaker: زيد بن ثابت، وزيد بن أسلم، وابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r4.claim: Another view says lamam means sins committed before Islam; it arose after polytheists reproached Muslims for having once acted as they had.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r4.anchor: زيد بن ثابت، وزيد بن أسلم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r5.claim: Ibn Amr defines lamam as anything short of associating partners with God; on this reading, major sins and indecencies lead to shirk.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r5.anchor: القول الثاني: هو قول عبد الله بن عمرو قال: اللمم ما دون الشرك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r6.speaker: الناس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r6.claim: The general tendency is to follow the first two interpretations, minor sins or a lapse followed by repentance.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r7.claim: Abu Ishaq prefers the repentance interpretation: a person approaches a sin without persisting, since ilām in Arabic means doing something briefly rather than remaining at it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r7.anchor: واختار أبو إسحاق الثاني منهما، قال: اللمم هو أن يكون الإنسان قد ألم بالمعصية ولم يصر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r8.claim: Abu Ishaq argues from Arabic usage that ilām means approaching something briefly without continuing in it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r8.anchor: والإلمام في اللغة يوجب أنك تأتي الشيء في الوقت ولا تقيم عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas explains God's vast forgiveness as applying to one who committed such a lapse and repented.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p60/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لمن فعل ذلك وتاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r1.claim: Ajnna is the plural of janīn, a child in the womb; the name derives from being concealed, as does the word for someone buried under earth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r1.anchor: أجنة جمع جنين، وهو الولد ما دام في البطن، سمي جنينا لأنه مستور

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r2.speaker: عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r2.claim: Amr's verse uses janīn for a person buried in a grave.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r2.anchor: قال عمرو: ولا شمطاء لم يترك شقاها ... لها من تسعة إلا جنينا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r3.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r3.claim: God knows what every soul will do, what it will make, and what its end will be.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r3.anchor: قال الحسن: علم الله من كل نفس ما هي عاملة وما هي صانعة وإلى ما هي صائرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r4.claim: Al-Farraʾ glosses God's knowledge as encompassing first and last.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء: هو أعلم أولا وآخرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r5.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r5.claim: They report that people boasted, saying they had prayed, fasted, and done good deeds, after which the verse forbade self-purification.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r5.anchor: قال الكلبي، ومقاتل: كان ناس يقولون: صلينا وصمنا وفعلنا وفعلنا، فأنزل الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r6.claim: Al-Farraʾ takes the command as forbidding people to boast that they have done particular deeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r6.anchor: قال الفراء: لا يقولن أحدكم عملت كذا وفعلت كذا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r7.speaker: آخرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r7.claim: Others interpret the command as forbidding people to declare themselves innocent or praise themselves; Zaynab bint Abi Salama's naming prompted the Prophetic correction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: معناه لا تبرؤوها ولا تمدحوها، يدل على هذا ما روى أن زينب بنت أبي سلمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r8.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r8.claim: When Zaynab bint Abi Salama was called Barrah, the Prophet said not to declare yourselves pure, since God knows your piety better, and renamed her Zaynab.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r8.anchor: قال النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-: "لا تزكوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r9.claim: The command means not to praise oneself for qualities one does not possess; taken generally, it encourages humility and worship while avoiding ostentation and self-admiration.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r9.anchor: والمعنى: لا تزكوها بما ليس فيها. ويجوز أن يكون المعنى على العموم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r10.claim: The phrase means God knows best who is righteous and obedient.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r11.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p62/r11.claim: Al-Hasan explains piety here as sincerity in one's deeds.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r1.claim: Being acceptable to God requires more than generosity: believers also avoid grave sins and ugly acts, showing moral sensitivity in their conduct.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r1.anchor: Allah katında makbul insan olma sadece iyilik severlikle tanımlanamaz; onlar ayrıca büyük günahlardan ve çirkin fiillerden kaçınan

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r2.claim: The commentary reports tafsir examples of lemam as forbidden kissing, touching, or looking.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r2.anchor: tefsirlerde, haram olan öpme, dokunma, bakma gibi örnekler verilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r3.claim: One reported sense of lemam is an evil thought that a person does not put into action.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r3.anchor: Kişinin aklından geçirdiği fakat eyleme dönüştürmediği kötülükler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r4.speaker: author
