KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r4.claim: Another reported sense is wrongdoing that a person begins but abandons after regret.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r4.anchor: Yapmaya başlamışken pişmanlık duyup vazgeçtiği kötülükler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r5.claim: A further gloss is shirk and other sins committed before becoming Muslim.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r5.anchor: Müslüman olmadan önce işlediği şirk ve diğer günahlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r6.claim: Another gloss is sins too slight to warrant punishment in this world or torment in the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r6.anchor: Dünyada cezayı âhirette de azabı hak ettirmeyecek derecedeki günahlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r7.claim: The phrase about being created from earth is explained as being created upon the earth.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r8.claim: It may refer to creating Adam, the human species, or the first human cell.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r8.anchor: atanız Âdem’i, insan cinsini, ilk insan hücreciğini yarattığı esnada

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r9.claim: It may refer to creating from earth the basic nourishment involved in human formation, including the parents' ovum and sperm.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r9.anchor: insanın oluşumundaki, yani annenin yumurtası ile babanın sperminin meydana gelmesindeki temel gıdayı topraktan yarattığı sırada

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r10.claim: Mention of the womb stage emphasizes that God knows periods of human existence that people cannot know or remember.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r10.anchor: Allah Teâlâ’nın, insanları kendilerinin dahi bilemedikleri, hatırlayamadıkları dönemleriyle bildiğine dikkat çekmenin amaçlandığını göstermektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r11.claim: The reminder of creation after urging avoidance of sin and recalling God's vast forgiveness humbles people before His knowledge and power and warns against imagining oneself sinless or self-important.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r11.anchor: insanın Allah’ın ilmi ve kudreti karşısındaki aczini iyi kavraması, kendisinin günahsız olabileceği gibi bir yanılgıya ve benlik iddiasına asla kapılmaması için yapılmış bir uyarı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r12.claim: God knows each person's piety and no one's reward is lost, so people need not seek approval for their goodness or praise themselves; a related event and Prophetic assessment are cited.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:32/r12.anchor: kimsenin ecrinin zayi olmayacağı, dolayısıyla insanların kendi iyiliklerini başka insanlara onaylatma ihtiyaçlarının bulunmadığı veya bu iyiliklerin değerini bulması için kendilerini anlatmaları, övmeleri gerekmediği

BURHAN:v1p355/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p355/r1.speaker: أبو عبيد
BURHAN:v1p355/r1.claim: Abu ʿUbayd permits pausing before the exception in ‘except error,’ ‘except minor sins,’ and ‘except greeting,’ taking each as disconnected: but error occurs, minor sins happen, and they exchange greetings.
BURHAN:v1p355/r1.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد يجوز الوقف دون ﴿ إلا خطأ ﴾ ﴿ إلا اللمم ﴾ ﴿ إلا سلاما ﴾ لأن المعنى لكن يقع خطأ

BURHAN:v1p355/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p355/r2.speaker: غيره
BURHAN:v1p355/r2.claim: Another view forbids stopping between a substituted term and its accusative antecedent, though stopping is allowed if it is nominative; in general, a phrase strongly attached to what precedes cannot be separated by a pause.
BURHAN:v1p355/r2.anchor: وقال غيره لا يجوز الوقف على المبدل دون البدل إذا كان منصوبا وإن كان مرفوعا جاز الوقف عليه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r1.claim: Fawāḥish is the plural of fāḥisha, something considered ugly in the soul; the related forms faḥīsha and faḥshāʾ are also used.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r1.anchor: الفواحش : جمع فاحشة . وهي ما قبحت في النفس . ويقال : فاحشة وفحشاء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r2.claim: The verb afḥasha means to speak obscenely, and the related adjectives are faḥḥāsh and fāḥish.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r3.speaker: الحديث
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r3.claim: A hadith says God detests the obscene and foul-mouthed person.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث : ' إن الله يبغض الفاحش البذيء '

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r4.claim: Anything that exceeds its proper measure is described as fāḥish.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r4.anchor: وكل شيء جاوز قدره فهو : فاحش

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r5.claim: One Qur'anic sense is sin or disobedience, including the target verse's exception for minor lapses.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الفواحش في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r6.claim: A second sense is adultery or fornication.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r6.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الفواحش في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r7.claim: A third sense is male same-sex intercourse, as in the account of Lot's people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r7.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الفواحش في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r8.claim: A fourth sense is a wife's nushūz or marital misconduct, in the contexts of financial harm and divorce.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p466/r8.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الفواحش في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

BURSEVI:v9p200/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p200/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p200/r1.claim: God knows His sanctified reality in a way no human can; knowledge of God belongs to God, except when a person is annihilated from limited knowledge and subsists by absolute knowledge.
BURSEVI:v9p200/r1.anchor: والله تعالى عالم بصورته المنزهة عن الشكل المقدسة عن الهيئة والإنسان غير عالم بها على كيفية علم الله

BURSEVI:v9p200/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p200/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p200/r2.claim: The truly God-fearing person makes God his protection from everything else and attributes every act of knowledge and work to God as the source of all existence and good.
BURSEVI:v9p200/r2.anchor: أي بمن اتقى بالله عما سواء بحيث جعل الله تعالى وقاية نفسه لينسب كل ما يصدر عنه من العلم والعمل إليه

TABATABAI:53:30-32/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r11.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r11.claim: Al-Raghib explains the root sense of sin as an act that delays a person from reward and good.
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r11.anchor: كما ذكره الراغب - الفعل المبطئ عن الثواب والخير

TABATABAI:53:30-32/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r12.speaker: الرواية
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r12.claim: A report defines major sins as those for which God has threatened the Fire.
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r12.anchor: كبائر الإثم المعاصي الكبيرة وهو على ما في الرواية ما أوعد الله عليه النار

TABRISI:53:31-41/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-41/r1.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:53:31-41/r1.claim: Al-Farraʾ defines lَمَم as a deed done once in a while without becoming a habit; Umayya's line uses ألما for such a lapse.
TABRISI:53:31-41/r1.anchor: قال الفراء اللمم أن يفعل الإنسان الشيء في الحين

TABRISI:53:31-41/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-41/r2.speaker: أمية
TABRISI:53:31-41/r2.claim: Umayya's line uses ألما as evidence for the occasional, nonhabitual sense of lَمَم.
TABRISI:53:31-41/r2.anchor: قال أمية: إن تغفر اللهم تغفر جما وأي عبد لك لا ألما

TABRISI:53:31-41/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-41/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:53:31-41/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet recited the two lines and explained them as meaning that he had not committed a sin.
TABRISI:53:31-41/r3.anchor: وقد روي أن إلنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان ينشدهما

TABRISI:53:31-41/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-41/r4.speaker: الأعشى
TABRISI:53:31-41/r4.claim: Al-Aʿshā's cited line uses ألم in the sense of briefly encountering or partaking of something.
TABRISI:53:31-41/r4.anchor: وقال أعشى باهله: تكفيه حزة فلذ إن ألم بها

TABRISI:53:31-41/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-41/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:31-41/r5.claim: Ajnna is the plural of janīn, an embryo; Ruʾba's line pictures embryos hidden in throats.
TABRISI:53:31-41/r5.anchor: أجنة جمع جنين قال رؤبة: أجنة في مستكنات الحلق

TABRISI:53:31-41/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-41/r6.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
TABRISI:53:31-41/r6.claim: The poet uses janīn for a person hidden in a grave, attesting its sense of something concealed.
TABRISI:53:31-41/r6.anchor: وقال عمرو بن كلثوم: ولا شمطاء لم يترك شقاها لها من تسعة إلا جنينا

TABRISI:53:31-41/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-41/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:31-41/r8.claim: Al-lamam is accusative as an exception from sins and indecencies; it is lesser than these yet still belongs to their category.
TABRISI:53:31-41/r8.anchor: إلا اللمم منصوب على الاستثناء من الإثم والفواحش

TABRISI:53:31-41/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-41/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:31-41/r9.claim: The time clause may be governed by aʿlamu bikum, attached to ajinna as its description, or understood with an omitted clause describing the embryos.
TABRISI:53:31-41/r9.anchor: إذ أنشأكم العامل في إذ قوله أعلم بكم

TABRISI:53:32-39/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:32-39/r1.claim: God knew people before creating them; their creation from earth first refers to their father Adam, made from the earth's surface.
TABRISI:53:32-39/r1.anchor: أي أنشأ أباكم آدم من أديم الأرض

TABRISI:53:32-39/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r2.speaker: البلخي
TABRISI:53:32-39/r2.claim: Al-Balkhī takes the earth reference to all people: God creates them from foods derived from earth, using His customary creation through their combined substances.
TABRISI:53:32-39/r2.anchor: قال البلخي يجوز أن يكون المراد به جميع الخلق

TABRISI:53:32-39/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r3.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:53:32-39/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says God knew, while they were embryos, what each person would do and what their eventual end would be.
TABRISI:53:32-39/r3.anchor: أي علم من كل نفس ما هي صانعة وإلى ما هي صائرة عن الحسن

TABRISI:53:32-39/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:32-39/r4.claim: The passage may also mean that God knew people's weakness and inclination toward minor lapses in the womb, so He certainly knows their deeds after they exist.
TABRISI:53:32-39/r4.anchor: علم ضعفكم وميل طباعكم إلى اللمم

TABRISI:53:32-39/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:32-39/r5.claim: Do not exalt yourselves or praise yourselves for qualities you do not possess, since God knows you better.
TABRISI:53:32-39/r5.anchor: أي لا تعظموها ولا تمدحوها بما ليس لها

TABRISI:53:32-39/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:32-39/r6.claim: An alternative is not to claim purity for one's good deeds, which would hinder devotion and humility and encourage ostentation.
TABRISI:53:32-39/r6.anchor: لا تزكوها بما فيها من الخير ليكون أقرب إلى النسك والخشوع

TABRISI:53:32-39/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:32-39/r7.claim: One explanation of the pious is those who avoid polytheism and major sins.

TABRISI:53:32-39/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:32-39/r8.claim: Another explanation is those who act righteously, obey, and sincerely devote their deeds.
TABRISI:53:32-39/r8.anchor: هو اعلم بمن بر وأطاع وأخلص العمل

THALABI:v9p148/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p148/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة ومجاهد والحسن وأبو صالح وابن عباس
THALABI:v9p148/r6.claim: One view treats the exception as connected and lamam as a major sin or indecency that a person commits, then repents and stops; this is reported from Abu Hurayra, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Abu Salih, and Ibn Abbas through Ata.
THALABI:v9p148/r6.anchor: فقال قوم: هو استثناء صحيح، واللمم من الكبائر والفواحش، ومعنى الآية: إلا ان يلم بالفاحشة ثم يتوب

THALABI:v9p148/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p148/r7.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v9p148/r7.claim: The Prophet’s quoted supplication asks God to forgive all people and observes that every servant has sinned at least a little.
THALABI:v9p148/r7.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن تغفر اللهم تغفر جما … وأي عبد لك لا ألما

THALABI:v9p148/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p148/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
THALABI:v9p148/r8.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says lamam means what is below associating partners with God.
THALABI:v9p148/r8.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص: اللمم: ما دون الشرك

THALABI:v9p148/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p148/r9.speaker: زيد بن ثابت وزيد بن أسلم وابنه وابن عباس
THALABI:v9p148/r9.claim: A disconnected-exception reading takes lamam as past pre-Islamic sins, for which people are not accountable; this view is attributed to Zayd ibn Thabit, Zayd ibn Aslam and his son, and Ibn Abbas, and arose after polytheists reproached Muslims for their former deeds.
THALABI:v9p148/r9.anchor: فقال بعضهم: هو ما سلف في الجاهلية فلا يؤاخذهم به، وذلك أن المشركين قالوا للمسلمين

THALABI:v9p148/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p148/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود ومسروق والشعبي وأبو سعيد الخدري وحذيفة وابن عباس
THALABI:v9p148/r10.claim: Another disconnected-exception view calls lamam minor sins such as a glance, wink, or kiss, because a person touches the act without persisting in it.
THALABI:v9p148/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هو صغار الذنوب مثل النظرة والغمزة والقبلة

THALABI:v9p148/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p148/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
THALABI:v9p148/r11.claim: The Prophet says each person has an unavoidable share of fornication: eyes gaze, tongue speaks, lips kiss, hands touch, feet walk, and the soul desires; intercourse makes it full fornication, otherwise it is lamam.
THALABI:v9p148/r11.anchor: قال أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «إن الله عز وجل كتب على ابن آدم حظه من الزنا أدركه ذلك لا محالة

THALABI:v9p149/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p149/r1.speaker: ابن الزبير وعكرمة وقتادة والضحاك وابن عباس
THALABI:v9p149/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr, Ikrima, Qatada, and al-Dahhak, with reports from Ibn Abbas, define lamam as sins between the worldly legal penalty and punishment in the Hereafter.
THALABI:v9p149/r1.anchor: وقال ابن الزبير وعكرمة وقتادة والضحاك: هو ما بين الحدين: حد الدنيا وعذاب الآخرة

THALABI:v9p149/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p149/r2.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v9p149/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi gives two senses: a sin with neither a worldly penalty nor afterlife punishment, forgiven by prayers if not major; or a grave sin a Muslim repeats and then repents.
THALABI:v9p149/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: اللمم على وجهين، كل ذنب لم يذكر عليه حدا في الدنيا ولا عذابا في الآخرة

THALABI:v9p149/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p149/r3.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v9p149/r3.claim: Muqatil says lamam means sins between the two limits and says the verse was revealed about Nabhan al-Tammar, whose story was told in Al Imran.
THALABI:v9p149/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: اللمم ما بين الحدين من الذنوب. نزلت في نبهان التمار وقد مضت القصة في سورة آل عمران

THALABI:v9p149/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p149/r4.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رياح
THALABI:v9p149/r4.claim: Ata ibn Abi Rabah says lamam is what the soul does from time to time.
THALABI:v9p149/r4.anchor: وقال عطاء بن أبي رياح: اللمم

THALABI:v9p149/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p149/r5.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
THALABI:v9p149/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib explains lamam as what falls upon or crosses the heart.
THALABI:v9p149/r5.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب: هو ما لم على القلب، اي حظر

THALABI:v9p149/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p149/r6.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
THALABI:v9p149/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya says anything a person intends, good or evil, is lamam.
THALABI:v9p149/r6.anchor: وقال محمد بن الحنفية: كل ما هممت به من خير أو شر فهو لمم

THALABI:v9p149/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p149/r7.speaker: الخبر المروي
THALABI:v9p149/r7.claim: A report says Satan has a prompting of whispering and the angel has a prompting of inspiration.
THALABI:v9p149/r7.anchor: الخبر المروي «إن للشيطان لمة، وللملك لمة، فلمة الشيطان الوسوسة، ولمة الملك الإلهام»

THALABI:v9p149/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p149/r8.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
THALABI:v9p149/r8.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl calls an unintentional glance lamam and forgiven; repeating the glance is a sin, no longer lamam.
THALABI:v9p149/r8.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل: اللمم: النظرة من غير تعمد، وهو مغفور، فإن أعاد النظر فليس بلمم

THALABI:v9p149/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p149/r9.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v9p149/r9.claim: Al-Farra says lamam means small, nearby sins; its root describes an act done now and then without delving into it or persisting, and alamma bihi means visiting and departing.
THALABI:v9p149/r9.anchor: وقال الفراء: اللمم: المتقارب من صغار الذنوب، وأصل اللمم والإلمام هو ما يعمله الإنسان المرة بعد المرة

THALABI:v9p149/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p149/r10.speaker: الأعشى
THALABI:v9p149/r10.claim: Al-Aʿsha’s poem uses alamma for a passing visit by a phantom, illustrating the root’s sense of coming briefly and leaving.
THALABI:v9p149/r10.anchor: قال الأعشى: ألم خيال من قتيلة بعد ما … وهي حبلها من حبلنا فتصرما

THALABI:v9p149/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p149/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p149/r11.claim: God’s forgiveness is ample and no sin is too great for Him; the author links this to 7:156, ‘My mercy encompasses everything.’
THALABI:v9p149/r11.anchor: إن ربك واسع المغفرة لا يتعاظمه ذنب، نظيره ورحمتي وسعت كل شيء

THALABI:v9p149/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p149/r12.speaker: أبو مسيرة عمرو بن شرحبيل
THALABI:v9p149/r12.claim: In a dream, Abu Maysara sees pavilions in Paradise for Dhu al-Kila and Hawshab, asks where Ammar and his companions are, and is told they met God and found Him vast in forgiveness despite fighting one another.
THALABI:v9p149/r12.anchor: قال: رأيت كأني دخلت الجنة فإذا قباب مضروبة فقلت: لمن هذه؟ فقالوا: لذي الكلاع وحوشب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r1.claim: Al-lamam means minor sins, such as a glance or a kiss.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r2.claim: God's creating people from earth refers to creating their forefather from dust; ajinnah is the plural of janin, an embryo.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r2.anchor: يعني: خلق أباكم من التراب { وإذ أنتم أجنة } جمع جنين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r3.claim: Do not praise yourselves; God knows best who is mindful and does good.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r3.anchor: لا تمدحوها { هو أعلم بمن اتقى } عمل حسنة

ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r21.claim: Major sins are sins carrying a grave punishment or specifically threatened in revelation.
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r21.anchor: ikābı büyük olan, yahut hakkında bihusûsihi va‘îd bulunan günahlar kebâirdir.

ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r22.claim: Fawahish are especially the manifestly shameful acts among major sins.
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r22.anchor: kebâir meyânında bilhassa çirkinliği açık olan fuhşiyyâttan

ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r23.claim: Lemam means small faults; when major sins are avoided, lesser lapses such as a glance, insinuating look, or kiss are forgiven.
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r23.anchor: Çünkü kebâirden ictinab edilince meselâ bir nazar, bir gamze, bir bûse gibi sağāir ma‘füv olur.

ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r24.claim: God forgives minor sins when major sins are avoided, may forgive major sins upon repentance or even without it, but does not forgive shirk without repentance.
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r24.anchor: kebâirden ictinab edilince sağāiri mağfiret buyurduğu gibi tevbe edilince kebâiri de mağfiret buyurur

ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r25.claim: God knows people completely, from the first human or human cell created from earth, or the earthly origin of their food, through their embryonic state and future conditions.
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r25.anchor: Arz’da ilk insan cinsinin, insan huceyresinin yaratılışı zımnında veya insan gıdasının topraktan yaratıldığı sırada

ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r26.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r26.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r26.claim: People must not praise themselves as entirely pure and faultless, since they may have many faults of which they are unaware.
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r26.anchor: hiç günahsız, kusursuz, tertemiz addederek övmeyin,

ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r27.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r27.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r27.claim: God alone fully knows who is truly pious; the people of good and evil will be distinguished before Him in the afterlife.
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r27.anchor: Ehl-i ihsan ile ehl-i isâe âhirette huzûr-ı Hak’ta seçileceklerdir.

BURHAN:v4p170/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p170/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p170/r3.claim: Sometimes afعل no longer expresses comparison: أعلم means knowing, since none shares God's knowledge, and أهون means easy, since all possibilities relate equally to God's power.
BURHAN:v4p170/r3.anchor: إذ لا مشارك لله تعالى في علمه بذلك وأهون عليه بمعنى هين

ITQAN:v1p57/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p57/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p57/r6.claim: The passage on avoiding major sins resembles Medinan revelation despite appearing in a Meccan sura: major sins end in fire, fawahish incur a legal penalty, and lamam falls between them, while Mecca had no such penalties.
ITQAN:v1p57/r6.anchor: مثال ما يشبه تنزيل المدني في السور المكية قوله في النجم

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r1.speaker: ثابت بن الحارث الأنصاري
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r1.claim: Thabit ibn al-Harith reports that Jews called a child who died young a “sidq”; the Prophet rejected this and said God knows whether each person formed in the womb will be wretched or fortunate.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r1.anchor: عن ثابت بن الحرث الأنصاري قال كانت اليهود تقول إذا هلك لهم صبي صغير هو صديق

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r1.speaker: ثابت بن الحارث الأنصاري
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r1.claim: Thabit ibn al-Harith says Jews called their deceased young children righteous; the Prophet answered that every soul is created either felicitous or wretched, and this verse followed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r1.anchor: عن ثابت بن الحارث الأنصاري قال: كانت اليهود تقول إذا هلك لهم صبي صغير: هو صديق

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r9.claim: Ibn Qutayba cites shifts in addressee, including a question to Moses and Aaron that names Moses alone, and a reference to humanity’s father Adam.

MAJAZ:v2p238/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p238/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p238/r1.claim: Ajinna is the plural of janīn, formed like sarīr and asirra.
MAJAZ:v2p238/r1.anchor: وهو جمع جنين، تقديره: سرير وأسرة..

NAHHAS:v4p274/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p274/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p274/r5.claim: Al-fawāhish is coordinated with the major sins.
NAHHAS:v4p274/r5.anchor: والفواحش ) عطف على الكبائر ( إلا اللمم

NAHHAS:v4p274/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p274/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p274/r6.claim: Al-lamam is accusative as an exception that is not from the same class as what precedes.
NAHHAS:v4p274/r6.anchor: إلا اللمم ) قد ذكرنا ما فيه من قول أهل التفسير وهو منصوب على أنه استثناء ليس من الأول

NAHHAS:v4p274/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p274/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p274/r7.claim: The most sound and inclusive view takes al-lamam as minor sins, related to lightly touching or taking little of something; God is greatly forgiving of them.
NAHHAS:v4p274/r7.anchor: ومن أصح ما قيل فيه وأجمعه لأقوال العلماء أنه الصغائر ويكون مأخوذا من لممت بالشيء إذا قللت نيله

NAHHAS:v4p274/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p274/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p274/r8.claim: God knows people's deeds and their eventual outcome from the beginning, when their father was created from earth and when they were embryos, better than they know themselves as adults.
NAHHAS:v4p274/r8.anchor: أي هو أعلم بما تعملون وما أنتم صائرون إليه حين ابتدأ خلق أبيكم من تراب وحين أنتم أجنة

NAHHAS:v4p274/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p274/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p274/r9.claim: Aʿlam may also simply mean ʿālim, knowing.
NAHHAS:v4p274/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون أعلم بمعنى عالم

NAHHAS:v4p274/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p274/r10.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
NAHHAS:v4p274/r10.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam explains this as not declaring yourselves free of sins or claiming to be virtuous.
NAHHAS:v4p274/r10.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم أي لا تبرئوها من المعاصي قال وشرح هذا لا تقولوا إنا أزكياء

NAHHAS:v4p274/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p274/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p274/r11.claim: God knows best who avoids sins, fears Him, and performs the obligations.
NAHHAS:v4p274/r11.anchor: هو أعلم بمن اتقى ) المعاصي وخاف وأدى الفرائض

ZAJJAJ:v5p74/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p74/r3.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v5p74/r3.claim: One view takes lamam as minor lapses such as a kiss, a glance, or similar acts.
ZAJJAJ:v5p74/r3.anchor: قيل إن اللمم نحو القبلة والنظرة وما أشبه ذلك

ZAJJAJ:v5p74/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p74/r4.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v5p74/r4.claim: Another view takes lamam as committing an indecency and then repenting.
ZAJJAJ:v5p74/r4.anchor: وقيل إلا اللمم إلا أن يكون العبد قد ألم بفاحشة ثم تاب

ZAJJAJ:v5p74#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p74#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p74#2/r1.claim: Broad forgiveness indicates lamam is a sin briefly touched and not persisted in; the Arabic word itself implies doing something temporarily and not continuing in it.
ZAJJAJ:v5p74#2/r1.anchor: إنما الإلمام في اللغة يوجب أنك تأتي الشيء الوقت ولا تقيم عليه، فهذا - والله أعلم - معنى اللمم في هذا الموضع

NASHR:v2p367/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p367/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
NASHR:v2p367/r5.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Khalaf read كبير الإثم as singular in both al-Shura and al-Najm; the others read كبائر الإثم as plural.
NASHR:v2p367/r5.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف، (كبير) بكسر الباء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p5#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p5#2/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p5#2/r15.claim: Lammam means something small or slight; related expressions describe brief contact or limited staying and eating.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p5#2/r15.anchor: اللمم: ما قل وصغر، ومنه اللمم: المس من الجنون، وألم بالمكان: قل لبثه فيه، وألم بالطعام: قل أكله منه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p5#2/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p5#2/r16.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p5#2/r16.claim: Al-Mubarrad says the root idea is to touch or approach something without fully undertaking it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p5#2/r16.anchor: وقال المبرد: أصل اللمم أن يلم بالشيء من غير أن يركبه، يقال:

DURR-FULL:v7p658/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r1.speaker: زينب بنت أبي سلمة
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r1.claim: When Zaynab bint Abi Salama was named Barrah, the Prophet invoked this verse and said God knows who is pious better than people do, then renamed her Zaynab.
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r1.anchor: عن زينب بنت أبي سلمة أنها سميت برة فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: {فلا تزكوا أنفسكم} الله أعلم بأهل البر منكم

DURR-FULL:v7p658/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r2.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r2.claim: Abu Bakr admired Qays ibn ʿAsim for declining to describe himself, citing God's prohibition on self-praise.
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r2.anchor: عن جده عبد الله بن مصعب قال: قال أبو بكر الصديق لقيس بن عاصم: صف لنا نفسك فقال: إن الله يقول {فلا تزكوا أنفسكم}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r1.claim: God's knowing people as embryos reflects forgiveness and gentleness toward this community, consistent with 2:185's teaching that God wills ease.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r1.anchor: وقوله : { وإذ أنتم أجنة في بطون أمهاتكم } يختص بسعة المغفرة والرفق بهذه الأمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r2.claim: Ajinna is the plural of janīn, offspring in the womb; the passive-pattern janīn means ‘concealed’ in three layers of darkness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r2.anchor: والأجنة : جمع جنين ، وهو نسل الحيوان ما دام في الرحم ، وهو فعيل بمعنى مفعول لأنه مستور في ظلمات ثلاث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r3.claim: The womb phrase is explanatory because a fetus is necessarily there; it recalls development from conception to birth and God's knowledge of it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r3.anchor: وفي { بطون أمهاتكم } صفة كاشفة إذ الجنين لا يقال إلا على ما في بطن أمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r4.claim: This parenthetical warning falls between God's knowledge and the account in 53:33; its fāʾ warns believers against pride in good deeds or others' praise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r4.anchor: وجملة { فلا تزكوا أنفسكم } اعتراض بين جملة { هو أعلم بكم } وجملة { أفرأيت الذي تولى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r5.claim: Tuzakkū is the doubled form of zakkā that ascribes a quality; here it means do not ascribe purity to yourselves.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r5.anchor: و { تزكوا } مضارع زكى الذي هو من التضعيف المراد منه نسبة المفعول إلى أصل الفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r6.claim: ‘Your selves’ includes private or public self-praise; the plural correspondence distributes each person's own self to them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r6.anchor: فقوله : { أنفسكم } صادق بتزكية المرء نفسه في سره أو علانيته فرجع الجمع في قوله : { فلا تزكوا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r7.claim: Do not regard yourselves as pure; seek closeness to God and avoid pride, including boasting or displaying good works except for a public benefit, as Joseph did.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r7.anchor: والمعنى : لا تحسبوا أنفسكم أزكياء وابتغوا زيادة التقرب إلى الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r8.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r8.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil report that some people did good deeds then boasted of their prayers, fasts, pilgrimage, and jihād; the verse was revealed about them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r8.anchor: وعن الكلبي ومقاتل : كان ناس يعملون أعمالا حسنة ثم يقولون : صلاتنا وصيامنا وحجنا وجهادنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r9.claim: The command also forbids praising fellow believers: anfusikum can mean one's community, as in 24:61's ‘greet yourselves’; praise may corrupt them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p124#2/r9.anchor: ويشمل تزكية المرء غيره فيرجع { أنفسكم } إلى معنى قومكم أو جماعتكم مثل قوله تعالى : { فإذا دخلتم بيوتا فسلموا على أنفسكم }

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r1.claim: الذين is an adjective attached to الذين in the preceding verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r1.anchor: قوله: الذين نعت ل الذين [النجم: 31] المتقدم قبله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r2.claim: يَجْتَنِبُونَ means to leave something aside or keep away from it.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r3.speaker: جمهور القراء والناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r3.claim: The majority read كبائر الإثم in the plural.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r4.speaker: ابن وثاب وطلحة والأعمش وعيسى وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r4.claim: They read كبير الإثم in the singular, intending a collective plural.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب وطلحة والأعمش وعيسى وحمزة والكسائي: «كبير الإثم» على الإفراد الذي يراد به الجمع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r5.claim: The singular can stand for a plural, as in the cited phrases about no intimate friend and the best companion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r5.anchor: فما لنا من شافعين ولا صديق حميم [الشعراء: 100]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r6.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r6.claim: The majority identify major sins as the seven destructive sins mentioned in hadith reports.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r6.anchor: فذهب الجمهور إلى أنها السبع الموبقات التي وردت في الأحاديث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r7.claim: Major sins are sins carrying a worldly penalty, an explicit threat of Hell, a curse, or the like; they are numerous.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r7.anchor: وتحرير القول في الكبائر أنها كل معصية يوجد فيها حد في الدنيا، أو توعد بنار في الآخرة، أو لعنة ونحو هذا خاصا بها فهي كثيرة العدد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r8.claim: Asked whether they numbered seven, Ibn ʿAbbās replied they were nearer seventy than seven.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس حين قيل له أسبع هي؟ فقال: هي إلى السبعين أقرب منها إلى السبع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r9.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r9.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says كبير الإثم means unbelief.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r9.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: «كبير الإثم» هنا يراد به: الكفر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r10.claim: The indecencies are the sins just mentioned.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r11.claim: The exception may be construed as connected, or validly as disconnected.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r11.anchor: هو استثناء يصح أن يكون متصلا، وإن قدرته منقطعا ساغ ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r12.claim: They explain lamm as shirk and sins committed before Islam.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r12.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وابن زيد معناه: ما ألموا به من الشرك والمعاصي في الجاهلية قبل الإسلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r13.speaker: الثعلبي عن ابن عباس وزيد بن ثابت وزيد بن أسلم وابنه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r13.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī reports that unbelievers taunted Muslims for acting similarly before Islam, prompting the verse; Ibn ʿAṭiyya links it to 4:23.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r13.anchor: قال الثعلبي عن ابن عباس وزيد بن ثابت وزيد بن أسلم وابنه: إن سبب الآية أن الكفار قالوا للمسلمين: قد كنتم بالأمس تعملون أعمالنا، فنزلت الآية وهي مثل قوله تعالى: وأن تجمعوا بين الأختين إلا ما قد سلف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r14.claim: Others take lamm as an occasional lapse, not persisted in, followed by repentance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r14.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره: ما ألموا من المعاصي الفلتة والسقطة دون دوام ثم يتوبون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r15.speaker: الحسن عند الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r15.claim: Al-Ḥasan defines lamm as an episode of fornication, theft, or wine drinking that is not repeated.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p203#2/r15.anchor: ذكر الطبري عن الحسن أنه قال في اللمة: من الزنا والسرقة والخمر ثم لا يعود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r1.claim: The lapse interpretation allows hope of the promised good, since believers commonly commit sins.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r1.anchor: وهذا كالذي قبله، فكأن هذا التأويل يقتضي الرفق بالناس في إدخالهم في الوعد بالحسنى، إذ الغالب في المؤمنين مواقعة المعاصي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r2.claim: A rajaz verse used by the Prophet says God may forgive a whole group, since no servant is wholly free of lapses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r2.anchor: وقد تمثل به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: [الرجز] إن تغفر اللهم تغفر جما ... وأي عبد لك لا ألما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة وابن عباس والشعبي وغيرهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r3.claim: They define lamm as lesser sins without a penalty or specified threat; lesser relative to worse sins, but serious relative to the prohibition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r3.anchor: اللمم صغار الذنوب التي بين الحدين الدنيا والآخرة وهي ما لا حد فيه ولا وعيد مختصا بها مذكورا لها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r4.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r4.claim: A Prophetic report gives the eye’s look and tongue’s speech as shares of fornication, which the genitals confirm or deny; without intercourse it is lamm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r4.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن الله كتب على ابن آدم حظه من الزنا لا محالة، فزنى العين: النظر، وزنى اللسان: المنطق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r5.claim: The verse is also reported to have been revealed about Nabhan al-Tammar; people cannot avoid minor sins but retain the promise if they avoid major sins.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r5.anchor: وروي أن هذه الآية نزلت في نبهان التمار فالناس لا يتخلصون من مواقعة هذه الصغائر ولهم مع ذلك الحسنى إذا اجتنبوا التي هي في نفسها كبائر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r6.claim: Many scholars strongly favor the minor-sins interpretation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r6.anchor: وتظاهر العلماء في هذا القول، وكثر المائل إليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports that Ibn ʿAmr defined lamm as below shirk, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the attribution is unsound.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r7.anchor:
وذكر الطبري عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاصي أنه قال:
اللمم ما دون الشرك، وهذا عندي لا يصح عن عبد الله بن عمرو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r8.speaker: ابن عباس والشعبي عند المهدوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r8.claim: Al-Mahdawī reports from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Shaʿbī that lamm is anything short of fornication.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r8.anchor: وذكر المهدوي عن ابن عباس والشعبي: اللمم ما دون الزنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r9.speaker: نفطويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r9.claim: Nuftawayh defines lamm as a sin that is not habitual.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r9.anchor: وقال نفطويه: اللمم ما ليس بمعتاد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r10.speaker: الرماني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r10.claim: Al-Rummānī defines it as intending or thinking of a sin without committing it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r10.anchor: وقال الرماني: اللمم الهم بالذنب وحديث النفس به دون أن يواقع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r11.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب عند الثعلبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r11.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī reports Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib’s definition as a passing thought in the heart, the devil’s touch.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r11.anchor: حكى الثعلبي عن سعيد بن المسيب: أنه ما خطر على القلب، وذلك هو لمة الشيطان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r12.speaker: الزهراوي والحسين بن الفضل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r12.claim: They say lamm means an accidental glance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r12.anchor: قال الزهراوي وقيل: اللمم نظرة الفجأة، وقاله الحسين بن الفضل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r13.claim: God consoles people after these accounts by affirming His vast forgiveness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r13.anchor: ثم أنس تعالى بعد هذا بقوله: إن ربك واسع المغفرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r14.speaker: عائشة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r14.claim: ʿĀʾisha says it concerned Jews who vaunted the righteousness of children who died young; its meaning extends to everyone.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r14.anchor: روي عن عائشة أنها نزلت بسبب قوم من اليهود كانوا يعظمون أنفسهم ويقولون للطفل إذا مات لهم هذا صديق عند الله، ونحو هذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r15.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل عند الثعلبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r15.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī reports that al-Kalbī and Muqātil place the revelation among believers boasting of their deeds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r15.anchor: وحكى الثعلبي عن الكلبي ومقاتل أنها نزلت في قوم من المؤمنين فخروا بأعمالهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r16.speaker: مكي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r16.claim: Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib takes أعلم بكم to mean simply that God knows you.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p204/r16.anchor: قال مكي بن أبي طالب في المشكل معناه: هو عالم بكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r1.speaker: جمهور أهل المعاني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r1.claim: Most specialists take the comparative literally and absolutely: God knows more than all others.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r1.anchor: جمهور أهل المعاني: بل هو التفضيل بالإطلاق، أي هو أعلم من الموجودين جملة، والعامل في إذ أعلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r2.speaker: بعض النحاة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r2.claim: Some grammarians make an implicit verb, تقديره اذكروا, govern إذ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r2.anchor: وقال بعض النحاة العامل فيه فعل مضمر تقديره: اذكروا إذ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r3.claim: Direct attachment to أعلم is clearer: if God knew people as embryos, He knows them all the more as responsible adults.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r3.anchor:
والمعنى الأول أبين، لأن تقديره:
فإذا كان علمه قد أحاط بكم وأنتم في هذه الأحوال فأحرى أن يقع بكم وأنتم تعقلون وتجترحون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r4.claim: Creation from earth may mean the creation of Adam or the formation of nourishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r4.anchor: والإنشاء من الأرض: يراد به خلق آدم عليه السلام، ويحتمل أن يراد به إنشاء الغذاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r5.claim: أجنة is the plural of جنين.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r6.claim: The apparent sense forbids self-praise; alternatively it forbids praising others for reputation, worldly flattery, or definitive claims of righteousness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r6.anchor: وقوله: فلا تزكوا أنفسكم ظاهره النهي عن أن يزكي نفسه، ويحتمل أن يكون نهيا عن أن يزكي بعض الناس بعضا وإذا كان هذا فإنما ينهى عن تزكية السمعة والمدح للدنيا والقطع بالتزكية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r7.claim: The author cites the report concerning ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn at his death in connection with praise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r7.anchor: ومن ذلك الحديث في عثمان بن مظعون عند موته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r8.claim: An imam may commend a model to follow, as the Prophet commended Abū Bakr and others; witness assessment is also permitted when needed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r8.anchor: وأما تزكية الإمام والقدرة أحدا ليؤتم به أوليتهم الناس بالخير فجائز، وقد زكى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعض أصحابه أبا بكر وغيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r9.claim: Assessing witnesses is permitted because legal proceedings require it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r9.anchor: وكذلك تزكية الشهود في الحقوق جائزة للضرورة إليها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r10.claim: Piety is the true basis of commendation, and God knows people’s piety best.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r10.anchor: وأصل التزكية إنما هو التقوى، والله تعالى هو أعلم بتقوى الناس منكم

JISHUMI:v9p6660/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r1.claim: The passage implies minor sins, contrary to Khārijites who regard every sin as major.
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r1.anchor: خلاف ما يقوله بعض الخوارج أن كل ذنب كبيرة

JISHUMI:v9p6660/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r2.claim: Forgiveness is deserved by avoiding major sins, supporting the author's doctrine of divine threat.
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r2.anchor: وتدل أن المغفرة تستحق باجتناب الكبائر، فيصح قولنا في الوعيد

JISHUMI:v9p6660/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r3.speaker: أبو علي وأبو هاشم
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r3.claim: Though Abū ʿAlī and Abū Hāshim differed on self-purification, they agreed no one may certify himself for Paradise, since he cannot know whether he fulfilled his duty or know hidden states and outcomes.
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r3.anchor: وشيخانا أبو علي وأبو هاشم وإن اختلفا في تزكية النفس كيف هي اتفقا أنه لا يجوز أن يشهد لنفسه بالجنة
